title: Move dev/smoke-test harness from main.rs into src/dev.rs
description:
## Goal
Move `MockLlmClient`, `MockPermissionRequester`, `DevSmokeResult`, `run_smoke_flow`, `build_dev_agent`, `print_dev_smoke_result`, `exercise_permission_gate_smoke`, and the `Backend` enum from `src/main.rs` into a new `src/dev.rs` module.

## Scope
- **In scope:** Extract those types and functions. Add `mod dev;` to `main.rs`. Update `main.rs` to import from `crate::dev`. Remove extracted code from `main.rs`.
- **Out of scope:** Moving tests (task 3), changing any behavior, touching non-dev code.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. `src/dev.rs` exists containing the dev harness types and functions.
2. `src/main.rs` imports dev harness items from `crate::dev`.
3. `cargo test -q` passes with same test count as baseline.
4. `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings` passes.

- `Backend` enum is used by CLI parsing; keep it accessible from `main.rs`.

title: Adapter-owned logging: per-session logs for serve, new proxy subcommand, shared sink
description:
## Problem Statement

Debug logging for the adapter lives entirely in `acp-debug.sh`, a bash wrapper the
user is expected to configure by hand. This has four consequences:

1. **Normal users get nothing.** Someone running the adapter from an ACP client
   (LouiseLM, Zed) has no log to attach to a bug report unless they are talked
   through installing a shell wrapper.
2. **Half the conversation is missing.** The wrapper tees the agent's stdout and
   captures stderr, but never records stdin. Every client-to-agent message —
   prompts, permission responses, cancellations — is absent from every log ever
   collected.
3. **Exit codes are wrong.** The wrapper pipes into `tee` without `pipefail`, so
   the reported status is `tee`'s, not the agent's. A crashed agent looks like a
   clean exit.
4. **Logs cannot be named by session.** The wrapper opens its files at exec time,
   before any ACP session exists, so filenames fall back to timestamp + PID +
   binary name. It also writes logs for foreign binaries (codex-acp, node,
   copilot, claude-agent-acp) into the adapter's own state directory, mixing
   unrelated agents' output with the adapter's session store.

## Solution

Move logging into the binary and delete the script. Two subcommands, one shared
logging sink:

- `serve` — the existing DeepSeek/GLM adapter. Gains adapter-owned per-session
  logging written alongside the session store's existing artifacts, with the log
  path returned to the client in `_meta` the same way `historyJsonlPath` already
  is. Because the adapter owns the ACP transport, it logs both directions of the
  wire plus its own internal tracing events (LLM requests, tool dispatch, retry
  decisions).
- `proxy` — new. Wraps an arbitrary external ACP agent (claude-agent-acp,
  codex-acp, copilot) as a protocol-aware man-in-the-middle. Because it parses
  the NDJSON frame stream it sees the `session/new` response, so it can name logs
  by real session id — the thing the bash wrapper structurally could not do.

Serve-mode logs are a strict superset of proxy-mode logs: same record format,
same directory layout, so one reader works on either. Proxy is the degraded
version available for agents the project does not own.

## User Stories

1. As a user running the adapter from an ACP client, I want a per-session log
   written automatically, so that I can attach it to a bug report without
   installing anything.
2. As a client author, I want the session log path returned in `_meta`, so that I
   can offer "open logs" without the user learning where XDG state lives.
3. As a maintainer debugging an external ACP agent, I want to run the adapter's
   `proxy` subcommand in front of it, so that I get both directions of the wire
   recorded and named by session id.
4. As a maintainer, I want the same record format from both modes, so that one
   reading tool works regardless of which agent produced the log.
5. As a user, I want old logs bounded, so that the state directory does not grow
   without limit.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Given `serve` running with persistence enabled, when a session is created,
   then a log for that session is written under the session's own directory and
   its path is returned to the client in `_meta`.
2. Given `serve` running, when frames cross the ACP transport in either
   direction, then both directions are recorded — not just agent-to-client.
3. Given `proxy` wrapping an external ACP agent, when the agent answers
   `session/new`, then subsequent records for that session are written under a
   directory keyed by the real session id.
4. Given `proxy` wrapping an agent that exits non-zero, then `proxy` exits with
   the child's status, not a pipeline artifact.
5. Given `proxy` running, when the log sink cannot keep up, then frames are still
   forwarded to the child without stalling, and dropped records are counted.
6. Given records produced by either mode, when read by the same tool, then the
   envelope fields parse identically.
7. Given proxy mode writing session directories, when `session/list` is served,
   then proxied foreign sessions never appear as resumable adapter sessions.
8. `acp-debug.sh` is deleted and the README documents the subcommands in its
   place.

## Implementation Notes

- **Shared** (one module, both modes): state-root and directory-layout
  resolution, per-session file handles, the pre-session fallback sink, the record
  envelope format (NDJSON: timestamp, session id, direction, kind, payload), the
  non-blocking buffered writer with drop-on-full counting, and the
  retention/redaction policy.
- **Serve-only**: a `tracing` layer routing events to the right session by span
  field. Requires session-scoped code paths to run inside a span carrying the
  session id, and a fallback sink for events with no session (startup, model list
  fetch, `initialize`). This is the largest piece of work — span plumbing across
  the handlers, not a subscriber swap. The adapter currently has no file sink at
  all; tracing goes to stderr only.
- **Proxy-only**: child process management, stdin/stdout duplication, exit-code
  and signal propagation, and sniffing the session id out of the `session/new`
  response.
- Do not force a single trait over both producers — they are legitimately
  different. The shared asset is the sink, layout, and format.
- **Byte transparency is mandatory in proxy mode.** Copy the byte stream verbatim
  to the child and split a second copy for the sniffing parser. Never
  reconstruct frames from parsed JSON — key order, number formatting, and
  unknown-field drops would make debugging change behavior.
- ACP over stdio is NDJSON, one JSON-RPC object per line, so incremental framing
  is a newline split.
- **Do not let proxy output land in the session store.** The store enumerates
  directories and skips ones without a readable metadata file, so foreign session
  directories would accumulate as invisible garbage — or, if proxy ever writes
  its own metadata for correlation, would surface in `session/list` as resumable
  adapter sessions. Separate roots.
- **Pre-session records** (`initialize`, `authenticate`, and processes that never
  open a session at all — the large majority of existing log files) have no
  session id. Decision taken: write them to a connection-scoped file and record
  the mapping when a session appears, rather than buffering and backfilling.
  Connection-scoped is a real thing that exists; pretending otherwise leads back
  to timestamp-PID filenames.
- **Binary layout decision**: ship two `[[bin]]` targets from this crate rather
  than one binary with both verbs, or a separate repo. `proxy` uses none of the
  crate's core — no LLM client, no backend, no turn loop — so the name
  `acp-llm-adapter` undersells it; but the log format is the shared asset and
  will drift if it lives in two repos.
- **Redaction consistency**: request bodies are deliberately kept out of
  trace-level logs because they contain prompts, injected skills, and tool
  results. The current wrapper then tees the identical content via stdout anyway.
  The new sink must apply one policy to both paths.
- **Retention**: the existing state directory holds over a thousand files and
  hundreds of megabytes with no cleanup, including single logs in the tens of
  megabytes. Moving logging into the binary means owning that growth for every
  user by default, so a retention policy ships with the feature, not after it.

## Testing Notes

- Fake/child-process fixtures for `proxy`: assert byte-for-byte passthrough,
  exit-code propagation, and that a `session/new` response reroutes subsequent
  records.
- Assert that records emitted by `serve` and by `proxy` deserialize with the same
  envelope type.
- Assert `session/list` ignores proxy-produced directories.
- Assert the sink does not block the forwarding path when the writer is saturated,
  and that dropped records are counted.
- Follow the existing test-logging convention: `test-log` as the default test
  attribute; `tracing-test` only where a test must assert on log output.

## Out of Scope

- A log viewer or reader tool. This feature guarantees a shared format; building
  something that reads it is separate work.
- Migrating or converting the existing wrapper-produced log files.
- Backward compatibility for `acp-debug.sh` invocations. The project is in early
  development and breaking changes are acceptable.
close_reason: All 10 child tasks completed, including adapter/proxy logging, retention, routing, migration cleanup, and documentation.

title: Cancelling run_command leaks the shell's backgrounded descendants
description:
Cancelling a run_command turn now kills the shell it spawned (daa-zsjw), but not that shell's own descendants. A command that backgrounds work leaks it.

## Evidence

Standalone reproduction of the exact pattern src/tools/execution/mod.rs now uses - tokio::process::Command with kill_on_drop(true), dropped by a cancellation select:

    command: sh -lc "sleep 300 & echo $! > /tmp/killprobe.pid; wait"

    cancelled
    sh(337482) alive=false
    grandchild(337486) alive=true

kill_on_drop sends a signal to the direct child only. The backgrounded sleep survives with no owner, exactly like the detached Agent descendants daa-eyj2 dealt with on the proxy side.

## Why it was left out of daa-zsjw

Fixing it properly is a different shape of change from the cancellation fix: the command needs its own process group (process_group(0) on Unix) and the cancel path needs to signal the group rather than the pid. That means deciding the non-Linux story, since rustix is currently a Linux-only dependency in this crate and the proxy's reaping code is already cfg(target_os = "linux"). Bolting it onto the cancellation fix would have widened that change past what it was verified to do.

## Scope

- Give the spawned shell its own process group.
- On cancellation, signal the group, not just the child.
- Decide and document the behaviour on platforms without the group primitives rather than silently doing nothing.
- Regression test using the backgrounded-descendant shape above, asserting the grandchild is gone after cancellation.

## Note on the terminal branch

run_command_via_terminal delegates to the client's terminal/kill, so whatever the client does about descendants applies there. This issue is about the in-process branch only. Worth checking whether the two branches should promise the same thing, and saying so in the tool's documentation either way.
close_reason: gate:src/tools/execution/tests.rs — run_command_cancellation_stops_backgrounded_descendants. The shell now gets its own process group via tokio process_group(0) on unix, and cancellation signals the group with rustix kill_process_group rather than relying on kill_on_drop reaching only the direct child. Red first with the shape from the issue, sh -lc "sleep 300 & echo $! > file; wait": "backgrounded descendant 430343 outlived the cancelled turn". Green after, and stress-run 30 consecutive times, all ok, rather than trusting one pass - daa-fji9 was a flaky test I wrote earlier today and did not stress. Full suite 126/320/18/1/11 green, fmt, clippy --all-targets --all-features, cargo doc and cargo audit clean. The test reads the /proc state field rather than testing directory existence, because the orphaned descendant is exactly the unreaped-zombie case daa-vh77 turned on; it is Linux-gated for that reason while the fix itself is unix-wide. rustix moved from a linux-only to a cfg(unix) dependency - no new crate, wider target. PID reuse is addressed by reading child.id() before the wait future takes ownership: the child stays unreaped until that future drops, so the kernel cannot recycle the pid onto an unrelated process before the signal. Both open questions from the description are answered in the run_command_tool_execution doc comment rather than left implicit: the terminal branch delegates descendant handling to the client via terminal/kill, and non-unix targets kill only the shell, which is now stated as a known limit instead of silently tolerated.

title: Advertised /clear command leaves conversation history intact
description: Observed in the 2026-10-08 audit at 034bd20b16093a099d547dc68f1e5b3c7252016e. src/main.rs:109 advertises clear as clearing conversation history and starting fresh; its tests assert advertisement only. rg -n 'clear|slash|AvailableCommand' src/main.rs src/acp/mod.rs src/turn.rs src/session.rs src/session_store.rs finds no dispatcher or history reset operation. handle_prompt_request treats /clear as ordinary user text, so it goes to the provider with previous history. Implement exact ordinary-session /clear admission using the existing session-store boundary: no provider/tool invocation, empty in-memory and persisted conversation, clear acknowledgement, retained model/mode and accurate cumulative spend. Reject clearing an active turn; selected-content one-attempt contract must not be bypassed. This is newly found, not a reinterpretation of a closed implementation.

title: Large current prompts are silently dropped before generation
description:
An accepted ordinary prompt can disappear from the outgoing model request while ACP reports a successful turn. The provider then sees only its system instruction or older history.

## Observed and reproduction
Reality check 2026-10-08 at 96f55d7322d41484e5c7a7c029770cbcbab7d29f on main (clean), Linux, Rust 1.97.1. Actor/session: 01a11b68-765b-7aa3-afe2-05845b03b78e. All 592 tests, fmt, Clippy, rustdoc, release build, cargo audit and instruction-size check passed for the audited tree; these additional probes nevertheless reproduced the failures. Reproductions used the built target/debug/acp-llm-adapter, synthetic inputs and isolated temporary state; no live provider credentials or paid requests.
Initialize serve --backend mock and create an ordinary session. Submit one text block containing "USER-SENTINEL " followed by 270000 ASCII x characters.
Actual: stopReason end_turn; assistant starts "mock response to: You are a coding assistant helping with the user's project..."; USER-SENTINEL is absent. The mock echoes the final request message, proving the submitted text never reached it. The accepted prompt was persisted.
Expected: preserve the whole current prompt or explicitly reject it before any provider work; never silently replace it with older context.

## Root cause and missed coverage
src/turn.rs:311-314 prepends the ordinary system instruction. filter_messages_truncate pins messages[0] (:152-155), then skips any group larger than the remaining budget (:167-171). stream_model_turn applies a 256 KiB message budget (:730-746), so the current prompt is eligible for dropping.
Closed daa-wx1 changed oversized historical/tool-group handling to skip-and-continue; daa-rts repairs role/tool-pair structure. Their tests do not protect the current user request through the shipped entry point. This repair must retain their useful grouping behavior, not revert to dropping all older context at the first large group.

## Fix direction
Distinguish the current request from expendable historical groups at the admission/request-sizing boundary. Preserve it intact when representable; if it cannot fit, return a useful bounded-input error before provider work. Keep the ordinary system instruction and assistant/tool units intact. Do not silently truncate user content, raise the cap to hide the case, or introduce a summarizing model call.

## Acceptance and tests
- Shipped serve regression reproduces the first-prompt case; a local HTTP fixture independently proves either the complete sentinel-bearing prompt is sent or rejection occurs with zero completion POSTs.
- Cover an oversized later prompt, a small current prompt with oversized older history/tool results, and a subsequent valid prompt after rejection.
- Unit size-filter/admission tests preserve system instruction and paired tool call/results; no dropped current prompt may produce end_turn as if answered.
- Error remains sanitized; tests/logs report sizes and protocol stages rather than dumping the large prompt.
Negative check: inspect provider request content/call count and ACP error/stop reason; persistence alone does not prove delivery.

## Scope, ordering and handoff
Size M. src/turn.rs and focused turn/request-contract tests; admission code only if necessary. No prerequisites; independent request-sizing lane. No automatic summarization, provider-specific context router or history-format redesign.
Implementation is deferred because the maintainer approved recording the audit delta, not code changes. Leave open and unclaimed. Start with a failing regression, then make the narrow fix and run focused plus complete gates from docs/agent-testing.md. Stress lifecycle/time/filesystem regressions. Record the lesson and exact consumer/gate evidence before closure; obtain maintainer confirmation of the exact reproduction as required by the repository's live-defect acceptance policy. Live third-party editors/providers and Rust 1.95 were not verified by this audit.

title: Dependabot major updates conflict with manifest requirements
description:
Dependabot PR69 and PR70 cannot pass the locked CI gate because their proposed major dependency versions are excluded by the unchanged Cargo.toml constraints.

Observed 2026-10-08: PR69 head de0449f5ac879fb4082fc9f1b7e253cd4b9cf050 sets agent-client-protocol 2.2.0 in Cargo.lock while Cargo.toml:23 requires ^1.3.0. PR70 head a2367f8d1bf30ef7d38fc8066729a8704aac6c83 sets rmcp 3.5.0 in Cargo.lock while Cargo.toml:38 and :73 require ^2.2.0.

Reproduction: cargo +1.95 clippy --locked --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings on each head. Hosted runs https://github.com/euri10/acp-llm-adapter/actions/runs/37800485655 and https://github.com/euri10/acp-llm-adapter/actions/runs/37800484032 fail with "cannot update the lock file .../Cargo.lock because --locked was passed to prevent this", exit 101.

Root cause: manifest/lockfile mismatch in both bot proposals. daa-fvy5 already fixed the previously missing CI guard; these are the invalid proposals now correctly rejected. Baseline main e645918030ad012e21c8c688ea8efabb94fb3b24 passes CI37800886271.

Fix locally within daa-5izp: deliberately adopt the proposed dependency requirements, consult upstream changes and adapt only necessary code, retaining the proposed versions and --locked validation. Review major-version protocol compatibility and run the full local/hosted regression gates. Preserve separate PR branches.

Acceptance: exact original heads fail locked validation without changing Cargo.lock; each corrected head resolves the requested major version, passes full local and hosted CI, and is reviewed before merging. Record any newly discovered independent behavior defect separately. This issue records the existing two-PR proposal defect; implementation is owned by the claimed parent maintenance task.

title: Create renovate.json with conservative config at repo root
description:
## Goal

Create a `renovate.json` configuration file at the repository root that instructs Renovate to open individual PRs weekly with caret-style version bumping, no automerge, and Cargo manager enabled.

## Scope

- **In scope:** A `renovate.json` file extending `config:recommended` with explicit overrides for conservative behavior.
- **In scope:** Enable the `cargo` manager specifically.
- **Out of scope:** Any CI workflow changes (we use the GitHub App, not a workflow-based runner).

## Config (target content)

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://docs.renovatebot.com/renovate-schema.json",
  "extends": ["config:recommended"],
  "rangeStrategy": "bump",
  "schedule": ["on monday"],
  "labels": ["dependencies"],
  "packageRules": [
    {
      "matchManagers": ["cargo"],
      "rangeStrategy": "bump"
    }
  ]
}
```

## Config rationale

- `config:recommended`: sensible defaults (individual PRs, no automerge, Cargo.lock updates enabled, grouping for monorepo patterns).
- `rangeStrategy: "bump"`: ensures Renovate keeps the caret (^) style when opening PRs.
- `schedule: ["on monday"]`: weekly cadence as agreed.
- `labels: ["dependencies"]`: makes it easy to filter Renovate PRs in the GitHub UI.
- `packageRules` scoped to `cargo`: ensures Cargo-specific range strategy.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `renovate.json` exists at repo root.
2. Valid JSON that conforms to the Renovate schema.
3. `config:recommended` is extended (not replaced).
4. Schedule is weekly.
5. No `automerge` is enabled.

## Testing

- Validate with `npx --yes renovate-config-validator` or manually check against schema.
- No application behavior change — this is purely a config file.

## Notes

- This is a child of daa-cen (Renovate automation feature).
- Blocks on daa-90u (pin conversion) and daa-g8l (CI verification).
close_reason: renovate.json created with config:recommended base, rangeStrategy: bump, weekly schedule, dependencies label, no automerge

title: Closing active sessions abandons work and permits stale cleanup
description:
ACP session/close drops an active cancellation owner without cancelling it. Removing an active session (close/delete) also permits the same ID to be restored before the old prompt finishes cleanup; stale completion can then clear a newer prompt owner or publish stale history.

Observed 2026-10-08 in session 01a11b90-9116-76a2-8e2b-1dac48e77bb3, Linux mock/local tests after daa-dwmh active-restore guard. RED: LLM_API_KEY=skip-ci-no-key cargo test -q --all-features --bin acp-llm-adapter active_session -- --nocapture: closing_an_active_session_cancels_its_owned_turn fails with session/close abandoned ongoing work; removed_active_session_cannot_be_republished_before_cleanup fails with removed active owner was replaced before its cleanup (delete=false). Installed ACP schema CloseSessionRequest explicitly requires cancellation as if session/cancel then release resources. Existing close tests cover only idle sessions.

Root cause: src/session_store.rs remove_session removes resources/record without cancelling token; delete_session cancels then removes record before cleanup; insert_session_with_resources sees no remaining record; clear_active_turn clears solely by session ID. save_history snapshots under a lock but commits filesystem/memory after releasing it, permitting lifecycle removal between snapshot and commit.

Fix direction: cancel at removal; retain removed active ownership in SessionStore until token-qualified turn cleanup; reject publication while that ownership remains. Serialize persistence commit with removal within the existing blocking I/O boundary. No new scheduler or lifecycle service.

Acceptance/TODO: [ ] red store close and removal/republication regressions; [ ] shipped serve pending close approval causes no side effects after late reply; [ ] running child close/cancel is reaped; [ ] delete and close keep publication blocked until old cleanup; [ ] old cleanup cannot clear a newer token; [ ] no removed session history is resurrected; [ ] focused/stress/full gates; [ ] lesson to issue and README update.

Discovered from code and synthetic probes, no maintainer live-editor report. Related daa-dwmh handles replacing an active record; this separately handles removal of that record. Parent authorized completing discovered gaps after core daa-dwmh implementation.

title: Supply the normal-session agent instruction promised by the harness
description:
Reality check 2026-10-07 at 37388ac0611632a5cd6215a5aae22ad1e59d8b2d (main, clean). Linux, Rust 1.97.1. The 507-test suite, fmt, Clippy, docs, release build and cargo audit passed; the evidence below came from source inspection and bounded offline runs of the shipped binary. No live provider calls or real credentials were used.

## Goal
Ordinary coding sessions send a concise adapter-owned instruction describing the coding task, advertised tools and actual permission behavior, as promised by AGENTS.md's harness scope.

## Current evidence
src/acp/mod.rs:512-519 creates an empty history in Ask mode. src/turn.rs:249-257 only prepends a system message for Plan; :260-265 contains the sole production ChatMessage::system call. The other examples in src/lib.rs are library documentation/tests. Normal Ask/AcceptEdits/YOLO requests contain only conversation messages and tool definitions. The original vision in closed daa-682 explicitly includes a system prompt; no recorded decision removes it.

## Scope and plan
Add the smallest stable base instruction at existing request assembly. Keep it separate from user history and persistence so it is not duplicated on tool follow-ups or replay. Describe only implemented capabilities and the current permission/mode boundary. Compose Plan's restrictive instruction coherently with normal-session behavior. Selected-content sessions retain their own immutable tool-less contract and do not inherit new coding-agent authority.
Do not add runtime AGENTS/skill discovery, configurable persona frameworks, prompt templates for hypothetical providers or a new filesystem policy. Prompt text is advisory; approval and confinement remain executable controls. Update the public description to accurately state who supplies the instruction.

## Acceptance and tests
1. A normal ordinary-session provider request contains the adapter instruction, user content and only the actually advertised tools.
2. Tool follow-ups, multiple turns and load/resume do not accumulate duplicate system instructions or store them as user messages.
3. Plan remains read-only; selected-content input/tool/persistence bounds stay intact.
4. Focused request-assembly tests and a real serve/local HTTP capture prove the instruction reaches the provider. The negative gate fails if assembly omits the base instruction, even if helper text exists.
5. Existing permission, replay and model tests pass; no real provider/model-quality assertion is inferred from fixture success.

## Scope boundary
Size S. Independent of path-confinement policy resolution because the instruction must accurately describe current authority and never promise a new sandbox. This is behavior completion, not a documentation-only issue.

## Verification and handoff
Run the focused regression red before changing executable behavior, then the complete affected suite and repository gates in docs/agent-testing.md. Use temporary state directories and localhost fixtures with dummy credentials. Tests must assert the observed consumer behavior and identify the failing protocol stage without logging real payloads. Record the root-cause lesson here before closing. Implementation is deferred because this approved operation records the audit findings; nothing has been fixed or claimed.
notes: Related audit owners: daa-r3vu owns the domain/ACP split and daa-eja6 records the unresolved ordinary filesystem authority decision. The base instruction may truthfully describe current authority without deciding that question.

title: SIGTERM during model discovery exits unsuccessfully in CI
description:
The current main branch fails its real-process SIGTERM shutdown test before any of the authorized dependency PRs (#62, #64, #65) have been merged. This prevents establishing a green integration baseline.

## Observed
GitHub Actions CI run https://github.com/euri10/acp-llm-adapter/actions/runs/37787576665, main commit dbebccc872a24e97bc035810da223a62e8e6841b, 2026-10-08, ubuntu-latest with Rust 1.95.
Command: cargo test --all-features.
Exact failing evidence:
test termination_during_stalled_discovery_releases_request_and_exits ... FAILED
thread 'termination_during_stalled_discovery_releases_request_and_exits' (4228) panicked at tests/serve_model_discovery.rs:185:9:
assertion failed: tokio::time::timeout(Duration::from_secs(2), child.wait()).await??.success()
test result: FAILED. 3 passed; 1 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out; finished in 4.20s
The child returned an unsuccessful exit status; this assertion is not evidence of a timeout. CI does not print the child ExitStatus and suppresses child stderr.

## Root cause
Unconfirmed hypothesis: startup signal registration races with provider discovery. src/main.rs:438 registers listeners inside async shutdown_signal(), while serve's tokio::select! at line 499 can poll the discovery branch first. tests/serve_model_discovery.rs:181-184 sends SIGTERM immediately after observing the HTTP request, without proof that handlers were installed. A default signal exit would match the unsuccessful status.
Record the actual exit status and reproduce under controlled scheduling before asserting this mechanism.

## Why it was not caught
The coverage was introduced by closed daa-sowr and passed three recorded local stress rounds, but the same committed test failed in CI. Observing a provider request is not necessarily evidence of signal readiness. This issue preserves the new CI failure without changing the prior accepted closure.

## Fix direction
If confirmed, establish shutdown signal ownership before externally observable startup work at the narrow shared startup boundary. Preserve cancellation, EOF bounds, socket cleanup and existing logging behavior. Do not hide the failure with arbitrary sleeps, retries, or weaker success assertions.

## Acceptance
- Record reproducible failing evidence and the actual child termination status.
- Real serve handles SIGTERM during both stalled response headers and a stalled partial body, exits successfully within the existing bound, and releases the HTTP request.
- Focused shutdown/discovery coverage, meaningful stress or deterministic race coverage, and the complete required Rust 1.95 gates pass.
- The current main CI run is green before resuming dependency PR merges.

## Scope and handoff
Discovered while executing the user's request to merge dependency PRs #62, #64, #65. No PR was merged. Code changes are deferred pending the user's answer about expanding this task to fix CI first. No live provider calls are needed. Related prior issue: daa-sowr.

Hosted main CI 37793399896 passed every gate, following local Rust 1.95 full validation, deterministic SIGTERM red/green, 200 registration probes and 200 real discovery shutdown iterations. Eager Unix registration closes the startup race; lesson retained in issue comments and README documents registration before discovery. Dependency merges may now proceed.

title: ACP errors disclose offending provider payload values
description:
Reality check 2026-10-07 at 37388ac0611632a5cd6215a5aae22ad1e59d8b2d (main, clean). Linux, Rust 1.97.1. The 507-test suite, fmt, Clippy, docs, release build and cargo audit passed; the evidence below came from source inspection and bounded offline runs of the shipped binary. No live provider calls or real credentials were used.

## Observed defect
Malformed provider responses are returned to the editor with offending payload text and internal error details. The same presentation boundary is used for internal transport, storage and MCP failures.

Reproduction: run shipped serve --backend groq with a loopback provider, dummy key/model and temporary state. Complete ACP initialize/session/new and send a text prompt. The SSE response is:
    data: {"choices":[{"delta":{"content":"ok"},"finish_reason":"stop"}],"usage":{"prompt_tokens":"AUDIT_PROVIDER_PRIVATE_SENTINEL"}}

    data: [DONE]
Actual root-session response:
    {"error":{"code":-32603,"message":"Internal error","data":"LLM API error: failed to parse LLM response: invalid type: string \"AUDIT_PROVIDER_PRIVATE_SENTINEL\", expected u64 at line 1 column 129"}}
Expected: a useful stable protocol error without the sentinel or internal payload/path/credential details.

## Root cause and missed coverage
src/error.rs:84-97 maps AdapterError into ACP; the generic branch uses Error::into_internal_error, whose SDK implementation serializes err.to_string() into data. src/llm/error.rs preserves serde's offending scalar. Internal source errors should remain typed and available internally, but presentation currently exposes their full Display text. InvalidParams/InvalidRequest messages and MCP wrappers also need an explicit trusted-versus-untrusted presentation review.
Existing src/error.rs tests around :289-302 positively assert internal strings are returned, encoding the wrong boundary.

## Contract and repair plan
Sanitize at the adapter-to-ACP presentation boundary while preserving error classification and internal causes. Return safe contextual messages that let an editor distinguish invalid input, permission refusal, provider failure and storage failure. Do not expose prompts, tool payloads, API keys, environment values, signed URLs or local internal paths by interpolating raw error strings. Keep unknown optional peer fields tolerated where the protocol permits them.
Keep diagnostic causes internally without moving sensitive data into default tracing; this issue does not require raw error logging. The shared log redaction issue separately owns fields written to structured logs.

## Proof
Add a real serve/local-provider sentinel test for the exact bad usage string. Add focused translation tests for representative provider, MCP/header/URL, I/O and invalid-parameter failures. Assert useful error category and absence of synthetic secrets in every editor-visible error field. Assert causes remain available internally. Tests must fail if raw Display or Debug strings are restored to protocol data. Preserve normal successful responses and safe validation diagnostics.

## Scope and dependencies
Size M. Shared error presentation only; no broad error-framework rewrite or suppression of all diagnostics. No prerequisite. This repair is a real completion dependency of daa-uei because its original criteria require sanitized MCP configuration failures.

## Verification and handoff
Run the focused regression red before changing executable behavior, then the complete affected suite and repository gates in docs/agent-testing.md. Use temporary state directories and localhost fixtures with dummy credentials. Tests must assert the observed consumer behavior and identify the failing protocol stage without logging real payloads. Record the root-cause lesson here before closing. Implementation is deferred because this approved operation records the audit findings; nothing has been fixed or claimed.

title: Deep-dive ponytail-audit on the codebase
description:
Run a deep-dive skill:ponytail-audit across the entire project. Produces a ranked, read-only report of over-engineering findings: dead code, stdlib replacements, YAGNI abstractions, shrinkable logic. No code changes, no bead filing from findings. Informational only.

Operating parameters (from grill-me):
1. Lint rules are non-negotiable — findings caused by missing_docs, clippy::pedantic, etc. are noted and rejected.
2. Module cohesion vs. lean code evaluated case-by-case.
3. Each flagged item gets explicit justification if disagreed with.
4. No code changes, no child beads filed.
5. Both monoliths and over-abstractions are valid concerns.
6. Dependencies that serve real features (grep/ignore/globset) are fine; unused or redundant deps (potential blocking → tokio) are fair game.
7. One-shot: audit runs, report produced, done.

Acceptance criteria:
- A ranked list of findings produced covering the full codebase

title: Improve test coverage to at least 90%
description:
## Goal

Raise project-wide line coverage from the current 87.23% (1448/1660) to at least 90% (≥1494/1660), which requires covering 46+ additional lines across the codebase.

## Current Coverage (cargo tarpaulin)

| Module | Covered/Total | Pct |
|--------|--------------|-----|
| src/acp.rs | 165/227 | 72.7% |
| src/deepseek/client.rs | 36/37 | 97.3% |
| src/deepseek/config.rs | 27/29 | 93.1% |
| src/deepseek/error.rs | 2/2 | 100% |
| src/deepseek/stream.rs | 56/66 | 84.8% |
| src/deepseek/types.rs | 94/94 | 100% |
| src/main.rs | 415/474 | 87.6% |
| src/mcp.rs | 75/95 | 78.9% |
| src/tools.rs | 459/512 | 89.6% |
| src/turn.rs | 119/124 | 96.0% |
| **Total** | **1448/1660** | **87.23%** |

## Scope

- In scope: add targeted unit tests for uncovered lines in acp.rs, tools.rs, main.rs, mcp.rs, and deepseek/stream.rs.
- In scope: use test-log and tracing where tests benefit from observable output.
- In scope: follow all repo lint policies — no unwrap, expect, panic, todo, or unimplemented in test code.
- In scope: prefer Result-returning tests with explicit error assertions.
- Out of scope: refactoring production code to make it testable (unless trivial and obviously safe).
- Out of scope: changing module boundaries or architecture.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `cargo tarpaulin` reports ≥90% line coverage.
2. `cargo test` passes with no new failures versus baseline.
3. `cargo fmt --all` and `cargo fmt --all -- --check` pass.
4. `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings` passes.
5. No new unwrap, expect, panic, todo, unimplemented, or unsupported lint suppressions.

## Strategy

Focus on the highest-ROI modules first:

1. **mcp.rs** (78.9%, 20 uncovered) — error paths, edge cases in tool mapping and invocation
2. **deepseek/stream.rs** (84.8%, 10 uncovered) — streaming edge cases, error handling
3. **acp.rs** (72.7%, 62 uncovered) — handler edge cases, error responses
4. **tools.rs** (89.6%, 53 uncovered) — tool-specific edge cases, permission paths
5. **main.rs** (87.6%, 59 uncovered) — integration-level request handling paths

## Notes

- Run `cargo tarpaulin` before and after changes to verify progress.
- Each module can be tackled independently; no ordering dependency.
- The task is complete when the total reaches ≥90%.

title: Restructure AGENTS.md on the louiselm contract pattern
description:
The current AGENTS.md is the original numbered-sections document (§0-§8) written at project start. It mixes Rust policy, the test procedure, Beads operations and generic workflow prose in one 13KB file, and its Beads section is stale: it instructs the agent to use `bv` (beads_viewer, the Go tool) when this machine has `bvr` (beads_viewer_rust) installed, and it omits the actor/claim attribution rules.

Adopt the structure louiselm/AGENTS.md settled on: a short root contract that routes to required references, with detailed procedures in docs/agent-*.md. This is the acp-llm-adapter half of the open design question louiselm-l9w7.

## Scope
- Rewrite AGENTS.md as a routing contract: project scope, required-references table, work tracking and triage (br/bvr with bounded query recipes), architecture and lifecycle, errors and validation, security, editing and completion.
- Add docs/agent-workflow.md (Beads operation, actor attribution, claims, close verdicts), docs/agent-rust.md (toolchain, lints, unsafe, ownership, async), docs/agent-testing.md (baseline-first procedure, red-green-refactor, test-log convention, coverage, gates).
- Correct every bv reference to bvr --robot-*; record br 0.5.12 / bvr 0.3.0 as the checked versions.
- Add scripts/check-agent-instructions enforcing the root file size limit, wired into CI.

## Acceptance
- AGENTS.md is under the byte limit and the gate passes in CI.
- No surviving reference to bare `bv`.
- Every rule in the old §0-§8 is either in the new root contract or in a required reference; none silently dropped.

title: serve: tracing layer routing events to the per-session sink
description:
## Goal
Adapter tracing events are written to the log of the session that produced them.

## Scope
- In scope: a `tracing-subscriber` layer that reads the session id from the current span scope and writes the event through the shared sink to that session's destination; a fallback destination for events with no session; keeping the existing stderr output intact.
- Out of scope: the span instrumentation itself; wire-frame logging; `_meta` exposure.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. An event emitted inside a session's span is written to that session's log.
2. Two concurrent sessions do not cross-contaminate each other's logs.
3. An event with no session in scope is written to the connection-scoped fallback and is not dropped.
4. Existing stderr logging behaviour and `RUST_LOG` filtering are unchanged.
5. Adapter-internal detail unavailable to a proxy — LLM request cycles, tool dispatch, retry decisions — appears in the session log.

## Testing
- Drive two sessions concurrently and assert no events cross over.
- Assert an event emitted outside any session reaches the fallback.
- Assert `RUST_LOG` still filters as before.

## Notes
- The adapter currently has no file sink at all; tracing goes to stderr only. This adds a second destination rather than replacing the first.
- This layer is what makes serve-mode logs a superset of proxy-mode logs, which is the whole justification for the shared format.
close_reason: Added tracing-subscriber layer routing session-scoped events to per-session logs, explicit connection fallback, isolation test, and documentation

title: Oversized SSE events silently corrupt executed tool calls
description:
Losing an oversized provider SSE event can turn a valid streamed tool call into a different valid tool call that executes and reports success.

## Observed and reproduction
Reality check 2026-10-08 at 96f55d7322d41484e5c7a7c029770cbcbab7d29f on main (clean), Linux, Rust 1.97.1. Actor/session: 01a11b68-765b-7aa3-afe2-05845b03b78e. All 592 tests, fmt, Clippy, rustdoc, release build, cargo audit and instruction-size check passed for the audited tree; these additional probes nevertheless reproduced the failures. Reproductions used the built target/debug/acp-llm-adapter, synthetic inputs and isolated temporary state; no live provider credentials or paid requests.
Use a localhost /models and /chat/completions fixture and an isolated ordinary YOLO session. Stream one write_file call in three argument deltas: prefix {"path":"proof.txt","content":" ; 614400 ASCII x characters in ONE subsequent SSE argument delta; suffix END"}. Finish with finish_reason tool_calls and a valid completion terminator; answer the tool-feedback request normally.
Actual: proof.txt contains "END", length 3 instead of 614403; ACP tool status completed and prompt stopReason end_turn; provider fixture observes a second completion POST. The 600 KiB middle delta disappeared before argument assembly.
Expected: lost completion data fails the completion before any tool is authorized/executed or its assistant/tool history is committed.

## Root cause and missed coverage
src/llm/stream.rs:71-73 logs SseEvent::Discarded and continues. The installed SSE decoder's default event limit is 512 KiB, and src/llm/client.rs:254 leaves discard behavior enabled. Existing malformed/truncated/retry tests do not supply an oversized middle event whose omission leaves syntactically valid arguments.
Also src/llm/stream.rs:59-79 treats errors after saw_finish as success. Simply toggling a fatal-oversize option is insufficient if a final accounting/parser error is then swallowed as ordinary EOF.

## Fix direction
Reject the whole completion at the common SSE translation boundary whenever an event is lost; distinguish allowed clean post-finish termination from actual parser/oversize failures. Propagate typed errors to the existing prompt failure path. Do not raise/remove the size guard, reassemble by silently omitting chunks, or replay after output. Preserve bounded ordinary retries and selected-content single-send behavior.

## Acceptance and tests
- Shipped serve/local provider regression using the three argument deltas above produces a provider error, no permission request, zero file writes, no tool-feedback POST, and a usable next prompt.
- Unit stream tests cover lost text, thought, tool-argument and usage events; oversized frames before and after finish must not silently succeed.
- Failed accounting cannot become successful known cost/usage. No corrupted completed assistant/tool history is committed. Ordinary accepted user-prompt persistence remains governed by its existing contract.
- Selected-content helpers using the same decoder reject lost events without another POST; maintain output caps and deadline/cancel behavior.
- Normal bounded fragmented/interleaved calls, legitimate finish without [DONE], and valid trailing usage still work.
Negative check: assert absence of authorization, side effects and success status, not just a warning log. Keep synthetic payload contents out of diagnostics.

## Scope, ordering and handoff
Size M. src/llm/stream.rs, src/llm/client.rs, stream tests and one real-serve regression. No blocking dependency. Provider lane; coordinate client.rs edits with model discovery work. No decoder replacement or dependency addition.
Implementation is deferred because the maintainer approved recording the audit delta, not code changes. Leave open and unclaimed. Start with a failing regression, then make the narrow fix and run focused plus complete gates from docs/agent-testing.md. Stress lifecycle/time/filesystem regressions. Record the lesson and exact consumer/gate evidence before closure; obtain maintainer confirmation of the exact reproduction as required by the repository's live-defect acceptance policy. Live third-party editors/providers and Rust 1.95 were not verified by this audit.

title: acp-debug.sh logs full LLM request bodies by default
description:
## Context

`acp-debug.sh` is the documented debug wrapper and is the default launcher in
louiselm's chat. It sets:

```sh
export RUST_LOG="${RUST_LOG:-acp_llm_adapter::llm=trace}"
```

At trace level, `src/llm/client.rs` logs the entire LLM request body:

```text
TRACE acp_llm_adapter::llm::client: LLM request body request_body={...full prompt, skills, tool payloads...}
```

Those request bodies contain user prompts, injected skills/context, and tool
results. They are written unredacted to
`~/.local/state/acp-llm-adapter/*-stderr.log`.

## Proposed

Default `RUST_LOG` to `acp_llm_adapter::llm=debug` (or `info`) in
`acp-debug.sh`. Keep the `llm=trace` request-body logging strictly opt-in by
setting `RUST_LOG` explicitly. Consider also not logging `request_body` at trace,
or truncating/redacting it, since trace-level diagnostics should not routinely
dump prompts and tool payloads to disk.
close_reason: acp-debug.sh now defaults RUST_LOG to acp_llm_adapter::llm=debug; llm=trace is opt-in. client.rs no longer emits request bodies at trace (logs serialized byte size only). README + CHANGELOG updated. cargo test/fmt/clippy all pass.

title: Near-term ACP spec parity slice
description:
## Problem Statement

ACP clients need the DeepSeek adapter to close the agreed near-term spec parity gaps without over-advertising unsupported DeepSeek capabilities or chasing Claude-specific SDK extensions.

## Solution

Deliver one coherent near-term ACP parity slice: `session/delete`, live `session_info_update`, stable message IDs, and explicit model/tool-driven plan updates. Keep deferred items tracked separately and keep unsupported image/audio/blob prompt input unadvertised.

## User Stories

1. As an ACP client, I want to delete persisted sessions, so that session history can be managed through the protocol.
2. As an ACP client, I want metadata updates when title or activity timestamp changes, so that active session UI stays current.
3. As an ACP client, I want stable message IDs, so that streamed and replayed chunks are grouped consistently.
4. As a user, I want plan updates to reflect deliberate agent planning, so that plan UI is trustworthy.
5. As a maintainer, I want unsupported and deferred capabilities separated from near-term work, so that implementation stays honest.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Given an active or persisted session, when `session/delete` is called, then active state is cancelled/closed and persisted metadata/history are removed.
2. Given a prompt turn that changes session title or activity timestamp, when the turn starts, then the adapter emits `session_info_update` with the changed metadata.
3. Given a prompt request with or without a client `messageId`, when chunks and the final response are emitted, then ACP message ID fields are stable and UUID-shaped where required.
4. Given a prompt turn, when the adapter emits a plan, then the plan came from an explicit model/tool planning mechanism rather than prompt sentence splitting.
5. Given initialization, when capabilities are advertised, then image/audio/blob prompt input remains unadvertised and unsupported content is rejected clearly.

## Implementation Notes

- The ACP handler layer will need new `session/delete` registration and response handling.
- Session persistence needs a deletion operation for session directories/history.
- Prompt-turn setup should return enough metadata-change information to notify the client without holding locks across awaits.
- Message ID plumbing should be centralized so stream, replay, and response paths do not diverge.
- Plan updates should be represented as a tool or similarly explicit model-visible mechanism, not as a derived prompt helper.

## Testing Notes

- Follow existing ACP transport and handler tests for request/notification flows.
- Add persistence tests for deleting session records safely.
- Add prompt-turn unit tests for metadata notification and message ID propagation.
- Add tool-loop tests for explicit plan updates and regression coverage around the removal of fake prompt-split plans.
- Each implementation task must run the repo-required test/fmt/clippy procedure before closure.

## Out of Scope

- MCP SSE transport.
- ACP elicitation.
- Image/audio/blob prompt input support.
- Claude private `_meta` notifications or raw SDK message passthrough.
close_reason: Implemented and verified in code/tests

title: Renovate stops proposing ACP updates after repository rename
description:
Renovate appears to have stopped surfacing ACP dependency updates after the GitHub repository was renamed. The hosted Dependency Dashboard/Mend link still points at the former repository identity, so the current repository may no longer be receiving Renovate runs or may be using stale dashboard state.

## Observed

Observed in repository `euri10/acp-llm-adapter` on 2026-08-23.

Verifiable local artifacts:
- `renovate.json` extends `config:recommended`, sets `rangeStrategy: "bump"`, and restricts runs to `"on monday"`.
- `Cargo.toml:20` declares `agent-client-protocol = { version = "^1.2.0", features = ["unstable"] }`.
- `Cargo.lock:33-34` records `agent-client-protocol` at `1.2.0`.
- `Cargo.lock:65-66` records the transitive `agent-client-protocol-schema` at `1.4.0`.
- `cargo update -p agent-client-protocol --dry-run` reports: `Updating agent-client-protocol v1.2.0 -> v1.3.0`; it also reports latest `2.0.0), which is outside the declared 1.x range.
- `cargo info agent-client-protocol@1.7.0` reports: `error: could not find agent-client-protocol@1.7.0 in registry`.
- Git history shows Renovate dependency PRs through 2026-08-22, but no ACP update proposal.
- Baseline `cargo test -q` has one pre-existing failure: `logsink::tests::structured_payloads_share_one_redaction_policy` (121 passed, 1 failed).

The claimed “ACP library 1.7.0 vs 1.4.0” may refer to `agent-client-protocol-schema` rather than the direct `agent-client-protocol` package; this is not yet confirmed.

## Symptoms

- The user sees the Renovate dashboard/link associated with the old repository name.
- No Renovate proposal is visible for the ACP dependency despite a newer compatible release.
- The lockfile remains at `agent-client-protocol 1.2.0` / schema `1.4.0`.

## Root cause

Unknown. Hypotheses:
1. The Mend Renovate App retained the old repository identity/dashboard after the GitHub rename and is no longer processing the renamed repository.
2. The Monday-only schedule delayed the update until the next scheduled run.
3. Renovate's Rust extraction sees the direct dependency but does not independently propose the transitive schema version; the direct package update must be proposed first.
4. The expected 1.7.0 version is not the `agent-client-protocol` crates.io package.

Discriminate by checking the current GitHub repository's Mend Renovate job log and app installation, then forcing a run from the current Dependency Dashboard or re-onboarding the current repository.

## Why it was not caught

There is no repository-side test or CI check asserting that Renovate is installed on the current GitHub repository, that the dashboard belongs to the current repository, or that the lockfile is current. Existing Renovate PR history proves earlier runs worked but does not cover the post-rename app/dashboard state.

## Fix direction

Confirm the Mend app is installed for `euri10/acp-llm-adapter`; if the dashboard is stale, follow Renovate's documented re-onboarding procedure. Independently update the compatible ACP dependency/lockfile and consider removing the Monday-only schedule if timely updates are expected. Do not claim a repository rename as the root cause until the current job log confirms it.

## Acceptance

- A regression/verification check demonstrates the declared ACP dependency resolves to the intended current compatible release.
- Renovate is configured or re-onboarded against `euri10/acp-llm-adapter`, and the current dashboard/run can be verified externally.
- The direct package and transitive schema versions are explicitly distinguished in the resulting change.

## Not covered

- The direct package's major upgrade to 2.x is not covered; it may require protocol/API changes.
- The existing unrelated logsink test failure is not covered by this bug.
- Mend account/app installation state cannot be verified from the local checkout.
close_reason: Fixed local stale dependency and schedule: Cargo.toml now targets agent-client-protocol ^1.3.0 and Cargo.lock resolves 1.3.0; renovate.json no longer restricts runs to Monday. Verification: cargo update resolves 1.3.0 (latest 2.0.0 is outside the declared 1.x range), cargo fmt/check passed, cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings passed, cargo doc --no-deps passed. Full cargo test remains blocked by the pre-existing logsink::tests::structured_payloads_share_one_redaction_policy failure (121 passed, 1 failed), same as baseline. Mend app installation/dashboard re-onboarding remains an external verification item.

title: Review Dependabot PRs, fix failures locally, and merge verified updates
description:
## Goal
Process the open Dependabot pull requests: review CI and the proposed updates, merge acceptable updates, and repair failing updates locally before validating and merging them.

## Scope
One maintenance pass over the Cargo and GitHub Actions Dependabot PRs open when this task starts. Inventory the PRs at execution time; do not rely on historical check results. This is an execution task, not a new scheduled bot or CI-based repair system.

## Procedure
1. Record each PR URL, dependency/action and version change, current head SHA, diff review, CI status, and disposition. Check failed logs and distinguish update defects from unrelated baseline or infrastructure failures.
2. Merge updates only after compatibility/security review and all applicable checks pass for the final head. Pending, missing, cancelled, stale, or failing required checks do not qualify. Recheck branch/base changes as earlier updates land; respect repository merge protections.
3. For failures or conflicts, use a local checkout/isolated worktree, preserve the maintainer's changes and other agents' claims, reproduce the failure, and file a defect with failing evidence before fixing. Make the smallest local correction, deliberately update the manifest and lockfile together where needed, commit/push the repair to the PR branch, then wait for its final hosted checks before merging. Fixes happen locally, not in GitHub's editor or a new CI repair workflow.
4. Major agent-client-protocol/rmcp updates require deliberate compatibility review and the full regression pass. Consult current upstream migration/API documentation when adapting code; retain protocol, permissions, confinement and lifecycle behavior.
5. Record blocked or deferred work in Beads with evidence and actual blocking dependencies. Do not mask failures by weakening tests/lints/security checks, removing --locked, or silently downgrading the proposed dependency.

## Validation
Follow docs/agent-testing.md and the current .github/workflows/ci.yml. Establish a baseline before repairs; use red-green-refactor for behavior changes. Validate repaired branches with formatting, locked Clippy (all targets/features), cargo test --locked --all-features, locked doc-tests, docs with warnings denied, locked release build, cargo audit, and the instruction-size check. Use mock providers. Keep the scheduled audit's stricter warning policy distinct from ordinary PR CI. Record unavailable gates as blockers to the affected validation.

## Context
.github/dependabot.yml covers Cargo and GitHub Actions; renovate.json disables the previous updater. Read AGENTS.md and its required references at execution time.
Prior lesson daa-fvy5: PR #69 (ACP) and #70 (rmcp) changed only Cargo.lock to incompatible major versions; old CI silently downgraded them. Locked validation was added and their refreshed heads failed as expected. Treat these as historical leads and refresh their status before acting.
daa-sjn3 records the Cargo-specific Dependabot configuration validation lesson. Existing updater configuration need not change to perform this task.

## Completion evidence
Record per-PR review/check URLs, tested head and merged commit (or a concrete blocker with a follow-up issue). Confirm CI on the resulting default branch after merges. Route lessons into the relevant issue or standing instructions, or explicitly record that none are warranted.
acceptance_criteria: All PRs in the initial inventory have an evidenced disposition. Acceptable PRs are merged only after review and green CI on their final head; repaired PRs have local reproduction/fix/validation evidence and green hosted checks before merge. No required check is bypassed. Any unmerged PR has a concrete blocker and tracked follow-up. The final default branch CI result is recorded.

title: serve: return the session log path in _meta on new/load/resume/list
description:
## Goal
An ACP client can offer "open logs" without the user ever learning where XDG state lives.

## Scope
- In scope: returning the session's log path in `_meta` on session creation, load, resume, and list, mirroring how the history path is already exposed.
- Out of scope: any client-side UI.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. Session creation, load, resume, and list responses each carry the session's log path in `_meta`.
2. The path is absolute and points at a file that exists once the session has produced any record.
3. When logging is disabled, the field is omitted rather than present-and-wrong.

## Testing
- Extend the existing `_meta` assertions that already cover the history path so the log path is covered on the same four responses.

## Notes
- The mechanism already exists for the history path, so this is deliberately shaped as "same pattern, second field" rather than a new protocol surface.

title: Add CodeCompanion minimal repro config
description:
## Goal

Add a runnable minimal Neovim/CodeCompanion repro config that exercises `acp-llm-adapter` using the README-documented ACP setup.

## Scope

- In scope: add `examples/codecompanion-minimal.lua` as a single-file repro runnable with `nvim --clean -u examples/codecompanion-minimal.lua`.
- In scope: bootstrap `lazy.nvim` using the upstream CodeCompanion `minimal.lua` pattern.
- In scope: configure minimal CodeCompanion dependencies only: `plenary.nvim` and `nvim-treesitter`.
- In scope: install only the `lua`, `markdown`, and `markdown_inline` Tree-sitter parsers.
- In scope: define ACP adapters for `deepseek_acp`, `glm_acp`, and `mock_acp` using one small local helper to avoid repeated adapter tables.
- In scope: default chat interactions to `deepseek_acp` only.
- In scope: map `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY` and `Z_AI_API_KEY` to the adapter's `LLM_API_KEY` env var for provider-backed adapters.
- In scope: call `acp-llm-adapter serve --backend ...` directly by default, with a commented debug-wrapper alternative showing how users can enable `acp-debug.sh` log capture.
- In scope: use `defaults = { mcpServers = {} }` with no real MCP server examples.
- In scope: set CodeCompanion log level to `DEBUG`.
- In scope: update the README CodeCompanion section with a short link to the example file.
- Out of scope: adding completion plugins, inline adapter configuration, real MCP examples, API-key fail-fast validation, or backward-compatibility shims.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `examples/codecompanion-minimal.lua` bootstraps a minimal runnable CodeCompanion setup for ACP chat.
2. The example exposes `deepseek_acp`, `glm_acp`, and `mock_acp` adapters.
3. `deepseek_acp` is the default chat adapter.
4. Provider API keys are read from provider-specific env vars and passed to the adapter as `LLM_API_KEY`.
5. The default command uses `acp-llm-adapter serve --backend <backend>` directly, and the file includes a commented debug-wrapper alternative for log capture.
6. README links to the example from the CodeCompanion setup section without duplicating the full config.

## Testing

- Run the project's required pre-change baseline before editing.
- After editing, run `cargo test -q 2>&1 | grep -E "^test result|FAILED"`.
- Run `cargo fmt --all && cargo fmt --all -- --check`.
- Run `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`.
- If a Neovim/plugin smoke test is feasible in the environment, run the minimal config far enough to verify it loads; otherwise record why it was skipped.

## Notes

- This repo is early development; do not add compatibility shims.
- Keep the example portable for installed users while making local CodeCompanion checkout and debug-wrapper usage easy to uncomment for maintainers.

title: DeepSeek-backed coding agent over ACP
description:
## Problem Statement

ACP-speaking editors (Zed, neovim/CodeCompanion) can drive Claude and Codex as coding agents, but not DeepSeek. DeepSeek exposes only a chat-completions API (tool-calling + streaming) with no agentic engine, so no existing adapter turns it into a full ACP coding agent. The one DeepSeek+ACP precedent (CodeWhale) is TUI-first and exposes only text prompt/response over ACP — tool-backed editing and permissions are not surfaced.

## Solution

A headless, ACP-first adapter binary that presents DeepSeek V4 as a coding agent to any ACP client. We build the agent harness ourselves (system prompt, tool catalog, the prompt→tool-call→execute→feed-back loop, conversation history, permission gating) on top of DeepSeek's streaming API, and crucially surface tool calls, edits and permission prompts THROUGH ACP — the part prior art skipped. The editor is the only UI.

## Architecture

Two independent channels. Editor⇄adapter: JSON-RPC 2.0 over stdio, handled by the agent-client-protocol crate (the official rust-sdk). Adapter⇄DeepSeek: HTTPS + SSE to the OpenAI-compatible chat endpoint, via a thin client we own. The adapter is the translator + agent loop in the middle. A translation boundary keeps ACP/HTTP types out of the harness core (AGENTS.md: business logic must not depend on I/O).

## Scope (features / milestones)

Tracer-bullet sequence, each demoable in a real editor: M0 connects (streaming text), M1 reads (read-only tool loop), M2 edits + permissions (= v0.1 release line), M3 runs (hybrid shell), M4 polish (model picker, images, docs).

## Out of Scope

No TUI. No MCP client support, no loadSession, no auto model-router, no apply_patch-style edits in v0.1.

## Key Constraints

Strict AGENTS.md: forbid unsafe; clippy pedantic; no unwrap/expect/panic/todo; minimal audited deps; documented public APIs; never log secrets.

title: Forward DeepSeek token detail fields into ACP turn usage
description:
## Context

DeepSeek sends richer token detail than the adapter currently forwards.

`src/llm/stream.rs` `ChatCompletionUsage` parses only `prompt_tokens`,
`completion_tokens`, and `context_length` (aliased `context_window`). The raw
DeepSeek payload also contains:

```json
{"total_tokens":3465,
 "prompt_tokens_details":{"cached_tokens":3072},
 "completion_tokens_details":{"reasoning_tokens":173},
 "prompt_cache_hit_tokens":3072,
 "prompt_cache_miss_tokens":124}
```

ACP's per-turn `PromptResponse.usage` (`Usage`, behind
`unstable_end_turn_token_usage`) supports `thought_tokens`, `cached_read_tokens`,
and `cached_write_tokens`. `src/turn.rs` currently builds only
`Usage::new(total, input, output)` and drops the rest.

## Proposed

Extend `UsageData` (or the parse layer) to carry the extra fields and populate
the ACP `Usage`:

- `thought_tokens` <- `completion_tokens_details.reasoning_tokens`
- `cached_read_tokens` <- `prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens` or
  `prompt_cache_hit_tokens` (decide which is authoritative)
- `cached_write_tokens` <- `prompt_cache_miss_tokens` (mapping decision needed)

`total_tokens` from the API should also be used directly rather than recomputed
as input + output when present.
close_reason: Forwarded total_tokens, reasoning_tokens, prompt cache hit/miss details, and aggregated them into ACP turn usage; added focused parsing and aggregation tests.

title: M3: Shell command execution (hybrid terminal)
description:
## Problem Statement

Many coding tasks need to run commands (build, test, git). Zed offers terminal callbacks; CodeCompanion does not advertise terminal capability — so a single mechanism will not work across both targets.

## Solution

Add run_command: use client terminal/* when advertised (Zed), fall back to local tokio::process when not (CodeCompanion), permission-gated like other mutations.

## User Stories

1. As a Zed user, I want the agent to run commands in the editor terminal, so that I see output natively.
2. As a CodeCompanion user, I want commands to still run (locally), so that the agent works despite no terminal capability.
3. As a user, I want to approve commands, so that nothing destructive runs without consent.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Given clientCapabilities.terminal, when run_command executes, then it uses terminal/create + output/wait_for_exit/release and surfaces output.
2. Given no terminal capability, then it runs via local tokio::process and reports output through tool_call_update.
3. Given run_command in ask/accept-edits mode, then it requires permission; cancellation kills the child process.

## Implementation Notes

- Capability detection chooses terminal vs local at runtime. Cancellation aborts running child processes.

## Testing Notes

- Both paths (terminal advertised vs not); cancellation kills the child.

## Out of Scope

Background/long-running terminal session management beyond a single command; model picker; images.
close_reason: Implemented in the current patchset and verified by tests/docs

title: How should AGENTS.md compose the LouiseLM workflow across multiple repositories?
description:
## Context

The repository needs a clearer AGENTS.md design that integrates the LouiseLM workflow without duplicating the workflow inside project instructions. The current AGENTS.md mixes Rust policy, test procedure, Beads operations, and LouiseLM process. A proposed rewrite made LouiseLM the top-level lifecycle and used bvr for triage plus br for persistence, but the structure still needs design validation.

## Design question

What should live in a repository AGENTS.md versus shared LouiseLM skills or shared documentation when the workflow spans multiple repositories?

## Requirements to preserve

- LouiseLM should own the lifecycle: understand, confirm, route, and execute.
- The project should use bvr for read-only Beads triage and br for Beads mutations.
- Behavioral changes should use a red-green-refactor loop: failing test, minimal fix, refactor, full validation.
- Repository instructions should remain short, high-signal, and resistant to drift.
- Shared workflow rules should not be copied into every repository.
- Repository-specific Rust, architecture, testing, and safety constraints must remain local.
- Remote Markdown must not become an implicit or higher-priority instruction source.

## Options to evaluate

1. Thin repository AGENTS.md that points to shared LouiseLM skills and contains only local constraints.
2. A shared parent AGENTS.md for the multi-repository workspace, with small child AGENTS.md adapters per repository.
3. A versioned shared workflow document or repository template, synchronized deliberately into each repository.
4. A hybrid: shared lifecycle and vocabulary rules, local execution and validation rules.

## Questions to resolve

- Which repository is authoritative when the same project is opened independently?
- How should shared instructions be versioned and updated across repositories?
- Should vocabulary live in one shared Beads project or be repository-local?
- Where should red-green-refactor be specified: shared LouiseLM skill, project AGENTS.md, or both?
- How should bvr triage operate when several repositories share one backlog?
- What is the minimum local AGENTS.md content that still gives an agent reliable context?

## Acceptance

- A documented multi-repository instruction structure is chosen.
- Ownership is explicit for shared workflow, repository-specific policy, vocabulary, and Beads state.
- The resulting AGENTS.md template avoids duplicated work-selection instructions.
- The red-green-refactor test process is placed at the correct shared/local boundary.
- The current acp-llm-adapter AGENTS.md rewrite is either accepted, revised, or reverted based on the decision.

## Current state

The working tree contains an uncommitted AGENTS.md rewrite from this design discussion. No Rust source or test files were changed.
close_reason: Moved to louiselm-l9w7: this is a design question about the shared LouiseLM workflow's contract with per-repository AGENTS.md files, so the discussion belongs in the louiselm repo, not here. Content copied verbatim. The uncommitted AGENTS.md rewrite in this working tree was left untouched.

title: session/cancel during a running command is never exercised end to end
description:
Cancellation of a running command is verified at two levels and neither is the one an editor actually uses.

- src/tools/execution/tests.rs calls run_command_tool_execution directly with a cancelled token.
- tests/serve_shutdown.rs closes stdin, which drops the whole serve future.

The path in between is untested: the client stays connected and sends session/cancel while a command is running. That is what pressing the stop button in an editor does, and it is the common case.

## Why it is not covered by the other two

The disconnect test passes because the serve loop is dropped wholesale, which is a much blunter event than a cancellation - it would still pass if session/cancel did nothing at all. The unit test passes a token that is already cancelled or cancelled by the test itself, so it never exercises the wiring from an inbound session/cancel request to the token the tool is watching. A break anywhere in that wiring is invisible to both.

## Scope

Using the mock tool directive from daa-wu5e:

- Drive a long-running run_command through a real serve process.
- Send session/cancel for that session while it runs, keeping the connection open.
- Assert the prompt turn returns with the cancelled stop reason rather than hanging or reporting success.
- Assert the command and its backgrounded descendants are gone, reusing the /proc state check from tests/serve_shutdown.rs rather than testing directory existence (daa-vh77).
- Assert the session is still usable afterwards: a second prompt on the same session should work, since cancelling a turn must not kill the session.

## Related

daa-hivc was a leak on the disconnect path that the cancellation-only test could not see. The inverse gap is this one: if session/cancel stopped reaching the token, every existing test would still pass.
close_reason: gate:tests/serve_tool_calls.rs — session_cancel_stops_the_command_and_leaves_the_session_usable drives a real serve process, starts a long command, sends session/cancel as a notification with the connection left open, and asserts the turn returns stopReason cancelled, the client is told the call failed with "run_command cancelled", the backgrounded descendant is gone, and a second prompt on the same session still reaches end_turn - cancelling a turn must not take the session with it. The behaviour was already correct; this is the regression guard the issue asked for, so nothing in src changed. The premise was verified rather than asserted: wiring cancel_active_turn to a no-op makes this test FAIL after 20s while the pre-existing disconnect test still reports ok - the stop button could have stopped working and the old suite would have stayed green, which was the whole argument for filing this. Stress-run 20 times; full suite 126/323/18/2/3/11 green with fmt, clippy --all-targets --all-features and cargo doc clean. Noted while writing it and filed rather than folded in: daa-reep, no in_progress update means an editor shows a 300-second command as pending for its whole run.

title: Groq effort controls advertise Max and silently ignore High
description:
Reality check 2026-10-07 at 37388ac0611632a5cd6215a5aae22ad1e59d8b2d (main, clean). Linux, Rust 1.97.1. The 507-test suite, fmt, Clippy, docs, release build and cargo audit passed; the evidence below came from source inspection and bounded offline runs of the shipped binary. No live provider calls or real credentials were used.

## Observed defect
Every model is offered High and Max reasoning settings. High is omitted from outgoing requests; Max is serialized literally. Those controls do not describe the default Groq models' supported request contract.

Evidence: src/session.rs:135-139 and :423-428 define High/Max globally; :366-373 advertises them. src/turn.rs:341-346 omits High, and :670-671 plus src/llm/client.rs:218-219 send nondefault values unchanged.
Groq's current API states that openai/gpt-oss-20b and openai/gpt-oss-120b accept low/medium/high, default to medium, and reject values outside that model's set with HTTP 400: https://console.groq.com/docs/api-reference (reasoning_effort, checked 2026-10-07).
Thus selecting High actually requests Groq's medium default, while selecting Max builds an unsupported request. This is established from code and official documentation; no paid/live 400 was requested.

## Reproduction
Run serve --backend groq against a localhost model-list/completion fixture using openai/gpt-oss-120b and dummy credentials. Initialize and create a session; inspect configOptions. Select High and send a prompt, recording the HTTP request body; reasoning_effort is absent. Select Max and prompt; reasoning_effort is "max". A fixture enforcing the published per-model set rejects the second request.
Closed daa-qbe introduced settings mapped to DeepSeek parameters before Groq was added. The missing boundary is selected-model capability validation, not the existence of configuration handlers.

## Contract and repair plan
Advertised options, accepted updates, stored session settings and outgoing requests must agree for the selected model. For GPT-OSS, High must request high, and unsupported Max must not be advertised or admitted. Represent provider-default behavior honestly. Validate before changing session state or starting a provider call. Model switches, load/resume and restored settings must not preserve an invalid effort for the new model.
Use existing backend/model metadata and request-construction boundaries; choose the smallest explicit mapping. Look up provider contracts when adding values. Do not invent options for an unknown model; do not introduce a dynamic capability service or auto model router.

## Proof
Unit tests pin provider/model-specific option values and invalid-update rejection. Real serve/local-provider tests inspect configOptions and captured JSON for default, explicit High, invalid Max and model switching. Preserve DeepSeek/GLM behavior supported by their documented APIs. The negative gate fails if High is omitted after explicit selection or Max reaches a GPT-OSS HTTP request.

## Scope
Size M. Configuration fidelity only; usage envelopes have a separate owner. No live credentials, model-quality evaluation or broad public-API redesign.

## Verification and handoff
Run the focused regression red before changing executable behavior, then the complete affected suite and repository gates in docs/agent-testing.md. Use temporary state directories and localhost fixtures with dummy credentials. Tests must assert the observed consumer behavior and identify the failing protocol stage without logging real payloads. Record the root-cause lesson here before closing. Implementation is deferred because this approved operation records the audit findings; nothing has been fixed or claimed.
notes: Related audit owner: daa-n6lq covers Groq/provider usage envelope normalization. Coordinate edits to src/turn.rs and src/llm/client.rs with daa-alau; shared files are an ownership concern, not a fabricated dependency.

title: Byte-cap grep/read_file tool output so history can't accumulate multi-MB results
description:
grep_tool_execution and read_file_tool_execution cap output by LINE/ENTRY count (TOOL_OUTPUT_LIMIT=200) but never by bytes. A minified/vendor file (e.g. alpine.min.js) is few lines but each line is enormous, so a single read_file or grep match produces a multi-MB tool result. These get persisted into session history, which bloated to 39MB in the daa-rts repro and forced the aggressive filtering that corrupted message structure.

bash already byte-caps its output via truncate_tool_output(.., COMMAND_OUTPUT_LIMIT). Apply the same helper to grep and read_file content (the model/history path - raw_output display is separate and not persisted). This is the root-enabler fix; daa-rts fixed the resulting structural corruption defensively.

Fix: add FILE_OUTPUT_LIMIT and truncate_tool_output() the read_file file_slice and grep output_text before they become tool-result content. codex-acp/claude-agent-acp cap output the same way and never accumulate multi-MB results.
close_reason: Fixed: added FILE_OUTPUT_LIMIT (65536 chars) and applied truncate_tool_output() to read_file file_slice and grep output_text (src/tools/execution/mod.rs) - the model/history content path, same helper bash uses. Line-count caps still bound normal files; this is the wide-line safety net. 2 new tests; fmt+clippy+doc+300 tests green.
