title: Use ACP terminal methods for command tools
description:
Audit finding: run_command executes locally with std::process::Command and reports text output, but ACP v1 terminal methods allow terminal/create, output, wait_for_exit, kill, release, and terminal content embedded in tool calls when clientCapabilities.terminal is true.

Acceptance criteria:
- run_command uses terminal/create + wait/output/release when the client advertises terminal support.
- Tool calls can include terminal content so clients can display live output.
- Local process execution remains a fallback when terminal support is absent.
- Cancellation attempts to stop active terminal/process work.
- Tests cover terminal-capability routing and fallback behavior.
close_reason: Implemented ACP terminal methods for run_command with client terminal fallback

title: Add Groq as a first-class backend with provider metadata
description:
## Context

The adapter reaches Groq today only by abusing `--backend deepseek` with
`LLM_BASE_URL=https://api.groq.com/openai/v1`. That works — the LLM_* env vars
are provider-agnostic and the backend only supplies defaults — but the
configuration then names a provider it does not talk to, and Groq gets none of
the provider metadata DeepSeek and GLM have.

## Evidence

Verified live against Groq with `--backend deepseek` + env overrides:
`initialize` ok, session opened, streaming tool call executed
(`finish_reason: "tool_calls"`), prompt returned `stopReason: end_turn` with
usage `{totalTokens: 1019, thoughtTokens: 50}`.

No `usage_update` notification was emitted during that session. `src/turn.rs:701`
returns early when the provider reports no `context_length` and
`context_window_for_model` has no entry, so the client shows no context gauge
and no cost for any Groq model.

## Scope

- `src/dev.rs`: add a `Groq` backend variant with provider defaults
  (`https://api.groq.com/openai/v1`, `openai/gpt-oss-120b`). Collapse the
  duplicated per-backend env-reading block while doing it — DeepSeek, Glm and
  Groq differ only in their defaults.
- `src/llm/models.rs`: context windows for the Groq models, taken from Groq's
  own `GET /models` payload.
- `src/llm/pricing.rs`: Groq pricing. The function and env override are
  DeepSeek-named but no longer DeepSeek-only; rename to match what they do.

## Acceptance

`--backend groq` appears in `serve --help`; a Groq session emits `usage_update`
with a context window and a cost; full suite, clippy and doc gates green.
close_reason: Groq backend implemented, prices corrected against published tables, verified live

comments.author: claude/5f91cf74-f8bc-4915-9fdd-9037c24e1442
comments.text:
Implemented and verified live against Groq with the locally built binary.

`serve --help` now lists the backend:

    - groq:     Connect to the Groq API (`api.groq.com`)

Live ACP session with `--backend groq` and only `LLM_API_KEY` set (no
`LLM_BASE_URL`/`LLM_MODEL`), prompting a file read in a scratch cwd:

    >>> USAGE_UPDATE: {"used": 482, "size": 131072, "cost": {"amount": 9.8e-05, "currency": "USD"}}
      [tool_call] Read: note.txt
    >>> USAGE_UPDATE: {"used": 525, "size": 131072, "cost": {"amount": 0.000209, "currency": "USD"}}
    result: {"stopReason": "end_turn", ...}

Both acceptance halves hold: the context window is populated (131072, from the
model table) and cost accrues across turns. Before this change the same session
emitted no `usage_update` at all, because `turn.rs:701` returns early for a
model with no known window.

Cost arithmetic cross-checked by hand: 438 input x $0.15/M + 44 output x
$0.75/M = $0.0000987, matching the reported 9.8e-05.

Regression checks on the two existing backends, using the same harness:

- `--backend deepseek`: 402 Payment Required. Reproduced identically on the
  released 0.7.5 binary that predates this change, so it is account balance,
  not the refactor.
- `--backend glm`: 429 Too Many Requests. Auth accepted and endpoint correct
  (a misrouted base URL would be 401/404); provider-side rate limiting.

Because neither live backend could complete a turn, the refactor that collapsed
their duplicated client construction is pinned by
`each_live_backend_keeps_its_own_defaults` instead — nothing previously asserted
the DeepSeek or GLM defaults, so a URL/model mix-up would have been silent.

Gates: 489 tests pass (baseline 484 + 5 new, 0 failures), `cargo fmt --check`,
`cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -D warnings`, `cargo doc` with
`RUSTDOCFLAGS=-D warnings`, and `scripts/check-agent-instructions` all green.

Note for review: the published Groq rates ($0.15/$0.75 per M for gpt-oss-120b,
$0.075/$0.30 for gpt-oss-20b) were transcribed from Groq's pricing page, not
fetched from an API — there is no pricing endpoint. The context windows *were*
taken from Groq's live `GET /models` payload. If the rates drift, `LLM_PRICING`
overrides them without a recompile.

comments.author: claude/5f91cf74-f8bc-4915-9fdd-9037c24e1442
comments.text:
## Lesson

The context windows in this change were correct because they were read from
Groq's live `GET /models` payload. The prices were wrong because they were
written from memory instead — gpt-oss-120b output was off by 25%, and the code
asserted Groq had no prompt-cache tier when it bills cache reads at half the
input rate. Both errors survived a green suite, because the tests asserted the
same remembered numbers the implementation used: a table and a test that agree
prove consistency, not accuracy.

The existing rule in docs/agent-rust.md covers third-party *crate* docs ("look
up a third-party crate's current documentation rather than guessing at method
signatures or feature flags"). It does not cover third-party *provider* facts —
prices, context windows, model ids — which are equally external, change more
often, and unlike a wrong method signature do not fail to compile.

Worth considering as an instruction amendment: any provider constant committed
to a table cites the page or API response it came from, and is fetched at the
time of writing rather than recalled. Left as a suggestion here rather than an
edit to the contract, which is the maintainer's to change.

## Closing evidence

Rates now cite the per-model pages
(<https://console.groq.com/docs/model/openai/gpt-oss-120b>, and the 20b
equivalent). Corrected in 278461d and verified live: a 431-input/27-output turn
reports $0.000080, matching 431 * $0.15/M + 27 * $0.60/M computed by hand.

Full acceptance as filed: `--backend groq` is listed in `serve --help`; a Groq
session emits `usage_update` with `size: 131072` and an accruing cost; suite
(489 tests), fmt, clippy `-D warnings`, `cargo doc` and the instruction size
check all green.

Two follow-ups were filed rather than folded in: daa-models-context-window-9cr3
(prefer the provider's own `/models` context_window over the static table) and
daa-base-url-desync-sx0r (P1 — `LLM_BASE_URL` is ignored by the model fetch,
found while verifying this work).

title: Migration scripts for removing acp-debug.sh
description:
## Goal
Two migration scripts so removing `acp-debug.sh` does not strand the existing config or the accumulated logs.

## Scope
- In scope: `scripts/migrate-legacy-logs.py` converting wrapper output into the new NDJSON layout; `scripts/migrate-config.py` reporting every config that launches an agent through the wrapper, with the correct per-entry replacement.
- Out of scope: automatically editing editor configs. The correct replacement differs per entry and a wrong automated rewrite to a dotfile is worse than a list the user applies.

## Status
Both written and exercised against real data. Log migration verified on a copied sample first, then dry-run against the live state directory: 584 connections, 376 of them version polls, 208 convertible, 58 sessions recoverable, 199MB. Config reporter verified against the live louiselm config, correctly classifying all 8 references.

## Notes
- This reverses a scope decision recorded on the parent feature, which listed migrating wrapper-produced files as out of scope. The user explicitly asked for a migration path, which is also the condition the project's development-phase rule requires before adding one.
- The log script routes by origin exactly as the running code does: this project's adapter to the state root, foreign agents to the proxy root. Old adapter session logs therefore land beside the `history.jsonl` those sessions already have.
- Version polls are detected exactly, from the `argv:` header the wrapper wrote, not guessed from file size. They are 64% of the legacy directory; converting them would move the old clutter into the new layout.
- Three things are unrecoverable and the script says so in its output and in a marker record it writes per connection: per-record timestamps (the wrapper stamped filenames, not lines), stdout/stderr interleaving (separate files, no shared ordering), and the entire client-to-agent direction (never teed).
- Session detection here is a heuristic the live sniffer does not need: with only one direction recorded there are no requests to correlate a `session/new` response against, so any `result.sessionId` or `params.sessionId` is taken at face value.
- A `logsink` test now asserts the Rust envelope deserialises a real migrated line, so the two implementations cannot drift.

## Follow-up
Both scripts are single-use and should be deleted once the migration has been run.
close_reason: Both scripts written and exercised against real data. Log converter verified on a copied sample before touching originals; live dry run reports 584 connections, 376 version polls, 208 convertible, 58 sessions, 199MB. Config reporter classifies all 8 live references correctly after fixing a bug where the wrapper's own path (which contains the adapter's name) made foreign agents look like the adapter.

title: Enforce Plan mode during turns
description:
## Goal
Make Plan mode enforce read-only behavior during model turns.

## Scope
- In scope: filter mutating tools out of the outgoing request, inject planning instructions only for Plan mode, and refuse any leaked disallowed tool call at execution time.
- Out of scope: session mode parsing, persistence, and ExitPlanMode.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. In Plan mode, the outgoing request does not advertise mutating tools or MCP tools.
2. In Plan mode, the outgoing request includes the planning instructions only for that turn and not in saved history.
3. In Plan mode, any disallowed tool call is rejected by the adapter before execution.
4. Leaving Plan mode restores normal request assembly and tool availability.

## Testing
- Integration coverage for the generated request contents.
- Regression coverage that the planning instructions are request-local.
- Coverage for the read-only execution backstop.

## Notes
- Treat this as self-enforced read-only behavior; do not rely on external SDK permission semantics.

title: Add ExitPlanMode transition flow
description:
## Goal
Add a transition flow that lets a plan session request exit from Plan mode and move into another mode.

## Scope
- In scope: a permission-prompt style transition that offers the next available modes and updates the active mode when the user chooses one.
- Out of scope: the slice 1 mode model, read-only enforcement, and planning prompt behavior.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. While a session is in Plan mode, the adapter can request an exit transition instead of continuing to plan indefinitely.
2. The user can choose the next mode from the offered options and the session updates to that mode.
3. The current mode update is visible to the client after the transition completes.

## Testing
- Cover the transition prompt and the resulting mode update.
- Verify the session resumes normal behavior after leaving Plan mode.

## Notes
- This is intentionally separate from the initial Plan-mode slice because it depends on the model reliably calling a transition tool.
close_reason: Implemented exit plan transition flow

title: Cancelling built-in tool approval can still execute the tool
description:
Cancelling a prompt while a built-in edit or shell tool awaits editor approval does not stop the approval wait. A later approval may still start the command or mutate a file.

Observed 2026-10-08 at 034bd20b16093a099d547dc68f1e5b3c7252016e; baseline Rust 1.95 cargo test --locked -q: 543 passing. Source verified by this session and an independent read-only audit.

Evidence: src/tools/execution/mod.rs:1024 require_tool_permission awaits request_tool_permission without a cancellation token. write_file_tool_execution (:389), edit_file_tool_execution (:472), and run_command_tool_execution (:631) all use it. run_command spawns the child before checking cancellation (:707, :722). File tools receive no token. src/turn.rs:488 iterates all tool calls without stopping between calls. MCP has its own cancellation-aware approval at src/mcp.rs:110-121, but the built-in boundary lacks it.

Why not caught: existing command cancellation tests use immediate approval and assert return time, not that approval waits end or that no side effects start. The serve MCP test covers only MCP approval.

Acceptance:
- A shipped-serve regression cancels at pending built-in approval; prompt returns cancelled promptly without approval, no command executes, late approval cannot execute it, and a subsequent prompt succeeds.
- File write/edit and terminal/local command tests cover pending and already-cancelled approval, with zero writes/spawns; check cancellation after awaited reads and before mutation.
- A cancelled tool batch starts no later calls and returns cancelled even on the last allowed loop iteration.
- Keep running-command cleanup, remembered permissions, selected-content and MCP behavior intact.
- Full suite, fmt, Clippy, rustdoc and release build pass.

Plan/TODO:
[ ] Record exact red regression output.
[ ] Make the shared approval boundary cancellation-aware and thread the existing token through built-in file tools.
[ ] Check before dispatch and before file mutation; stop cancelled tool batches.
[ ] Add meaningful local/client file and terminal tests plus real stdio approval/late-reply/recovery regression.
[ ] Run focused tests red/green and stress lifecycle regression.
[ ] Update public cancellation contract; run affected/full gates.
[ ] Record root-cause lesson and close with evidence.

Other ordered work remains in existing owners: daa-2boq base instruction; daa-8mrl effort settings; daa-n6lq usage envelopes; daa-r3vu protocol separation. daa-eja6 awaits the explicit filesystem-authority choice; daa-uei depends on protected claims; daa-kzl5 requires maintainer/editor confirmation. No competing claims taken.

title: Client disconnect leaves a running command's descendants alive
description:
Found by the serve-level test the mock work (daa-wu5e) made possible, and fixed in the same change.

Closing the client connection while a run_command is still running left the command's backgrounded descendants alive after the adapter had exited.

## Evidence

Driving a real "acp-llm-adapter serve --backend mock" over ACP, running "/bin/sleep 300 & echo $! > file; wait", then closing stdin:

    serve 562630  shell child: 562650  descendant: 562654
    serve exit: 0 after 0.00s
      shell 562650:      GONE
      descendant 562654: S      <- still running, adapter already gone

After the fix the same probe reports the descendant as Z, i.e. killed.

## Root cause

daa-0yi0 put the process-group kill on the cancellation branch of the tokio::select! only. Client disconnect does not go through cancellation: the serve loop's select! takes the shutdown branch and the whole serve future is dropped, so the turn's future is dropped without anything being cancelled. On that path kill_on_drop still reaped the shell - which is why the shell was GONE - but nothing ever signalled the group.

The kill belonged on the drop path all along. Cancellation is one way to stop waiting for a command; the client going away is another, and both should take the command's descendants with them.

## Fix

A CommandGroup guard owning the process group id, killing it in Drop, released only when the command runs to completion. Completion is deliberately excluded: if the command exited on its own, whatever it chose to leave behind is its business, and killing a daemon a user explicitly started would be a different bug.

## Verification

tests/serve_shutdown.rs::serve_shutdown_takes_a_running_commands_descendants_with_it drives the real binary through initialize, session/new, a tool call, the permission round-trip and the disconnect. Mutation-checked rather than assumed: with the guard owning None the test fails with "descendant 565964 outlived the disconnected client", and 20 consecutive runs pass with the fix in place.
close_reason: gate:tests/serve_shutdown.rs — serve_shutdown_takes_a_running_commands_descendants_with_it. The process-group kill moved from the cancellation branch to a CommandGroup drop guard, so it fires on every path that stops waiting for the command, including the client disconnect that drops the serve future without cancelling anything. Released on normal completion by design: a command that exited on its own keeps whatever it deliberately left, since killing a daemon a user started would be a different bug. Mutation-checked rather than assumed - with the guard owning None the test fails with "descendant 565964 outlived the disconnected client" after 5.04s, and passes 20 consecutive runs with the fix. Full suite 126/323/18/2/11 green, fmt, clippy --all-targets --all-features and cargo doc clean. This completes daa-0yi0, which I closed earlier today having attached the group kill to one branch when it belonged to the drop path; the earlier test only ever exercised explicit cancellation, so it could not see this.

title: Expose max_tokens as a session config option
description:
## Problem

The DeepSeek ACP adapter currently exposes three session config options:
- mode (ask, accept-edits, yolo)
- model (deepseek-v4-pro, deepseek-v4-flash)
- reasoning_effort (high, max)

There is no way to control `max_tokens` (the maximum number of tokens the model can output per response), even though the DeepSeek API supports it via the `max_tokens` parameter.

From https://github.com/euri10/deepseek-acp-adapter/issues/8

## Solution

Add `max_tokens` as a session config option, similar to how model and reasoning_effort work:

1. Add `max_tokens: Option<u32>` to `ChatRequest` with a `with_max_tokens()` builder
2. Add `max_tokens` to the wire `ChatCompletionRequest` struct in client.rs
3. Add `max_tokens: Option<u32>` to `SessionRecord`
4. Add `max_tokens: Option<u32>` to `TurnSetup`
5. Add `max_tokens: Option<u32>` to `ModelRequestSettings`
6. Wire it through `stream_model_turn` into `ChatRequest::with_max_tokens()`
7. Add `SESSION_CONFIG_MAX_TOKENS_ID` constant
8. Register it as a session config option in `session_config_options()`
9. Handle it in `handle_set_session_config_option_request_notifying`
10. Validate the value (must be a positive integer)
11. Update tests

## Implementation Notes

- Use `Option<u32>` — `None` means "use the model's default" (don't send the parameter)
- The config option should be a text input (not a select), accepting an integer string
- Keep it simple: allow any positive integer, let the API reject invalid values
- Default is `None` (unset) — the DeepSeek API uses its own default when not specified
close_reason: Implemented max_tokens as a session config option. Since the pinned agent-client-protocol 0.14.0 only supports select/boolean config kinds (no freeform text), exposed it as a select with a 'Default' entry plus common presets (4096-131072) rather than the originally-noted freeform text field. Wired end-to-end: ChatRequest::with_max_tokens -> ChatCompletionRequest wire field (omitted when unset) -> SessionRecord/TurnSetup/ModelRequestSettings -> session persistence (PersistedSessionMeta). 7 new tests added across session/turn/acp/deepseek test modules, full suite green (294 tests), fmt+clippy+doc clean.

title: Add Plan session mode
description:
## Problem Statement

Users need a selectable planning mode for ACP sessions that is read-only by design, but still produces a concrete step-by-step implementation plan.

## Solution

Add a fourth session mode, "Plan", that appears in the mode picker and config surface, persists across resume, prevents file edits and command execution, and injects planning instructions so the model responds with an implementation plan rather than carrying out changes.

## User Stories

1. As a user, I want to switch a session into Plan mode, so that I can ask the adapter to investigate and outline work without making changes.
2. As a user, I want Plan mode to stay read-only, so that accidental edits or command execution are prevented.
3. As a user, I want the plan to come back through the normal plan/update channel, so that I can review it in the same session flow.
4. As a user, I want Plan mode to persist when a session is resumed, so that the session keeps its intended behavior.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Given a new or resumed session, when the mode list is shown, then Plan appears alongside the existing modes.
2. Given a session in Plan mode, when a request is assembled, then mutating tools are not advertised and planning instructions are included only for that request.
3. Given a session in Plan mode, when the model attempts a disallowed action, then the adapter refuses execution and the session remains read-only.
4. Given a session saved in Plan mode, when it is restored, then it still opens in Plan mode.

## Implementation Notes

- Touch the session mode model, the mode picker/config surface, and the request assembly path.
- Keep the planning instructions request-local; do not persist them into history.
- Treat the plan mode as self-enforced read-only behavior rather than delegating to an external SDK.

## Testing Notes

- Cover mode parsing, mode IDs, default mode lists, and config option acceptance.
- Cover request-time filtering of mutating tools and the injected planning instructions.
- Cover the execution backstop for leaked or disallowed tool calls.
- Cover persistence and resume behavior.

## Out of Scope

- ExitPlanMode transition flow.
- Slash commands for entering plan mode.
- Any model-specific coupling.

title: M2: File editing with permissions over ACP (v0.1)
description:
## Problem Statement

The whole point of the adapter: let DeepSeek edit code with the user in control. Prior DeepSeek+ACP art does not surface edits or permissions through ACP. This feature is the v0.1 release line.

## Solution

Add write_file and edit_file (string-replace) via client fs, gated by session/request_permission, with permission-posture modes (ask / accept-edits / yolo) switchable via session/set_mode. Edits render as native diffs in the editor.

## User Stories

1. As a user, I want the agent to edit files, so that it can implement changes.
2. As a user, I want to approve or reject each edit, so that I stay in control.
3. As a user, I want to choose a posture (ask / accept-edits / yolo), so that I trade safety for speed.
4. As a user, I want edits shown as diffs, so that I can review them in my editor.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Given a mutating tool in ask mode, when the agent wants to run it, then it first calls session/request_permission offering allow_once/allow_always/reject_once/reject_always and proceeds only on allow.
2. Given allow_always for a tool, then later calls of that tool in the same session are not re-prompted.
3. Given edit_file, then the file is read (via client fs) first, the exact old_string is replaced, and the result written via fs/write_text_file (native diff shown); a missing or non-unique old_string fails the tool with a clear error fed back to the model.
4. Given mode=accept-edits edits auto-allow but shell still prompts; mode=yolo auto-allows all; session/set_mode switches posture live.

## Implementation Notes

- String-replace edit (NOT apply_patch) — DeepSeek is weaker at exact patch syntax; the write still goes through client fs so the editor renders the diff.
- Permission memory keyed per-tool per-session.
- Modes advertised in session/new (currentModeId/availableModes).

## Testing Notes

- proptest the string-replace (apply-then-read-back invariants); no-match/ambiguous-match cases. Permission gating + allow_always memory; mode posture matrix.

## Out of Scope

Shell/terminal, model picker, image input, MCP.
close_reason: Implemented in the current patchset and verified by tests/docs

title: Provider token counts crash debug builds and wrap release usage
description:
Reality check 2026-10-07 at 37388ac0611632a5cd6215a5aae22ad1e59d8b2d (main, clean). Linux, Rust 1.97.1. The 507-test suite, fmt, Clippy, docs, release build and cargo audit passed; the evidence below came from source inspection and bounded offline runs of the shipped binary. No live provider calls or real credentials were used.

## Observed defect
Malformed provider token counts are consumed with unchecked arithmetic. Debug serve exits instead of replying; release serve reports an impossible successful zero-token total.

Reproduction: start real serve --backend groq against a localhost /models and /chat/completions fixture with dummy key/model audit-model and isolated state. After ACP initialize/session/new/session/prompt, emit a normal content "ok" / finish_reason "stop" chunk with:
    "usage":{"prompt_tokens":18446744073709551615,"completion_tokens":1,"context_length":4096}
Then emit [DONE].
Observed debug result: exit 101; "src/turn.rs:796:24: attempt to add with overflow"; no prompt response.
Observed release result:
    {"stopReason":"end_turn","usage":{"totalTokens":0,"inputTokens":18446744073709551615,"outputTokens":1}}
    {"sessionUpdate":"usage_update","used":0,"size":4096}
The release reproduction used a fresh successful cargo build --locked --release --all-features.

## Root cause
src/turn.rs:794-796 computes input_tokens + output_tokens in unwrap_or, eagerly even when a supplied total is present. UsageTotals::add at :553-565 and src/llm/pricing.rs:30 contain related unchecked counter arithmetic. Values originate outside the process.
Existing usage fixtures contain small internally consistent numbers and do not distinguish debug panic from release wraparound.

## Contract and fix direction
Validate consumed usage counters and derived sums at the shared normalization/accumulation boundary before notification, cost or session-state mutation. Use checked arithmetic and a typed error for invalid or unrepresentable totals; do not invent a plausible zero or silently clamp malformed values into valid telemetry. Preserve unknown-usage behavior and legitimate cache/thought accounting. Inspect both per-response and cumulative additions, including an explicitly supplied total and cost conversion limits.

## Proof
Unit tests cover boundary additions, inconsistent/unrepresentable counters, cumulative multi-tool-turn totals and ordinary small usage. A localhost provider regression through shipped serve sends the exact payload above and requires a bounded protocol error, a still-live usable adapter and no fabricated usage/cost update. The negative test must fail on both current debug and release behavior. No huge allocation or stress run is necessary.

## Scope
Size S. Counter validation only; valid provider-specific usage frame shapes belong to the separate normalization issue, and presentation sanitization has its own owner. No dependency is needed to start this repair.

## Verification and handoff
Run the focused regression red before changing executable behavior, then the complete affected suite and repository gates in docs/agent-testing.md. Use temporary state directories and localhost fixtures with dummy credentials. Tests must assert the observed consumer behavior and identify the failing protocol stage without logging real payloads. Record the root-cause lesson here before closing. Implementation is deferred because this approved operation records the audit findings; nothing has been fixed or claimed.
notes: Related audit owners: daa-n6lq owns supported usage envelopes; daa-2jci owns safe ACP error presentation; daa-u8tu owns tool-index allocation limits. No claim that malformed numeric counts and sparse tool indices share one implementation defect.

title: Shared sink: retention bounds and one redaction policy for both paths
description:
## Goal
Logging can be turned on by default for every user without the state directory growing without bound or writing prompt content the project already decided not to write.

## Scope
- In scope: a size and age bound applied by the shared sink, with old records removed; one redaction policy applied to both wire frames and tracing events; documented defaults.
- Out of scope: a log viewer; migrating existing wrapper-produced files.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. Records past the configured age or total size bound are removed, and the bound holds across process restarts.
2. Content the project excludes from trace-level logging is excluded from wire-frame logging by the same policy — the two paths cannot disagree.
3. Defaults are documented and overridable.
4. Retention never deletes the session store's own artifacts, only log records.

## Testing
- Drive the sink past both bounds and assert enforcement, including across a simulated restart.
- Assert a payload that redaction should remove is absent from both a wire record and a tracing record.

## Notes
- Request bodies are deliberately kept out of trace-level logs because they contain prompts, injected skills, and tool results. The current shell wrapper then tees the identical content via stdout anyway, so the policy exists on paper but not in practice. One sink is the chance to make it real.
- The existing state directory holds over a thousand files and hundreds of megabytes with no cleanup, including single logs in the tens of megabytes. Turning logging on by default without this ships that growth to every user.
notes:
Reality check 2026-10-07 at 37388ac0611632a5cd6215a5aae22ad1e59d8b2d (main, clean). Linux, Rust 1.97.1. The 507-test suite, fmt, Clippy, docs, release build and cargo audit passed; the evidence below came from source inspection and bounded offline runs of the shipped binary. No live provider calls or real credentials were used.

## Observed defect
Enabling structured logs while retaining default redaction writes source-derived titles, shell command arguments and output in clear text. The same shared sink affects serve and acp-proxy.

Reproduction: run target/debug/acp-llm-adapter serve --backend mock with an isolated XDG_STATE_HOME, ACP_LOG=1 and ACP_LOG_UNREDACTED=0. Initialize, create a normal Ask session, submit "!tool run_command printf AUDIT_LOG_SECRET_SENTINEL", and approve the harmless command. Search the resulting session log for the marker.
Actual stored fields include:
    session_info_update.title = "!tool run_command printf AUDIT_LOG_SECRET_SENTINEL"
    tool_call.title = "printf AUDIT_LOG_SECRET_SENTINEL"
    tool_call.rawInput.command = "printf AUDIT_LOG_SECRET_SENTINEL"
    session/request_permission.toolCall.rawInput.command = "printf AUDIT_LOG_SECRET_SENTINEL"
    tool_call_update.rawOutput.stdout = "AUDIT_LOG_SECRET_SENTINEL"
The content field on that final frame was "[REDACTED]" while rawOutput retained the same output. Both server and proxy paths were reproduced.
Inspection artifact at audit time: /tmp/acp-audit-selected.rtVx1K/logging/acp-llm-adapter/sessions/session-f261a5a8-f128-4088-b8e5-3cf44f354249/log.jsonl lines 3,4,5,8. This temporary path is supplementary; the recipe and exact fields above are the durable evidence.

## Root cause and missed coverage
src/logsink.rs:723 recursively applies a key list at :741-745 containing only arguments/content/input/messages/prompt/text. ACP exposes equivalent payloads under rawInput, rawOutput, titles, edit fields and nested configuration. Existing generic prompt/arguments fixtures do not represent these actual messages.

## Contract and repair plan
Preserve the original acceptance criteria and current retention policy from daa-kz74: unbounded/foreign logs and session metadata/history must remain protected. Correct the shared redaction boundary for actual ACP frame shapes and tracing events. Preserve structural diagnostics such as method, status, tool id, timing and session routing. Treat opaque tool arguments/results and source-derived titles as content; cover configured credentials/env/header values where frames can contain them. Explicit ACP_LOG_UNREDACTED=1 remains the intentional opt-out. Do not alter live ACP payloads delivered to the editor.

## Proof
Use synthetic sentinels through both shipped serve and proxy. With unset/0 unredacted flag, scan every written record and assert no sensitive sentinel remains anywhere, while structural diagnostics remain useful. Cover command output, file edits, permission requests, session titles, MCP configuration and malformed/raw frames. With explicit opt-out, sentinels must be present. Preserve all shared-retention and artifact-preservation regressions. A generic {"prompt":"secret"} test alone must not satisfy this issue.

## Scope
Size M. Independent logging lane. No log viewer, retention redesign, historical-log deletion, or default enabling of logging. Keep the fix at the shared sink.

## Verification and handoff
Run the focused regression red before changing executable behavior, then the complete affected suite and repository gates in docs/agent-testing.md. Use temporary state directories and localhost fixtures with dummy credentials. Tests must assert the observed consumer behavior and identify the failing protocol stage without logging real payloads. Record the root-cause lesson here before closing. Implementation is deferred because this approved operation records the audit findings; nothing has been fixed or claimed.

title: Proxy with default log retention deletes other agents' unlimited-retention logs
description:
Any acp-proxy process started without unlimited retention deletes other agents' proxy logs, including agents configured with `ACP_LOG_MAX_BYTES=unlimited` / `ACP_LOG_MAX_AGE_DAYS=unlimited`. It happens silently whenever such a process starts and the shared log directory is above that process's limit. On this machine it removed the evidence of a finished QA round and about half of all connection logs.

## Observed

Found 2026-09-24 while resuming LouiseLM QA round `louiselm-hz8mz` (Codex compaction events), session `claude/f81a23f5-242f-430f-b0c5-767b206c5765`. Environment: acp-proxy 0.8.0 (`~/.cargo/bin/acp-proxy`, built 2026-09-21 18:41), repo at `775d3b9`. Log root `~/.local/state/acp-llm-adapter/proxy/`.

Per-agent environment in `~/dotfiles/nvim/.config/nvim/lua/config/plugins/louiselm.lua`: codex, claude, copilot, opencode and grok pass `ACP_LOG_MAX_BYTES = "unlimited", ACP_LOG_MAX_AGE_DAYS = "unlimited"`; antigravity passes only `ACP_LOG_UNREDACTED = "0"`, so it gets the defaults (100 MiB, 30 days).

- `sessions/a11d1b78-1ca2-48ba-939b-022a9b899d90/log.jsonl` (127556 bytes, Claude session, evidence for closed QA round `louiselm-pbu4i`) existed on 2026-09-22. On 2026-09-24 the directory is empty; directory mtime `2026-09-23 17:28`.
- Antigravity connection log `connections/466f0163-53bb-4d4f-a461-db97065d2b5d.jsonl` written `2026-09-23 17:28:35.93 +0200`: the same minute.
- Antigravity connection `connections/636f8b4c-4440-441f-9d5f-9a16b74d574b.jsonl` at `2026-09-24 05:07:39.66 +0200` matches the `connections/` directory mtime (`2026-09-24 05:07`).
- Connection logs: 239 on 2026-09-22, 134 on 2026-09-24. Session `log.jsonl` files remaining: 18, oldest dated 2026-09-22.
- `du -sb` of `connections` + `sessions` after the sweeps: 10517533 + 88779262 bytes = 94.7 MiB, just under the 100 MiB default, as a size sweep would leave. Nothing was 30 days old, so the byte limit did the deleting.

## Symptoms

- Proxy logs of Codex/Claude sessions disappear although their agents ask for unlimited retention.
- Nothing reports it; no error, no record of which process removed what.

## Root cause

`RetentionPolicy::from_env` (`src/logsink.rs:137-158`) reads the limits from each process's own environment. `LogWriter::prune` (`src/logsink.rs:544-567`) then applies that one process's limits to every file returned by `log_files()` (`src/logsink.rs:569-574`), which collects all of `connections/` and `sessions/` under the shared root. It sorts by mtime and deletes oldest first until the total is under this process's `max_bytes` (default `DEFAULT_MAX_BYTES` = 100 MiB, `src/logsink.rs:73`). So the most restrictive process running decides retention for every agent.

The code path is verified by reading. The link to the antigravity process is inferred from matching timestamps and the remaining size; it has not been reproduced.

## Why it was not caught

`retention_bounds_apply_on_startup_and_preserve_session_artifacts` (`src/logsink/tests.rs:430`) and `retention_overrides_parse_unlimited_values_and_positive_bounds` (`:545`) use a single writer with a single policy. No test has two writers with different policies on one root. `daa-kxx7` (closed) introduced the shared-sink retention without that case.

## Fix direction

Undecided; options:

- Prune only files this process owns (a per-process or per-agent subdirectory, or a record of written files). Keeps each agent's policy meaningful.
- Record each writer's policy in the root and apply the most permissive one seen. Simpler but keeps one global policy.
- Rejected as the fix: only aligning the dotfiles env. That is the workaround (give antigravity the unlimited env too), but any future agent without it silently deletes the rest again.

## Acceptance

- A regression test: writer A with unlimited retention writes logs; writer B with a small `max_bytes` on the same root starts and prunes; A's logs survive.
- On the live machine, starting an agent with default retention no longer removes logs of agents configured as unlimited.

## Not covered

- Not reproduced on the live machine; mechanism from source plus timestamps.
- The deleted logs are not recoverable.
- The age-based sweep (`src/logsink.rs:545-551`) has the same shared scope; not observed here because nothing was 30 days old.
close_reason: Fixed in d0d05d8. Root cause: per-process retention policy applied to the shared log root. Fix: writers record bounds in <file>.retention; sweeps only evict logs whose record accepts a bound; unknown retention is kept; default unlimited. Tests: 4 red-then-green logsink tests; suite 501 passed; fmt/clippy/doc clean. Live: on a copy of the real proxy root with a 1-byte bound, old binary left 0/163 logs, fix kept 163; installed acp-proxy 2026-09-24 05:22; QA round louiselm-hz8mz ran on it and its session log carried an unlimited record. Maintainer confirmed the fix on 2026-09-24. Lesson recorded in the issue comments: shared state with per-process policy must record intent beside the data.

comments.author: claude/f81a23f5-242f-430f-b0c5-767b206c5765
comments.text: Attribution correction: this bug was filed by claude/f81a23f5-242f-430f-b0c5-767b206c5765; the created_by 'assistant' came from the br skill fallback, which docs/agent-workflow.md forbids.

comments.author: claude/f81a23f5-242f-430f-b0c5-767b206c5765
comments.text:
Fix implemented (uncommitted at time of comment; commit follows). Each writer records its bounds beside a log in <file>.retention (most permissive writer wins per axis); prune only evicts logs whose record accepts a bound on that axis; logs with no record (all pre-existing logs, foreign processes) are never evicted. Default RetentionPolicy is now unlimited on both axes; invalid/zero overrides stay unlimited. DEFAULT_MAX_BYTES/DEFAULT_MAX_AGE removed. README updated.
Red first: 4 new tests failed before the fix (a_bounded_writer_never_evicts_logs_written_under_unlimited_retention, a_bounded_writer_never_evicts_logs_of_unknown_retention, any_unlimited_writer_keeps_a_shared_log, default_retention_never_evicts). retention_bounds_apply_on_startup_and_preserve_session_artifacts now seeds its logs through a bounded writer (hand-written files are unknown retention, kept by design).
Gates: cargo test 501 passed (baseline 497), 5 more full runs clean; logsink tests 40x stress clean; fmt, clippy -D warnings, cargo doc -D warnings clean. One earlier full run reported one failed test in a target that was not captured; it did not recur in 6 runs; not attributed.
Live reproduction on a copy of the real ~/.local/state/acp-llm-adapter/proxy (163 logs, 100 MiB), XDG_STATE_HOME pointed at the copy, ACP_LOG_MAX_BYTES=1 ACP_LOG_MAX_AGE_DAYS=1, `acp-proxy -- true`: installed 0.8.0 binary left 0 logs / 0 MiB; fixed build left 163 logs / 100 MiB.
Lesson: shared state with per-process policy must record the owner's intent next to the data; the deletion test only ever used one writer. Kept open for maintainer confirmation per docs/agent-testing.md.

title: MCP approval maintainer confirmation
description:
# Final acceptance — 2026-10-08

Accepted: all three required real-editor cases and optional running-tool cancellation/recovery passed. The maintainer confirmed "yes all was normal afaict" after the last exact Session, adapter_mcp_qa/session-9f2d27f9-d125-4c9d-ab12-41d9520f74da. Fixture totals: invoked=2 cancelled=1. Last cancellation settled in 35 ms; recovery returned OK with no late tool success.

The sole final round report is LouiseLM louiselm-sx1on, including exact Session IDs, counts, times, build hashes, setup checks, lessons and retained evidence. Temporary adapter_mcp_qa/adapter_audit configuration was removed; installed setup/headless normalization and formatting pass. Normal Agents and Codex QA remain unchanged. Build/logs/live chat are retained.

Separate input finding louiselm-qszkk remains open: literal <D-v> during case 3. Its source is unknown; acceptance does not claim it fixed. Implementation owner of daa-deo retains that claim and receives the acceptance evidence.

## Historical plan and earlier findings

The original description below is retained as history. Its blocked/unrun/incomplete statuses describe the earlier round, not the final result above.

# MCP approval and cancellation: maintainer confirmation

Maintainer confirmation round for daa-deo, fixed by commit 38f42f1. In progress: the maintainer independently ran the scripted production-path reproduction and supplied its passing transcript. The required real-editor cases have not been run. The previous closure was premature; the implementation and its passing automated evidence remain unchanged. The maintainer uses LouiseLM in Neovim. Its installed session lifecycle starts new Sessions with an empty MCP-server list, so the original fixture setup cannot currently reach the required manual cases. The maintainer will add native MCP support to LouiseLM, then resume this QA round.

## Status

| Case | State |
| --- | --- |
| Scripted production-path regression | Passed: 7 tests, 0 failures, 0.20 seconds; maintainer transcript |
| Editor Ask: reject before invocation | Not run; setup blocked on F2 |
| Editor Ask: allow exactly once | Not run; setup blocked on F2 |
| Editor cancellation during approval | Not run; setup blocked on F2 |
| Optional editor cancellation during invocation | Not run; setup blocked on F2 |

## Scripted check

From a terminal:

```sh
cd /home/lotso/code/acp-llm-adapter
cargo build --locked --bin acp-llm-adapter --example mcp_stdio_fixture
LLM_API_KEY=skip-ci-no-key cargo test --locked --test serve_mcp_permissions -- --nocapture
```

Expect seven passing tests and exit status zero. The example build is explicit because a focused integration-test invocation need not rebuild the example artifact.

The tests launch the actual adapter binary, a localhost HTTP/SSE provider, and the stdio MCP fixture, using dummy credentials. They assert rejection with zero invocations, approval with exactly one invocation and provider result feedback, AcceptEdits/YOLO, remembered decisions, Plan/selected-content refusal, cancellation during approval and invocation, and session recovery. This checks adapter behavior; it does not exercise your editor's approval UI or prove that your normal editor configuration launches the freshly built executable.

## LouiseLM setup limitation — resolve before testing

The maintainer confirmed LouiseLM in Neovim. Both the checkout and installed plugin construct new Session parameters with `mcpServers = {}`:

- `/home/lotso/code/louiselm/lua/louiselm/session/lifecycle.lua:1227`
- `/home/lotso/.local/share/nvim/site/pack/core/opt/louiselm.nvim/lua/louiselm/session/lifecycle.lua:1227`

LouiseLM's Agent configuration has no MCP-server setting. The adapter's `serve --help` likewise exposes no alternative MCP configuration flag. Therefore the `defaults.mcpServers` example below is CodeCompanion-specific and must not be pasted into LouiseLM's closed configuration schema. The absence of a permission dialog in a Session with no audit MCP server is not a rejection/approval QA result.

Two possible routes, neither implemented in this round:

1. Temporary QA-only ACP wrapper that supplies the harmless audit fixture in new-Session requests. This leaves LouiseLM's source unchanged and exercises its real permission UI, but does not certify native MCP configuration.
2. Implement native MCP-server configuration in LouiseLM first. This is work in a different repository and needs the maintainer's direction.

Selected route: the maintainer will implement native MCP support in LouiseLM. Do not prepare the temporary wrapper or change LouiseLM in this adapter session. Resume manual QA after the maintainer reports that the installed plugin can attach the audit fixture through `session/new.mcpServers`. Keep the scripted pass and all unrun manual statuses unchanged until actual results are supplied.

Verified LouiseLM commands for the eventual manual cases are `:LouiselmChat`, `:LouiselmSessionNew`, `:LouiselmSessionOptions`, and `:LouiselmCancel`. Prompt submission is Insert-mode Enter. Approval selection uses the configured `vim.ui.select` provider, so physical keys depend on that provider. Dismissing the permission picker is not equivalent to explicitly cancelling the ACP turn.

## Reference fixture setup — not yet runnable through ordinary LouiseLM Sessions

1. Build using the first two commands above.
2. Temporarily point your editor's adapter command to the absolute executable below, keeping your usual provider/backend arguments and credentials:

   ```text
   /home/lotso/code/acp-llm-adapter/target/debug/acp-llm-adapter serve --backend YOUR_USUAL_BACKEND
   ```

   Restart the adapter process so the editor uses the new build. A new conversation inside an old process is insufficient.
3. Add this harmless server to the MCP servers sent to ACP session/new. With this repository's CodeCompanion configuration, that is the adapter's defaults.mcpServers array:

   ```json
   {
     "name": "audit",
     "command": "/home/lotso/code/acp-llm-adapter/target/debug/examples/mcp_stdio_fixture",
     "args": ["manual-qa"],
     "env": [
       {"name": "ACP_LLM_ADAPTER_RUN_MCP_FIXTURE", "value": "1"},
       {"name": "MCP_FIXTURE_TOKEN", "value": "manual-qa"},
       {"name": "MCP_FIXTURE_MODE", "value": "echo"},
       {"name": "MCP_FIXTURE_INVOCATION_LOG", "value": "/tmp/acp-mcp-qa.UixYSM/invocations"}
     ]
   }
   ```

4. Start a fresh ordinary session and select Ask. Use a fresh session for each case so remembered permissions and earlier model replies do not affect the result. Keep the same invocation-log path; compare the count before and after each case. The fixture records invocations, not server startup/tool discovery.

## Invocation evidence

This command prints the number of tool invocations:

```sh
if [ -f /tmp/acp-mcp-qa.UixYSM/invocations ]; then
  awk '$0 == "invoked" { n++ } END { print n+0 }' /tmp/acp-mcp-qa.UixYSM/invocations
else
  printf '0\n'
fi
```

The committed regression already validates that the fixture writes one invoked record per call and a cancelled record after receiving remote cancellation. Counts prove execution or non-execution; only your observation establishes whether the editor showed a usable dialog and recovered its input after cancellation.

## Cases

### 1. Reject in Ask

Record the initial invocation count. In a fresh Ask session, send:

> Call mcp__audit__stdio_echo exactly once with {"message":"manual-confirm"}. Do not use another tool. If I reject it, stop without retrying.

Wait for the approval dialog before choosing an option. The invocation count must still equal its initial value. Choose Reject once.

Expect: a permission request for the MCP echo tool, a failed/rejected tool result, and an unchanged invocation count.

Failure signature: the count increases before approval or after rejection, or the tool completes without any permission request.

If the model selects a different tool or never selects the echo tool, this case did not reach the changed path; it is not a pass. If it asks again after rejection, record that separately as model retry behavior and check that no rejected attempt executed.

### 2. Allow in Ask

Open a fresh Ask session, record the invocation count, and send the same prompt. Choose Allow once.

Expect: the counter increases by exactly one, the tool completes, and its output contains:

```text
stdio echo: manual-confirm; arg: manual-qa; env: manual-qa
```

Failure signature: no approval dialog, more than one invocation, or no completed tool result/output after approval.

### 3. Cancel while approval is pending

Open a fresh Ask session and record the invocation count. Send the same prompt, then cancel the turn using the editor's cancellation action while the permission dialog is pending.

Expect: no new invocation, the turn ends, the editor is usable, and a follow-up prompt such as "Reply OK without calling tools" completes.

Failure signature: the tool executes, the pending dialog blocks further input, or the session cannot accept another prompt. Closing a dialog is not enough unless the editor also cancels the ACP turn.

### 4. Optional: cancel during execution

Open a fresh Ask session and send:

title: Acknowledged session settings disappear on close and resume
description:
A successfully selected read-only posture can revert to automatic tool approval when the session is restored.

## Observed
Set YOLO, complete an ordinary mock prompt (persists YOLO), successfully set Plan, close, resume: response reports currentModeId=yolo. Expected Plan. Reproducer: /tmp/acp-reality-sessions-b3plnxoc/reproduce.py; root independently confirmed. src/session_store.rs:345-391 changes settings only in RAM; src/acp/mod.rs:517 reloads saved mode.

## Root cause and missing coverage
Mode/model/effort/token setters do not persist acknowledged changes. Existing restore tests save through a subsequent prompt, hiding idle-setting loss.

## Fix direction and acceptance
Persist acknowledged ordinary settings at the common session-store boundary, including both set_mode and mode config selector, model, reasoning effort and max tokens. Do disk I/O off the async executor and avoid locks across await. A failed save must report sanitized storage failure and preserve coherent in-memory state; no successful acknowledgment followed by stale disk settings. Keep selected-content sessions nonpersistent. Serialize settings/history lifecycle sufficiently to prevent a concurrent prompt save or close/delete from undoing settings or resurrecting state. Reuse existing persistence and locking conventions; no generic transaction framework.

Unit and shipped-serve regressions: YOLO saved -> Plan acknowledged -> close/load and close/resume retain Plan without a second prompt; all config settings survive restart/restore; unset optional values survive; disk failure preserves state; selected-content updates never create raw history or restorable metadata. Confirm existing concurrent prompt ownership and delete guarantees. Size M/L; root owns session_store.rs, acp settings handlers and relevant tests.

## Audit boundary and verification
Reality check 2026-10-08 at dbebccc872a24e97bc035810da223a62e8e6841b, main, initially clean, Linux. title: Multi-provider backend with dynamic model discovery

title: Prefer provider /models context_window over the static table
description:
## Context

`KNOWN_CONTEXT_WINDOWS` in `src/llm/models.rs` is a hand-maintained table, and
`src/turn.rs:701` suppresses the whole `usage_update` when a model is missing
from it. Every new provider model therefore silently costs the client its
context gauge until someone edits the table.

## Observation

Groq's OpenAI-compatible `GET /models` already returns the answer per model:

    openai/gpt-oss-120b   context_window=131072  max_completion_tokens=65536
    qwen/qwen3.8-27b      context_window=131042  max_completion_tokens=16384

The adapter already calls that endpoint — `fetch_available_models` in
`src/llm/client.rs` hits `{base_url}/models` at startup for the model picker —
and throws the `context_window` field away, keeping only the ids.

## Proposed

Capture `context_window` during the existing model fetch and prefer it over the
static table, keeping the table as the fallback for providers that omit the
field. No extra request: the call already happens.

Deliberately deferred out of daa-groq-backend-jbm5, which only needed the Groq
rows. This changes behaviour for DeepSeek and GLM too, so it wants its own
red-green pass rather than riding along with a backend addition.

## Acceptance

A model absent from `KNOWN_CONTEXT_WINDOWS` but present in the provider's
`/models` payload still produces a `usage_update` with the correct window.

title: Remove fixed prompt turn cap that ends long tool conversations
description:
Observed behavior:
- Long conversations with repeated model-requested tool calls stop with ACP stopReason=max_turn_requests.
- Example log from 2026-06-04:
  DEBUG connection{name="deepseek-acp-adapter"}: ... Response { id: Number(3), method: "session/prompt", response: Ok(Object {"stopReason": String("max_turn_requests")}) }
- This prevents the user from running conversations to completion when the model legitimately needs more than the adapter's local cap.

Current deepseek-acp-adapter findings:
- src/main.rs defines MAX_TURN_REQUESTS as 25.
- run_prompt_turn iterates for _ in 0..MAX_TURN_REQUESTS and sets StopReason::MaxTurnRequests if every iteration requested tools.
- The test prompt_tool_loop_stops_at_turn_cap currently locks in this behavior by expecting StopReason::MaxTurnRequests and exactly MAX_TURN_REQUESTS client requests.

Reference implementation checked locally:

title: Usage-only and Groq metadata frames lose otherwise valid completions
description:
Reality check 2026-10-07 at 37388ac0611632a5cd6215a5aae22ad1e59d8b2d (main, clean). Linux, Rust 1.97.1. The 507-test suite, fmt, Clippy, docs, release build and cargo audit passed; the evidence below came from source inspection and bounded offline runs of the shipped binary. No live provider calls or real credentials were used.

## Observed defect
The streamed-response parser assumes every chunk has a choice and only reads top-level usage. Two supported usage envelopes are therefore rejected or silently ignored at the same normalization boundary.

Reproduce through shipped serve --backend groq with a dummy key, model audit-model, temporary state and a localhost provider whose GET /models returns context_window=4096. After ACP initialize/session/new/prompt:
A. Send {"choices":[{"delta":{"content":"ok"},"finish_reason":"stop"}]}, followed by {"choices":[],"usage":{"prompt_tokens":3,"completion_tokens":4,"total_tokens":7}}, then [DONE].
Actual: the client first sees "ok", then prompt fails with -32603 and "chat completion chunk did not include any choices"; no usage_update.
B. Send {"choices":[{"delta":{"content":"ok"},"finish_reason":"stop"}],"x_groq":{"id":"fixture","usage":{"prompt_tokens":3,"completion_tokens":4,"total_tokens":7}}}, then [DONE].
Actual: end_turn succeeds, but neither response usage nor usage_update is emitted.
These were re-executed by the root session during tracker preparation.

## Root cause and prior coverage
src/llm/stream.rs:79-82 only models top-level usage. :154-158 rejects empty choices before considering whether the chunk carries valid usage.
Groq's official streamed-response schema documents x_groq.usage and optional top-level usage: https://github.com/groq/groq-python/blob/main/src/groq/types/chat/chat_completion_chunk.py (checked 2026-10-07).
Existing tests and tests/serve_model_discovery.rs place usage beside a nonempty choice. Closed daa-groq-backend-jbm5 recorded a successful live provider shape; this new bug does not invalidate that historical run, but covers additional documented envelopes.

## Contract and fix direction
Normalize documented provider usage envelopes into the existing UsageData/StreamEvent representation. Accept a usage-only chunk without inventing content or a finish reason. Keep a prior real finish event intact while accepting the final accounting frame. Extract Groq usage and preserve context discovery, cost, cache and reasoning-token behavior. Define precedence/deduplication when the same counters occur in both envelopes; reject consumed contradictory values rather than double-counting. Ignore unrelated optional metadata.
A missing choice with no meaningful allowed accounting payload remains malformed; accepting all empty objects is not the repair.

## Proof
Parser fixtures cover both exact payloads, top-level legacy shapes, null/absent usage, unknown metadata, duplicate/conflicting envelopes and truncated streams. Real serve/HTTP tests require end_turn plus correct prompt-response totals and usage_update for both shapes; use a known priced model in one fixture to verify cost reaches the client. Do not make a paid request or alter provider constants from memory. Negative checks must fail if metadata is ignored or the empty-choice guard is restored.

## Scope
Size M. Usage normalization at the existing provider boundary only. Numeric overflow and error presentation have separate owners and are independently implementable. No generalized multi-provider framework.

## Verification and handoff
Run the focused regression red before changing executable behavior, then the complete affected suite and repository gates in docs/agent-testing.md. Use temporary state directories and localhost fixtures with dummy credentials. Tests must assert the observed consumer behavior and identify the failing protocol stage without logging real payloads. Record the root-cause lesson here before closing. Implementation is deferred because this approved operation records the audit findings; nothing has been fixed or claimed.
notes: Related audit owners: daa-iqn7 covers invalid arithmetic; daa-8mrl covers provider-model request options. Closed daa-groq-backend-jbm5 remains the historical implementation record; this issue's explicit missing stream shapes are the new work.
close_reason: Documented usage envelopes produce correct prompt totals, context and cost without false stream failures

Plan checklist: [x] reproduce shipped failure; [x] inspect official Groq schema; [ ] normalize top-level/nested usage and reject contradictions; [ ] preserve empty/null/unknown/overflow checks; [ ] verify prompt totals, context discovery, one cumulative cost charge per completion; [ ] all gates plus repeated real serve runs; [ ] README and lesson. Accounting requires explicit input/output counts; identical required counters merge nonconflicting optional details, never sum envelopes.

comments.text:
Completed checklist: [x] real serve and parser red regressions; [x] top-level, usage-only and x_groq.usage normalization; [x] deduplicate required counters and merge nonconflicting optional details; [x] reject conflicting envelopes/cache aliases and malformed accounting, preserve overflow validation; [x] absent/null accounting and nullable optional detail handling; [x] no synthetic finish for truncated streams; [x] prompt-response totals, discovered context window and one cumulative cost increment per completion; [x] README updated; [x] all 563 tests, fmt, Clippy -D warnings, rustdoc -D warnings, release build, cargo audit, instruction-size and diff checks passed; [x] ten consecutive shipped usage-envelope fixture runs passed. No live providers used.

Lesson: completion events and final accounting are separate provider protocol stages. Normalize envelopes before the empty-choice guard; usage must neither invent a finish reason nor count twice. Optional null detail objects are valid in Groq’s published schema. Meaningful accounting requires explicit input/output token counts. The existing UsageData validation remains the arithmetic boundary; no provider prices changed.

title: Migrate agent-client-protocol and RMCP to next major versions
description:
Upgrade agent-client-protocol from 1.3.x to 2.x.

## Context
Renovate identified agent-client-protocol 2.0.0 as a major update. The upstream ACP migration guide confirms this is a source migration, not a routine dependency bump: https://github.com/agentclientprotocol/rust-sdk/blob/main/md/migration_v2.0.md
The repository uses agent-client-protocol = ^1.3.0 with the unstable feature, with ACP APIs extensively across src/ and tests. RMCP is used independently for MCP connections.

## Confirmed breakpoints
1. ConnectionTo::attach_session is removed in ACP 2.0. Current use: src/dev.rs:191. Replace with build_session, build_session_cwd, or build_session_from; rework dev smoke session startup and response/session routing.
2. AcpAgent::server() / into_server() are removed. Current uses: src/dev.rs:392 and src/dev.rs:541; builder: src/dev.rs:129-146. Replace MCP-schema process configuration with AcpAgentConfig; use config() / into_config(); update both dev-agent assertions.
3. ACP 2.0 changes the in-process Channel boundary to TransportFrame. Current channel construction: src/dev.rs:414, src/acp/tests.rs:846, 1400, 1459, 2102, 2203, 2274, and src/tools/execution/tests.rs:214. The code mostly uses Channel::duplex() without direct frame manipulation, but all transport tests must be recompiled and verified.
4. Session/requester APIs and ordering behavior change. Connection implementations are in src/acp/requesters.rs:65-184; handler registration and async response paths are in src/acp/mod.rs:169-268. Re-check ConnectionTo, send_request, block_task, cx.spawn, notifications, and response callbacks for compile errors, ordering changes, or deadlocks.
5. ACP MCP-over-ACP transport changed. Upstream 2.0 uses native McpServer::Acp/mcp/connect types and unstable_mcp_over_acp. The adapter deliberately rejects McpServer::Acp in src/mcp.rs:165-169; test: src/mcp/tests.rs:449-461. Preserve this out-of-scope behavior unless schema changes require edits. Do not accidentally enable ACP MCP-over-ACP.
6. Optional protocol-v2 schema 1.7 is separate. The guide says unstable_protocol_v2 tracks agent-client-protocol-schema 1.7. Do not treat that as a direct agent-client-protocol 1.7.0 release or enable it without a separate compatibility decision.

## Existing code likely unaffected
- src/main.rs:396 already constructs Lines with Lines::new(...).
- No current use was found of DynamicHandlerRegistration, ResponseRouter::id, Channel::copy, util::both, or process_stream_concurrently.
- Existing responder.respond_with_result calls are request-responder APIs, not the removed Dispatch::respond_with_error API.

## Acceptance
- Upgrade agent-client-protocol and coordinated derive/schema dependencies to 2.x.
- Resolve all compile errors without compatibility shims.
- Migrate attach_session and AcpAgent::server() usages.
- Re-run ACP, dev smoke, MCP, and tool execution tests.
- Verify stdio transport, session creation/resume, permissions, terminal requests, prompt streaming, notifications, and MCP server rejection behavior.
- Run cargo test -q, cargo fmt --all -- --check, cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings, and cargo doc --no-deps.
- Record upstream protocol behavior changes separately from pure Rust API changes.

## Not covered
- RMCP 3.x migration; track separately.
- Enabling ACP protocol v2 or native MCP-over-ACP.
- Resolving the existing unrelated logsink test failure.
close_reason: Upgraded agent-client-protocol 1.x -> 2.0.0 and RMCP 2.x -> 3.1.4; migrated ACP session/config APIs and RMCP CallToolResponse handlers. cargo check, fmt, clippy, docs, targeted ACP/MCP tests pass. Full suite retains only the pre-existing logsink redaction failure.

title: acp-proxy binary: byte-transparent passthrough, stderr capture, exit-code propagation
description:
## Goal
An `acp-proxy` binary that wraps an external ACP agent with byte-exact passthrough and correct exit status, replacing what `acp-debug.sh` does today.

## Scope
- In scope: a second `[[bin]]` target in this crate; spawning the wrapped agent; duplicating stdin and stdout byte-for-byte; capturing the child's stderr; propagating the child's exit code and signals; EOF ordering on shutdown; writing all captured traffic to the shared sink's connection-scoped file.
- Out of scope: parsing frames or discovering session ids. This task logs everything to one connection-scoped destination.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. Bytes forwarded to the child and back to the client are identical to what was received, including key order and whitespace.
2. Both directions are recorded — client-to-agent traffic is present, which the shell wrapper never captured.
3. When the wrapped agent exits non-zero, the proxy exits with the child's status.
4. When the client closes stdin, EOF reaches the child, remaining stdout is drained, and the proxy then exits.
5. `cargo build` produces two binaries from this crate.

## Testing
- Integration test against a scripted fake ACP agent child: assert byte-identical passthrough, non-zero exit propagation, and clean EOF shutdown.
- Assert client-to-agent frames appear in the log.

## Notes
- Copy the byte stream verbatim to the child and hand a second copy to any future parser. Never reconstruct frames from parsed JSON — number formatting and unknown-field drops would make attaching the debugger change the behaviour being debugged.
- The exit-code bug is the concrete reason this cannot stay in bash: `exec "$@" | tee` without `pipefail` reports `tee`'s status, so a crashed agent looks clean.
close_reason: Shipped as a second [[bin]] target, acp-proxy, with the logic in acp_llm_adapter::proxy so it is testable. Forwards bytes verbatim and splits a copy into lines for logging; captures client-to-agent traffic the shell wrapper never recorded; propagates the child's exit code (verified end to end: agent exit 17 -> proxy exit 17). Fake agent is a harnessless test target, matching the existing MCP stdio fixture pattern. 7 integration + 9 unit tests.

title: Logsink redaction tests inherit ACP_LOG_* from the ambient environment
description:
logsink::tests::structured_payloads_share_one_redaction_policy (src/logsink/tests.rs:117) reads the process environment instead of controlling it, so a developer who exports ACP_LOG_UNREDACTED=1 for local debugging sees a spurious failure:

    thread 'logsink::tests::structured_payloads_share_one_redaction_policy'
    panicked at src/logsink/tests.rs:117:5:
    assertion failed: !frame.payload.to_string().contains(secret)

## Evidence

    cargo test -q --no-fail-fast
    # test result: FAILED. 124 passed; 1 failed

    env -u ACP_LOG_UNREDACTED -u ACP_LOG_MAX_BYTES -u ACP_LOG_MAX_AGE_DAYS cargo test -q --no-fail-fast
    # test result: ok. 125 passed; 0 failed

The maintainer's shell exports ACP_LOG_UNREDACTED=1, ACP_LOG_MAX_BYTES=unlimited and ACP_LOG_MAX_AGE_DAYS=unlimited. CI does not, which is why this is green there and red locally.

## Why it matters

This is the worst shape of test defect: it makes the local baseline lie about a **security** property. An agent following the baseline-first procedure in docs/agent-testing.md sees a redaction test failing before it touches anything, records it as pre-existing, and moves on - exactly what happened while fixing daa-30py. If redaction genuinely regressed, that signal would be indistinguishable from this noise.

## Scope

ENV_UNREDACTED is src/logsink.rs:71; the opt-out arrived in 71fe063 and the test in 119a253. Audit the other ACP_LOG_* readers (retention bounds from 8ec536c) for the same ambient dependency - those currently pass, but only because 'unlimited' happens not to break their assertions.

## Acceptance

- The redaction test asserts redaction regardless of the ambient environment, and a separate test covers the ACP_LOG_UNREDACTED=1 opt-out explicitly.
- Full suite green with ACP_LOG_UNREDACTED=1 exported.
- No test reads an ACP_LOG_* variable it does not set itself.
close_reason: gate:src/logsink/tests.rs — structured_payloads_share_one_redaction_policy now pins the policy through LogRecord::new_with_redaction(.., true) instead of LogRecord::new, so the security assertion no longer depends on the ambient ACP_LOG_UNREDACTED. The seam already existed at src/logsink.rs:220; the test simply used the wrong entry point. Added new_applies_whichever_redaction_setting_the_environment_selects to pin the remaining wiring (new delegates to new_with_redaction with redaction_enabled()) in a form that holds under any ambient setting. Full suite is green with the maintainer's env exported as-is — 126/317/18/1/11, no env -u needed — and identical with ACP_LOG_* cleared; fmt, clippy --all-targets --all-features and cargo doc clean. Audit result for the rest of the acceptance: the retention tests all construct explicit RetentionPolicy values and use channel_with_policy, so ACP_LOG_MAX_BYTES and ACP_LOG_MAX_AGE_DAYS have no ambient path into any test; RetentionPolicy::from_env is reached only by LogSink::spawn, which no test exercises, so it is untested but not env-fragile. Honest limit, verified by mutation rather than asserted: replacing redaction_enabled() with a hardcoded true in LogRecord::new fails the new wiring test only on a machine that has opted out, and passes with the default setting, so that test is vacuous in CI and has teeth exactly where the environment hid the problem. Closes the third and last of the environment-dependent failures found while fixing daa-30py; the local baseline now matches CI.

title: edit_file string-replace tool (+ proptest)
description:
## Goal
Reliable targeted edits via exact string replacement.

## Scope
- In: edit_file(path, old_string, new_string): read via client fs, replace the unique exact occurrence, write via client fs; error clearly on no-match or non-unique match; result fed back to the model.
- Out: apply_patch/unified-diff format (explicitly out per plan).

## Acceptance Criteria
1. A unique old_string is replaced and written via client fs (native diff).
2. Absent or ambiguous (non-unique) old_string fails with a descriptive error; the file is unchanged.

## Testing
- proptest: apply-then-read-back invariants; unit tests for no-match and ambiguous-match.

## Notes
- Depends on the permission gate and read_file. String-replace, not patch (DeepSeek is weaker at patch syntax).
close_reason: Implemented in the current patchset and verified by tests/docs

title: Dependency audit retains unsound event-listener and yanked chacha20 warnings
description: Baseline cargo audit on 2026-09-07 exits 0 but reports event-listener 5.4.1 RUSTSEC-2026-0221 (!Send StackSlot tags crossing threads), reached through async-process/agent-client-protocol and blocking; chacha20 0.10.1 is yanked, reached through rand/rmcp/quinn/reqwest. Observed before changing the dependency graph for daa-eyj2. Deferred from that lifecycle fix: assess applicability and update the affected transitive chains, preserving current protocol tests. No finding concerns rustix 1.1.4.
close_reason: gate:cargo audit — now reports nothing at all, where it previously ended with "2 allowed warnings found". Both resolved by semver-compatible patch bumps in Cargo.lock, no manifest change and no source change: event-listener 5.4.1 to 5.4.2 and chacha20 0.10.1 to 0.10.2. Full suite 126/320/18/1/11 green, fmt, clippy --all-targets --all-features, cargo doc and cargo build --release all clean, so the protocol tests the issue asked to preserve are intact. Applicability, which the issue asked for rather than a blind bump: RUSTSEC-2026-0221 requires Event::with_tag with a !Send tag type and a StackSlot crossing threads. Neither with_tag nor StackSlot appears anywhere in the crates between us and event-listener - blocking 1.7.0, async-process 2.5.0, async-lock 3.4.2, async-channel 2.5.0 - and this crate never names event-listener itself, so the unsoundness was not reachable in this graph. It is fixed because the fix was free, not because it was exploitable here. chacha20 0.10.1 carried no vulnerability either; yanked means the author withdrew it, so the cost was resolution fragility rather than risk. Worth noting for whoever reads this next: cargo audit exits 0 for the warning classes, unsound and yanked, so neither finding could ever have failed CI. That is why they sat long enough to need an issue. Raised with the maintainer as a separate decision rather than changed here, since --deny warnings turns any future upstream yank into a red build at an arbitrary moment.
