title: Permission requests for file edits carry an ACP diff preview
description:
Send an ACP `diff` content entry with the file-edit permission request, so
editors can show an accurate preview before approval, not only after the edit.

Today the permission request for edit_file/write_file carries only `rawInput`
(the tool arguments verbatim: `{path, old_text, new_text}` or
`{path, content}`; src/acp/requesters.rs RequestPermissionRequest::new with
`.raw_input(tool_raw_input(call))`). The full-file `Diff` (path, oldText =
original, newText = updated) is only emitted after execution
(src/acp/turn_events.rs:158 from ToolExecution.edit). Each client must guess
the preview from rawInput; LouiseLM guesses wrong (louiselm-hht64: shows
new_text as the whole file). ACP v1 tool calls allow `content` with
`{"type":"diff","path","oldText","newText"}` on the request's ToolCallUpdate
(https://agentclientprotocol.com/protocol/v1/tool-calls#content,
#requesting-permission).

Design points:
- Compute the preview from the same confined read the edit uses (edit_file
  already rereads after approval and fails on change; the preview must not
  weaken that check or become a second, unconfined read).
- edit_file: oldText = current file, newText = replacen(old_text, new_text, 1);
  only when old_text matches exactly once (otherwise the call fails anyway).
  write_file: oldText = current content or absent for a new file.
- Size: bound previews (large files) and decide fallback (omit diff) explicitly.
- Logging: diff text is content; the existing redaction policy must cover it.
- Plan mode / remembered decisions: no change to gating.

Acceptance: ACP handler test asserts the permission request carries a diff
entry with full old/new text for edit_file and write_file (new and existing
file); Zed and LouiseLM previews show the real change (manual check).

Refs claude/b9707559-6fe1-42c2-94af-e24e2b00aec8

title: Upgrade agent-client-protocol from 0.14.0 to 1.2.0
description:
## Problem

`agent-client-protocol` is exact-pinned to `0.14.0` in Cargo.toml (`= "0.14.0"`,
`features = ["unstable"]`), while `1.2.0` is available on crates.io. This is a
major version jump on the crate this entire adapter is built against (schema
types, session config options, jsonrpc transport, unstable feature flags like
`unstable_boolean_config`).

Every dependency in this project is exact-pinned by design, so this won't
happen via `cargo update` - it requires a deliberate version bump + full
regression pass.

## Solution

1. Read the agent-client-protocol changelog/release notes between 0.14.0 and
   1.2.0 for breaking changes (schema types, feature flag renames/removals,
   trait signature changes).
2. Bump the version pin in Cargo.toml and run `cargo build` to find compile
   breaks.
3. Check whether the `unstable` feature bundle (unstable_auth_methods,
   unstable_boolean_config, unstable_elicitation,
   unstable_end_turn_token_usage, unstable_mcp_over_acp,
   unstable_session_fork) still exists in the same shape, since
   SessionConfigOption's select/boolean kinds and other adapter code depend
   on it directly.
4. Re-verify the session config option handling added for reasoning_effort
   and max_tokens (src/session.rs, src/acp/mod.rs) still compiles and behaves
   the same - these depend directly on SessionConfigOption::select,
   SessionConfigSelectOption, and SessionConfigValueId APIs.
5. Full test suite must pass with no regressions (cargo test, cargo fmt,
   cargo clippy per AGENTS.md).

## Out of Scope

- Bumping other exact-pinned dependencies (clap, reqwest, uuid, thiserror,
  etc.) - those are routine patch/minor bumps, not covered by this task.
close_reason: Upgraded agent-client-protocol to 1.2.0 and verified tests, clippy, and docs

title: session/new + streaming text prompt turn
description:
## Goal
A text-only prompt turn: session/prompt streams DeepSeek output to the editor.

## Scope
- In: session/new (in-memory session: history, cwd, mode); session/prompt → call DeepSeek (stream) → forward text as agent_message_chunk, reasoning as agent_thought_chunk; append to history; return StopReason end_turn/max_tokens.
- Out: tools, permissions, cancellation (next task).

## Acceptance Criteria
1. session/new returns a session id and advertised modes.
2. A prompt streams agent_message_chunk updates; reasoning maps to thought chunks; turn returns end_turn (or max_tokens).
3. Conversation history is retained per session and replayed on the next prompt.

## Testing
- Mock LlmClient + fake ACP client; assert update sequence, StopReason, and history replay.

## Notes
- Depends on initialize + DeepSeek client.
close_reason: Implemented in-memory ACP sessions, streamed DeepSeek prompt turns, and history replay tests.

title: Expose ACP session options for model effort and thought level
description:
In Neovim, `acp_session_options` exposes controls for model/session settings such as model effort and thought level. Those controls work with Codex ACP, but the `deepseek_acp_adapter` session only exposes permission modes, so the user cannot change model effort, thought level, or related model/session options from the ACP client.

Observed behavior:
- Typing `acp_session_options` in Neovim shows the adapter does not provide controls for effort/thought-level/model settings.
- The adapter can stream DeepSeek reasoning content, but there is no ACP session configuration surface for choosing reasoning behavior.

Expected behavior:
- The adapter should advertise and handle ACP session config/model options that Neovim can render in `acp_session_options`.
- At minimum, expose model-related options that map cleanly to DeepSeek request parameters, such as reasoning/thinking effort or thought level if supported by the selected model/API.
- Setting an option from the client should update the session state used for later prompts and return updated config options when the ACP protocol expects it.

Reference implementation checked locally:
- `/home/lotso/code/codex-acp/src/codex_agent.rs`
  - registers handlers for `SetSessionModelRequest` and `SetSessionConfigOptionRequest` in addition to `SetSessionModeRequest`.
  - `new_session` and `load_session` return `.models(load.models)` and `.config_options(load.config_options)`.
  - `set_session_config_option` calls `thread.set_config_option(...)` and returns `SetSessionConfigOptionResponse::new(config_options)`.
- `/home/lotso/code/codex-acp/src/thread.rs`
  - builds `SessionConfigOption::select("model", ...)` with category `Model`.
  - builds `SessionConfigOption::select("reasoning_effort", ...)` with category `ThoughtLevel` when the current model preset supports multiple efforts.
  - handles config ids `mode`, `model`, and `reasoning_effort`.
  - also exposes `SessionModelState` with model IDs encoded as `model/effort` and handles `SetSessionModelRequest`.

Current adapter findings:
- `src/main.rs` registers `InitializeRequest`, `AuthenticateRequest`, `NewSessionRequest`, `SetSessionModeRequest`, `PromptRequest`, and cancel handling, but no `SetSessionModelRequest` or `SetSessionConfigOptionRequest` handlers.
- `handle_new_session_request` returns `NewSessionResponse::new(session_id).modes(default_session_modes())` only.
- `build_initialize_response` advertises prompt/auth/load-session capabilities only; there is no model/config option path.

Acceptance criteria:
- `acp_session_options` in Neovim shows relevant model/session settings for this adapter.
- The adapter accepts ACP requests to change those settings and applies them to subsequent DeepSeek chat/completions requests.
- Unsupported options are rejected with clear `invalid_params` errors rather than silently ignored.
- Add tests covering advertised options, option updates, and prompt behavior using the updated session settings.
close_reason: Implemented ACP session config options for model and reasoning effort, wired updates into DeepSeek requests, and added regression tests

title: Report accurate context window for DeepSeek models
description:
## Context

DeepSeek does not send `context_length`/`context_window` in its usage payload.
The adapter handles that by logging
`API chunk did not include context_length/context_window in usage` and then
filling `context_length = 0` from `get_context_length_for_model()` in
`src/turn.rs`.

That function returns `1_000_000` for every unknown model, including
`deepseek-v4-pro` and `deepseek-v4-flash`, which are the adapter's defaults.

## Evidence

Every `usage_update` on the ACP wire reports the same synthetic window:

```json
{"sessionUpdate":"usage_update","used":86898,"size":1000000}
```

61/61 notifications in the latest deepseek stdout log use `size=1000000`. The
context percentage shown by clients (e.g. `83677/1000000`) is therefore
misleading.

## Proposed

Give `deepseek-v4-pro` and `deepseek-v4-flash` their real context window sizes
instead of the 1M fallback, and make the fallback explicit about being unknown
rather than silently asserting 1M. If the model list is dynamic, the override
should live next to the model table rather than as a hardcoded match arm.
close_reason: Added explicit model context-window table (llm/models.rs): deepseek-v4-pro/flash/vision 1M, deepseek-chat 4096, glm-4.6 128K. Unknown models now return None and skip the usage_update with a warning instead of silently asserting 1M. Also stopped logging raw SSE payload at debug in stream.rs. Added unit tests for table and turn behavior. cargo test (73/312/1/11 + doctests), fmt, clippy, doc all pass.

title: No serve-level coverage that tool-call status updates reach the client
description:
The mock backend can now emit a run_command tool call (daa-wu5e), so the serve-level path an editor drives is reachable from a test for the first time. tests/serve_shutdown.rs uses that to cover disconnect, and deliberately covers nothing else.

What the editor sees during a tool call is still unverified end to end. The adapter sends session/update notifications carrying tool-call status as the call moves through pending, in progress and completed, plus the tool's output and kind. Unit tests construct those updates; nothing asserts that a real serve process emits them, in the right order, with the right content, over real ACP.

This matters because the notifications are the entire UI. An editor showing a stuck spinner, no command output, or a tool call that never resolves is indistinguishable, from the adapter's own unit tests, from one that works.

## Scope

- Drive a run_command tool call through a real serve process, as tests/serve_shutdown.rs does.
- Collect the session/update notifications for the turn.
- Assert the status sequence reaches a terminal state, that the tool kind and title are what the editor needs to render, and that the command's output actually arrives.
- Assert a failing command reports failure rather than silently completing.

## Note

Keep the assertions about the contract an editor depends on, not the exact notification count - the adapter is free to add updates, and a test that pins the count will fail on every unrelated improvement.
close_reason: gate:tests/serve_tool_calls.rs — a_tool_call_and_its_output_reach_the_client asserts the client is shown a tool_call carrying kind execute and a usable title, then a tool_call_update resolving that same toolCallId with status completed and the command stdout; a_failing_command_is_reported_as_failed covers a non-zero exit arriving as failed rather than quietly completed. Selected by sessionUpdate kind rather than by position, as the issue asked, so the adapter stays free to add unrelated updates without breaking these. The behaviour was already correct, so no src change; what did not exist was any evidence it reaches a real client. Factored the ACP client into tests/acp_client/mod.rs, shared with serve_shutdown.rs, which got smaller as a result: it spawns serve, handshakes, grants permissions inside the pump and records session/update notifications so tests assert on what an editor would render. Stress-run 20 times; full suite green with clippy clean - clippy caught an assigning_clones in the new harness that cargo test did not, which would have failed CI. Follow-up filed: daa-reep for the missing in_progress update.

title: Restore the protocol translation boundary around the agent core
description:
Reality check 2026-10-07 at 37388ac0611632a5cd6215a5aae22ad1e59d8b2d (main, clean). Linux, Rust 1.97.1. The 507-test suite, fmt, Clippy, docs, release build and cargo audit passed; the evidence below came from source inspection and bounded offline runs of the shipped binary. No live provider calls or real credentials were used.

## Goal
Session policy, turn decisions and the core tool interface can be exercised through adapter-owned values without importing ACP wire schema or constructing an ACP client. Wire translation remains at the ACP/tool I/O edges, as promised by AGENTS.md and README.md:275-279.

## Current evidence
Production src/turn.rs:10-15 and :296-304 consumes ACP prompt requests/notification types directly. src/session.rs:17 imports ACP mode/config/session types into mutable session state and policies. src/tools/registry.rs:7 and :23-28 embeds ACP SessionId and kind/status types in the tool core interface. The LlmClient seam exists, but the intended left-side boundary is incomplete.
Related closed architecture epics daa-e7a and daa-arch-decomp-6ly are history, not evidence that this remaining coupling disappeared.

## Bounded implementation plan
Start from passing characterization coverage. Move one responsibility at a time, compiling and testing each slice:
1. Use minimal adapter-owned session identity, tool permission/category and mode/config values for core policy/state; put ACP option builders and conversions at the existing edge.
2. Separate prompt admission/turn orchestration inputs and events from ACP request/notification construction. Reuse existing LlmClient, tool registry and session-store boundaries; plain functions and narrow value types suffice.
3. Move concrete ACP filesystem/terminal/permission request construction into edge execution/requester code while preserving domain tool results and explicit resource ownership.
Trace every public entry point after each move. Keep async cancellation, locking, process ownership, history persistence and error presentation intact.

## Acceptance and proof
- Core production state/policy, turn orchestration and tool interface no longer depend on ACP schema, raw HTTP/SSE objects or concrete editor connections. Actual edge code still may.
- At least one full prompt/tool/history/cancellation domain test is expressed using adapter-owned inputs/events and the existing fake LlmClient/registry, with no ACP setup.
- Characterization tests through shipped serve preserve JSON-RPC frames, permission ordering/denial, cancellation, selected-content bounds, persistence/replay, usage and client fs/terminal behavior.
- Review remaining imports and dependency directions; moving ACP imports into a differently named core file is not success.
- Focused and full project gates stay green at each stable slice; public docs reflect the resulting boundary.

## Scope and risk
Size L; the three cohesive slices belong to this one outstanding contract and should be implemented incrementally. Existing edge files may gain extracted conversion functions; avoid a broad folder rewrite, framework, generic event bus or speculative extension point. No intended wire or user-visible behavior change. This debt must not be used as a prerequisite for the independent safety fixes; priority controls sequencing without fake dependencies.

## Verification and handoff
Run the focused regression red before changing executable behavior, then the complete affected suite and repository gates in docs/agent-testing.md. Use temporary state directories and localhost fixtures with dummy credentials. Tests must assert the observed consumer behavior and identify the failing protocol stage without logging real payloads. Record the root-cause lesson here before closing. Implementation is deferred because this approved operation records the audit findings; nothing has been fixed or claimed.
notes: Audit repair owners for characterization coverage: daa-deo (MCP authorization), daa-kxx7 (redaction), daa-alau (HTTP replay policy), daa-iqn7 (usage arithmetic), daa-2jci (presentation), daa-n6lq (usage envelopes), daa-8mrl (effort choices), daa-u8tu (tool cardinality). Priority, not graph blockers, keeps this structural debt behind urgent behavior repair.
close_reason: Protocol translation boundary restored; 587 tests, all required gates and isolated release mock smoke pass. Evidence and lesson recorded in issue comments.

comments.author: 01a11a2d-1cf2-7620-abe6-ce12e14e76fd
comments.text: 2026-10-08 independent source audit confirmed the current core/wire coupling. Also preserve runtime ownership during extraction: local file reads/writes/search run synchronously in async dispatch (tools/execution/mod.rs and tools/registry.rs), and session save_history performs filesystem persistence from the turn. The edge extraction must put blocking filesystem work behind an explicit bounded async/blocking boundary; moving ACP imports alone does not satisfy AGENTS runtime/no-I/O contract. Existing executable behavior and cancellation characterization remain required. No claim or code changes for this task yet; ordered after safety and request-contract repairs.

comments.author: 01a11a2d-1cf2-7620-abe6-ce12e14e76fd
comments.text:
2026-10-08 handoff after the independent behavior repairs. This architectural task remains OPEN and UNCLAIMED; no structural refactor is being represented as complete. New baseline: 573 passing tests plus fmt, all-target/all-feature Clippy -D warnings, rustdoc -D warnings, release, audit and instruction-size checks. Real serve characterization now covers ordinary/mode-specific instructions, provider reasoning roundtrips across tools and restore, reasoning config fidelity, alternate usage envelopes/cost, approval cancellation, bounded terminal cleanup/late creation, and /clear memory/disk/reset semantics.

Granular next slices: [ ] Extract adapter-owned session identity, capability flags and tool categories plus pure mode/permission policies; move ACP mode/config/permission builders to the existing ACP edge. [ ] Translate prompt inputs and response/notification events at that edge; keep LlmClient/model history and cancellation decisions in the core. [ ] Remove ACP requester signatures from the core registry seam without introducing a generic event bus; preserve the terminal/create acceptance handshake and connection-owned late cleanup. [ ] Keep persistence and local filesystem work off async executor threads, preserving atomic history reset and session admission/removal ordering. [ ] Add a full domain-only prompt/tool/history/cancel test. [ ] Rerun the existing real-serve characterization and every project gate after stable slices; inspect dependency directions, not just imports. [ ] Update README and record the root-cause lesson before closure.

The file/shell contract question daa-eja6 is still awaiting the maintainer; do not decide confinement by refactoring. daa-deo and daa-2jci retain their owners, so coordinate changes that would overlap their live permission/presentation work. These are handoff constraints, not fabricated new graph dependencies. This larger change was not folded into the completed behavior-fix batch.

comments.author: 01a11ade-38c4-7892-8886-a9990c95866c
comments.text: Claimed protocol-boundary refactor. Scope: session/turn core values and orchestration, ACP conversions/requesters, tool registry/execution boundary, blocking persistence/file dispatch, domain characterization and README. Will preserve active MCP authorization and presentation behavior; no changes to provider arithmetic or logsink policy. Starting from clean worktree and running existing suite before edits.

comments.author: 01a11ade-38c4-7892-8886-a9990c95866c
comments.text:
Implemented the three boundary slices with adapter-owned values and existing extension seams. SessionRecord/policy, PromptInput/TurnEvent/PromptResult/StopReason, and the ToolRegistry/ToolExecutor interface have no production ACP schema, raw HTTP/SSE or concrete editor dependencies. ACP prompt/options/events and editor permission/filesystem/terminal request translation live at the existing ACP and tool execution edges. SessionStore explicitly owns reconnect configuration and MCP handles separately from core session records; blocking persistence and served load/list/delete work use the existing blocking boundary. Wire frames and persisted JSON shapes are unchanged.

Added domain_turn_pairs_tool_history_and_cancels_remaining_calls using only adapter-owned input/events and fake LlmClient/registry: a complete tool-feedback turn, then mid-batch cancellation, undispatched remaining tool results paired in history, and turn-admission release. Existing shipped-serve, permission, denial, confinement, selected-content, replay, usage and child ownership characterization coverage remains passing. Stop-reason tests now target the actual production core mapping; domain success checks plus real edge update tests preserve tool status coverage. README documents the new boundary. Independent MCP authorization, error presentation and logsink policies were not changed.

Verification: clean passing baseline of 586 tests before this pure refactor, so no artificial failing behavior test was introduced. Final LLM_API_KEY=skip-ci-no-key cargo test -q --all-features passes 587 tests including integration tests and doctests. cargo fmt --all -- --check, cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings, RUSTDOCFLAGS='-D warnings' cargo doc --no-deps --all-features, cargo build --release -q, cargo audit -q, ./scripts/check-agent-instructions and git diff --check all pass. Release dev --backend mock smoke returns EndTurn and the expected response with isolated temporary state; no live provider or real credentials were used. Final production-import review confirms the boundary and removes the domain type modules' circular dependency.

Lesson: a file/module extraction is not a protocol boundary if signatures still carry wire DTOs or concrete connections, or core state still owns external resources. Use minimal owned values for policy and orchestration, perform translation at the existing edges, and keep handles under an explicit I/O owner. Pair a domain lifecycle test with existing real-edge characterization so architectural independence does not trade away behavior and safety evidence. This lesson is issue-local; no additional standing rule or design question is warranted.

title: Deferred: ACP elicitation support
description:
## Problem Statement

ACP elicitation lets an agent ask the client to collect structured user input during a turn. Claude ACP needs this because Claude SDK and MCP tools can ask user questions, but the DeepSeek adapter currently has no upstream AskUserQuestion surface and no MCP elicitation bridge. The team chose to defer this during the ACP parity grill-me session.

## Solution

Keep ACP elicitation as a future feature. Revisit when the adapter intentionally adds a model-visible `ask_user` tool, enables MCP elicitation in `rmcp`, or a target client workflow requires structured user input beyond permission prompts.

## User Stories

1. As an agent, I want to ask the user for missing structured information, so that I can continue a turn without guessing.
2. As an MCP server user, I want MCP elicitation requests to flow through the ACP client, so that external tools can collect required input.
3. As a maintainer, I want elicitation separated from permission prompts, so that approval and information-gathering flows do not get conflated.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Given a future elicitation implementation, when the client advertises form or URL elicitation capabilities, then the adapter can forward supported requests and handle accept/decline/cancel outcomes.
2. Given a client without elicitation capabilities, when a tool needs elicitation, then the adapter fails clearly or suppresses the tool path rather than hanging.
3. Given permission requests, when elicitation is added, then permission behavior remains unchanged.

## Implementation Notes

- Deferred by product decision.
- Do not add an `ask_user` tool unless the model contract and UX are intentionally designed.
- If MCP elicitation is pursued, check `rmcp` feature flags and bridge ACP client capabilities into MCP client initialization.

## Testing Notes

- Add form and URL elicitation tests when implemented.
- Include cancel/decline paths and no-capability fallback tests.

## Out of Scope

- Near-term ACP parity slice.
- Permission prompt behavior changes.
close_reason: Out of scope for the current parity slice: ACP elicitation remains intentionally deferred until an explicit ask_user or MCP elicitation bridge is designed

title: README rework: concise landing page with tested LouiseLM/Zed/CodeCompanion setup
description:

title: No in_progress update while a long command runs, so the editor shows it as pending
description:
Observed while writing the serve-level tests (daa-r2mv). The adapter announces a tool call and then sends nothing until it finishes:

    tool_call        toolCallId=mock-tool-call-0 title="echo hello" kind=execute
    tool_call_update toolCallId=mock-tool-call-0 status=completed ...

There is no update carrying status "in_progress" in between. ACP's ToolCallStatus has Pending, InProgress, Completed and Failed; a tool_call with no status is Pending by default, so an editor renders a 300-second command as pending for its entire run and only ever sees it move once, at the end.

This is not a protocol violation and not a bug in the sense of anything being wrong with the result. It is a UX gap: "queued" and "running" look identical to the user, and a slow command is indistinguishable from a stuck one.

## Scope

- Emit a tool_call_update with status in_progress once the command has actually been spawned, not when the call is announced - the distinction is only useful if it means the work started.
- Decide whether the same applies to the other tools. read_file and write_file complete fast enough that an intermediate update is probably noise; run_command is the one that can run for minutes.
- Extend the serve-level assertions in tests/serve_tool_calls.rs to cover the sequence rather than just the terminal state.

## Why it was not done with daa-r2mv

That issue was about whether the notifications reach the client at all, which they do. Adding a new update to the sequence is a behaviour change with a UX decision attached, not test coverage, so it is tracked separately rather than smuggled into a test commit.
close_reason: gate:tests/serve_tool_calls.rs — a_running_command_is_reported_in_progress_before_it_finishes asserts the client sees exactly [in_progress, completed] and, separately, that in_progress arrives AFTER session/request_permission. Implemented as option B after the maintainer chose it: a ToolProgressReporter capability on the connection, added to the ToolCallRequester composite and threaded into run_command, fired where work actually starts - after the permission round-trip and the spawn in the in-process branch, after terminal/create in the terminal branch. The cheap alternative was rejected on evidence, not taste: reporting from the turn loop would fire before the permission gate, since gating happens inside execution, and the mutation proving it fails with "in_progress arrived before the permission prompt, so it reported work that had not started". The ordering assertion exists precisely because presence alone would pass under either placement. Answers the "which tools" question by construction - fast synchronous tools simply never report, so no notification noise. Full suite 126/323/18/2/4/11 green, fmt, clippy --all-targets --all-features and cargo doc clean; tool-call suite stress-run 20 times. Two older assertions in that file pinned "exactly one tool_call_update" and had to be relaxed to the terminal update - my own issue text warned against pinning the count and I wrote it that way anyway; they now take the last update so the adapter stays free to add progress. README updated, since this is behaviour a user sees.

title: DeepSeek 400 after /resume: size filter emits structurally invalid messages
description:
After a /resume of a large session, session/prompt fails with DeepSeek 400 Bad Request.

Root cause (evidence from 20260716-062059 logs + captured request body):
- The request SENT to DeepSeek was only 264KB / 141 msgs - well under CloudFront's ~1MB limit. So the 400 is NOT a size-limit problem.
- filter_messages_by_size (src/turn.rs) shrinks history by walking tool-call groups newest->oldest and skipping oversized groups (the multi-MB grep/read_file results). It is role- and position-blind, so it drops big assistant+tool groups while cherry-picking tiny scattered user messages.
- This punches holes in the conversation, producing two structurally invalid shapes that DeepSeek rejects:
  1. 8 consecutive 'user' messages at the head (the filter created these; raw history alternates correctly).
  2. An empty assistant message serialized as {"role":"assistant"} (no content, no tool_calls) - carried through from history.

Fix: sanitize the filtered message list before sending - drop empty assistant messages and coalesce consecutive same-role user/assistant text messages (leave tool messages and assistant-with-tool_calls untouched). This guarantees a valid alternating conversation regardless of how history was filtered.

Related follow-up (separate): byte-cap grep/read_file tool output like bash already is (COMMAND_OUTPUT_LIMIT), so history never accumulates multi-MB tool results. codex-acp/claude-agent-acp cap output and never hit this.
close_reason: Fixed: added sanitize_conversation() in src/turn.rs, applied after size filtering in stream_model_turn. Drops empty assistant messages and coalesces consecutive same-role user/assistant text messages (tool messages and assistant-with-tool-calls untouched, so pairing stays intact). Verified against the captured 400 request (141->132 msgs, 0 consecutive-role runs, 0 empty assistants, 0 orphaned tools). 4 new tests in src/turn/tests.rs; fmt+clippy+298 tests green.

title: Collapse 5 individual terminal requester traits into TerminalRequester
description:
## Source

Ponytail-audit finding #1 (yagni).

## Problem

`src/acp/requesters.rs` defines five single-method terminal requester traits plus a composite `TerminalRequester` supertrait:
- `CreateTerminalRequester` (create_terminal)
- `TerminalOutputRequester` (terminal_output)
- `WaitForTerminalExitRequester` (wait_for_terminal_exit)
- `ReleaseTerminalRequester` (release_terminal)
- `KillTerminalRequester` (kill_terminal)

None of the individual traits is ever used as a bound — only `TerminalRequester` appears in function signatures and test fakes. Each has exactly one production impl (`ConnectionTo<Client>`).

## What to do

1. Delete the 5 individual trait definitions.
2. Add their 5 methods directly to `TerminalRequester`.
3. Update the single `ConnectionTo<Client>` impl to implement `TerminalRequester` directly (one impl block instead of 5).
4. Update the test fakes in `src/test_utils.rs` that implement the individual traits to implement `TerminalRequester` instead.
5. Run full test/fmt/clippy procedure.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The 5 individual traits no longer exist.
- `TerminalRequester` has 5 methods.
- All existing tests pass identically.
- No behavior change.

## Estimated impact

~65 lines removed.
close_reason: Collapsed 5 individual terminal requester traits (CreateTerminalRequester, TerminalOutputRequester, WaitForTerminalExitRequester, ReleaseTerminalRequester, KillTerminalRequester) into TerminalRequester trait with all 5 methods directly. Updated all impl blocks: ConnectionTo<Client>, FakeTerminalRequester, CancelTracker, TransitionRequester, RecordingToolCallRequester. All tests pass (384 total), formatting and clippy clean. Net -76 lines.

title: Dependabot rejects Cargo versioning strategy
description:
Dependabot rejects the repository configuration and cannot activate Cargo updates because Cargo does not accept versioning-strategy: increase.

## Observed
GitHub check .github/dependabot.yml failed on PR #65 commit d790e2678ad4355c6dfa0e1143476daba7965d5a. Check-run id 113372757796, retrieved via gh api repos/euri10/acp-llm-adapter/commits/d790e2678ad4355c6dfa0e1143476daba7965d5a/check-runs.
Exact hosted error:
The property '#/updates/0/versioning-strategy' value "increase" did not match one of the following values: lockfile-only, auto

## Root cause
.github/dependabot.yml sets increase for the Cargo ecosystem. The earlier migration daa-fufg validated a generic schema but not hosted ecosystem-specific restrictions. Rust CI does not validate Dependabot configuration, so its green checks did not establish activation.

## Fix direction
Remove the unsupported override and use Dependabot's default auto strategy. Preserve daily Cargo/GitHub Actions checks, dependencies labels, manual review, and Renovate enabled:false. Do not replace this with custom automation.
Official reference: https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/reference/supply-chain-security/dependabot-options-reference#versioning-strategy . Its generic value list explicitly cautions that individual ecosystems may not support every strategy; the hosted check supplies the Cargo-specific allowed values.

## Acceptance
- The corrected commit passes GitHub's .github/dependabot.yml configuration check.
- Daily Cargo and GitHub Actions entries remain configured; Renovate remains disabled.
- Diff and instruction checks pass, and the final combined PR passes the normal CI gates.
- Record the hosted check result and the lesson that a generic schema does not prove ecosystem-specific acceptance.

## Scope
Configuration and its existing documentation only, plus this issue record. Discovered while integrating the authorized Tokio update after the earlier dependency PRs. No artificial Rust red test is needed for this mechanical configuration correction; the hosted rejection is the failing validation.
close_reason: Removed unsupported Cargo versioning-strategy increase; GitHub hosted config check 113374361660 passes, both corrected-head full CI runs pass, and PR #65 is merged. Daily Cargo/Actions schedules, labels, manual review and disabled Renovate remain configured. Lesson retained in issue comment and Rust policy.

title: Stalled model discovery prevents ACP startup and EOF cleanup
description:
Optional model-list discovery can block the whole adapter before it begins serving ACP or observing client disconnect.

## Observed and reproduction
Reality check 2026-10-08 at 96f55d7322d41484e5c7a7c029770cbcbab7d29f on main (clean), Linux, Rust 1.97.1. Actor/session: 01a11b68-765b-7aa3-afe2-05845b03b78e. All 592 tests, fmt, Clippy, rustdoc, release build, cargo audit and instruction-size check passed for the audited tree; these additional probes nevertheless reproduced the failures. Reproductions used the built target/debug/acp-llm-adapter, synthetic inputs and isolated temporary state; no live provider credentials or paid requests.
Start a localhost HTTP listener that accepts GET /models and leaves the connection open without replying. Run serve --backend groq with LLM_BASE_URL pointing to that listener, a dummy LLM_API_KEY/model and temporary state. Send an ACP initialize request. Actual: no response after two seconds. Close stdin; the process remains alive after another two seconds. The probe was then killed and reaped. These bounded observations plus the source below establish the missing application deadline; the audit did not wait indefinitely.
Expected: bounded discovery falls back to the configured default model and startup remains responsive to disconnect/shutdown.

## Root cause and missed coverage
src/llm/client.rs:99-113 constructs HttpClient::new and awaits send and JSON body without connect/read/overall deadline. src/main.rs:495-506 awaits the fetch before constructing the transport, EOF cancellation and shutdown select (:508-532). A pending response is neither a returned transport error nor parse error, so fallback is never reached.
The existing real-serve discovery test supplies a complete response. Related closed daa-e4w promises default-model fallback on failure, daa-4v0 wires startup discovery, and daa-base-url-desync-sx0r fixes endpoint selection; none covers a response that never finishes.

## Fix direction
Bound the entire optional discovery operation, including response headers AND body, and retain the default catalogue on timeout. Ensure startup's network wait participates in disconnect/shutdown ownership. Use the existing runtime/client boundaries, without background-refresh infrastructure or repeated per-turn discovery.

## Acceptance and tests
- Shipped serve tests separately stall response headers and a partially supplied body; within a documented bounded deadline initialize completes with the configured default model and a prompt can proceed.
- Closing editor stdin or terminating the adapter during either stall exits/reaps promptly and releases the pending HTTP request.
- Successful discovery still populates model IDs/context windows, and configured/unset base URL/model paths retain their behavior.
- Unit/focused tests exercise timeout-to-fallback without live networks. Timing assertions use generous bounds around a documented deadline, not millisecond equality.
Negative check: assert an actual initialize result/default model and process termination, not just that a timeout helper exists.

## Scope, ordering and handoff
Size M. src/llm/client.rs, src/main.rs and tests/serve_model_discovery.rs or focused startup lifecycle coverage. No prerequisite. Share coordination for client.rs with SSE integrity work; no artificial blocker. No live provider calls or new dependency.
Implementation is deferred because the maintainer approved recording the audit delta, not code changes. Leave open and unclaimed. Start with a failing regression, then make the narrow fix and run focused plus complete gates from docs/agent-testing.md. Stress lifecycle/time/filesystem regressions. Record the lesson and exact consumer/gate evidence before closure; obtain maintainer confirmation of the exact reproduction as required by the repository's live-defect acceptance policy. Live third-party editors/providers and Rust 1.95 were not verified by this audit.

title: Populate ACP _meta field with session history JSONL path
description:
## Goal

Populate the `_meta` field (ACP protocol extensibility, see https://agentclientprotocol.com/protocol/v1/extensibility#the-_meta-field) on session-related ACP responses with the absolute path of the session history JSONL file. This enables client-side tools (e.g., Neovim/CodeCompanion) to locate and read the chat history file for each session.

## What needs to change

The `_meta` field (`Meta = serde_json::Map<String, serde_json::Value>`) is available on several ACP response types via builder methods:
- `NewSessionResponse.meta(...)` — created in `insert_session_record()` (src/acp/mod.rs)
- `LoadSessionResponse.meta(...)` — created in `handle_load_session_request()` (src/acp/mod.rs)
- `ResumeSessionResponse.meta(...)` — created in `handle_resume_session_request()` (src/acp/mod.rs)
- `SessionInfo.meta(...)` — created in `SessionStore::list_sessions()` (src/session.rs) and `FilesystemSessionStore::list_persisted()` (src/session_store.rs)

For each, add a `_meta` map with a key like `"historyJsonlPath"` containing the absolute path to `<state_dir>/sessions/<session_id>/history.jsonl`.

The history file path can be derived from the `FilesystemSessionStore` state directory (which is the `state_dir` field) combined with `sessions/<session_id>/history.jsonl`.

## Scope

- **In scope:** Add `_meta` with history JSONL path to NewSessionResponse, LoadSessionResponse, ResumeSessionResponse, and SessionInfo (for list/resume/load)
- **In scope:** The `_meta` key should follow camelCase convention: `"historyJsonlPath"`
- **In scope:** Only set `_meta` when persistence is available (when `FilesystemSessionStore` exists)
- **In scope:** Tests that verify `_meta` is populated correctly
- **Out of scope:** Adding `_meta` to other response types (InitializeResponse, SetSessionModeResponse, etc.)
- **Out of scope:** Backward-compatibility shims

## Implementation hints

1. `FilesystemSessionStore` has a method `session_dir(session_id)` that returns `<state_dir>/sessions/<session_id>`. The history file path is that directory joined with `"history.jsonl"`.
2. To access the `FilesystemSessionStore` from response builders, you may need to:
   - Store the state dir path in the `SessionStore` (it already has `persistence: Option<FilesystemSessionStore>`)
   - Add a helper method on `FilesystemSessionStore` or `SessionStore` to compute the history JSONL path for a given session_id
3. In `list_sessions()`, each `SessionInfo` needs its own `_meta` with the correct per-session history path.
4. In `insert_session_record()`, `handle_load_session_request()`, and `handle_resume_session_request()`, add `.meta(...)` to the response builder chain.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `NewSessionResponse._meta` contains `{"historyJsonlPath": "<absolute_path>"}` when persistence is available
- [ ] `LoadSessionResponse._meta` contains `{"historyJsonlPath": "<absolute_path>"}` when persistence is available
- [ ] `ResumeSessionResponse._meta` contains `{"historyJsonlPath": "<absolute_path>"}` when persistence is available
- [ ] Each `SessionInfo` in session/list response has `_meta.historyJsonlPath` when persistence is available
- [ ] `_meta` is `None` when no persistence store is configured (tests for this path)
- [ ] `cargo test` passes
- [ ] `cargo clippy` passes
- [ ] `cargo fmt` passes
- [ ] No new unwrap/expect/panic

## Testing

- Add tests in `acp/tests.rs` and `session/tests.rs` verifying `_meta` content
- Test with and without persistence store
- Verify the path is absolute and points to a valid history.jsonl location
close_reason: Implemented: NewSessionResponse, LoadSessionResponse, ResumeSessionResponse, and SessionInfo (in session/list) all include _meta.historyJsonlPath when persistence is configured. 5 new tests verify the field. All 313 tests pass, fmt/clippy clean.

title: Large tool arguments bypass request history size budget
description:
Large historical tool argument strings bypass the estimated 256 KiB request-message budget even when their tool results are small. The next model request resends the oversized assistant/tool unit instead of dropping it atomically, risking avoidable provider size-limit failures.

Observed 2026-10-08 in session 01a11b90-9116-76a2-8e2b-1dac48e77bb3 while independently reviewing daa-1c9z. Existing source path src/turn.rs::estimate_message_size charges a flat 150 bytes per tool call but no bytes for its variable-length arguments, name or id. PendingToolCalls accepts fragmented arguments, so this is reachable without violating the per-SSE-event limit. A FakeLlmClient consumer regression drives stream_model_turn with system + current user + write_file arguments containing 300000 ASCII characters + small saved result.

RED command: cargo test -q --bin acp-llm-adapter provider_request_drops_oversized_tool_arguments_with_their_results
Observed assertion: provider received 300389 message bytes despite the 256 KiB budget.
The same test verifies a 1024-byte argument remains intact when it fits.

Prior lessons reviewed: daa-wx1 (skip oversized units but keep useful smaller history), daa-rts (preserve tool pair structure), daa-1c9z (mandatory current user). Duplicate searches for tool arguments, estimate and size found no owner for omitted argument accounting. Existing large-message tests cover content, reasoning or tool results, not tool argument strings.

Fix direction: count variable tool-call strings at the existing estimator alongside message/reasoning content; retain existing overhead estimate, request budget, shared filter and grouping. No exact serialization redesign, new dependency, output cap or transport rewrite.

Acceptance: regression fails before fix and passes afterward; small tool unit remains unchanged; oversized argument/call and its small result are dropped together before LlmClient; mandatory system/current prompt survive; focused turn and serve request suites plus root full gates pass. Lesson belongs in this issue. This is an automated/code-discovered defect, not a maintainer-reported live failure.

title: serve: log ACP transport frames in both directions
description:
## Goal
`serve` records both directions of its own ACP wire traffic, so adapter logs are a superset of what a proxy could observe.

## Scope
- In scope: logging JSON-RPC frames at the adapter's ACP transport boundary in both directions, through the shared sink; connection-scoped destination until a session id exists.
- Out of scope: routing tracing events by session (separate task); `_meta` exposure; retention.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. Frames received from the client and frames sent to the client are both recorded.
2. Records use the same envelope as proxy-mode records and deserialize with the same type.
3. Logging is off unless enabled, and enabling it does not alter the frames on the wire.
4. Frames arriving before a session exists (`initialize`, `authenticate`) land in the connection-scoped file.

## Testing
- Use the existing in-memory fake client connection test seam: drive a session and assert both directions appear.
- Assert a record produced here and a record produced by proxy mode deserialize with the same envelope type.

## Notes
- Because the adapter owns the transport it can log at the boundary rather than teeing stdout, which is what makes both directions available and makes redaction possible at all.
close_reason: Added opt-in ACP_LOG serve transport logging for both wire directions, session binding from session/new responses, connection-scoped pre-session records, flush-on-shutdown, and regression coverage.

title: M1: Read-only tool loop
description:
## Problem Statement

A chat-only agent cannot investigate a codebase. The model must read files and search before it can help.

## Solution

Add the agentic tool loop with read-only tools: read_file (via client fs when advertised, else local), list_dir/glob/grep (local), each reported through tool_call/tool_call_update updates. No permission prompts (read-only).

## User Stories

1. As a user, I want the agent to read files, so that its answers reflect my actual code.
2. As a user, I want the agent to search/glob/list the project, so that it locates relevant code on its own.
3. As a user, I want each tool call shown in my editor, so that I can see what the agent is doing.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Given DeepSeek returns tool_calls for read-only tools, when the loop runs, then each is reported as tool_call (pending) then tool_call_update (completed) and the result is fed back to the model.
2. Given read_file and client advertises fs.readTextFile, then the read goes through fs/read_text_file (respecting unsaved buffers); otherwise a local read.
3. Given grep/glob/list_dir, then they execute locally (ripgrep engine / globset) and return bounded results.
4. Given the model issues further tool calls, then the loop iterates until none remain, or the iteration cap (default ~25) trips returning StopReason::max_turn_requests.

## Implementation Notes

- Tool JSON-schema registry passed in the DeepSeek tools param; accumulate streamed tool-call arguments by index.
- Search via ignore + grep crates; glob via globset.
- Capability-driven routing of read_file (client vs local).

## Testing Notes

- Mock model emitting tool calls; assert the tool_call/tool_call_update sequence and history feedback. Test the max_turn_requests cap.

## Out of Scope

Mutating tools, permissions, shell.
close_reason: Read-only tool loop implemented and verified

title: Provider tool-call indices can cause unbounded allocation
description:
Reality check 2026-10-07 at 37388ac0611632a5cd6215a5aae22ad1e59d8b2d (main, clean). Linux, Rust 1.97.1. The 507-test suite, fmt, Clippy, docs, release build and cargo audit passed; the evidence below came from source inspection and bounded offline runs of the shipped binary. No live provider calls or real credentials were used.

## Observed defect
A consumed provider tool-call index controls a synchronous allocation loop without an application bound. A tiny delta can request a vector with an enormous number of entries before normal cancellation or validation can run.

Static evidence: src/llm/stream.rs:136-141 deserializes index as usize; src/session.rs:270-274 then executes "while self.calls.len() <= index { self.calls.push(PendingToolCall::default()); }". Missing id/name/arguments are validated only later by finish(). The loop is real production code.
Minimal illustrative SSE input on a 64-bit build:
    data: {"choices":[{"delta":{"tool_calls":[{"index":18446744073709551615,"id":"audit","function":{"name":"read_file","arguments":"{}"}}]},"finish_reason":null}]}
This extreme payload was NOT executed: the audit deliberately avoided resource-exhaustion testing. The source establishes unbounded growth; actual OOM timing/process behavior is unverified.

## Root cause and missed coverage
Sparse, untrusted indices are treated as an instruction to allocate every preceding entry. Existing fixtures use small normal provider indices and do not assert resource limits. This is a separate mechanism from token-counter overflow and needs its own regression.

## Contract and fix direction
Validate tool-call index/cardinality before resizing or accumulating and before changing history or authorizing any execution. Introduce a justified finite bound or bounded sparse representation at the shared tool-delta boundary; make rejection a typed protocol failure. Preserve legitimate fragmented and interleaved tool calls. No unchecked loop may derive its work/memory directly from an arbitrary index.
Do not allocate a giant vector in a regression test, and do not raise a lint/resource threshold as the fix.

## Proof
Add a cheap unit test passing an index just beyond the chosen bound; it must reject immediately without growth proportional to the index. Include normal interleaved deltas and incomplete-call rejection. A bounded shipped-serve/local-provider test emits an invalid index and verifies prompt failure, zero permission/execution calls, a live responsive adapter and bounded memory/time. A stub that silently drops all tool deltas must fail the positive case.

## Scope
Size S. The tool-call accumulator and error propagation only. No provider limits are to be guessed from memory; document the local defensive bound and its rationale when implementing.

## Verification and handoff
Run the focused regression red before changing executable behavior, then the complete affected suite and repository gates in docs/agent-testing.md. Use temporary state directories and localhost fixtures with dummy credentials. Tests must assert the observed consumer behavior and identify the failing protocol stage without logging real payloads. Record the root-cause lesson here before closing. Implementation is deferred because this approved operation records the audit findings; nothing has been fixed or claimed.

description:

title: MCP SSE connections fail against legacy servers
description:
## Problem Statement

The adapter currently supports stdio and streamable HTTP MCP servers but explicitly rejects MCP SSE transport, while Claude ACP advertises SSE support. The team chose to defer this during the ACP parity grill-me session.

## Solution

Keep MCP SSE transport as a future parity feature. Revisit when near-term lifecycle, metadata, message ID, and plan-update work is complete or when a target ACP client/MCP server requires SSE.

## User Stories

1. As a user with an SSE-based MCP server, I want the adapter to connect to it, so that existing MCP integrations work without migration.
2. As a maintainer, I want SSE support to be evaluated separately, so that the near-term parity slice does not expand unexpectedly.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Given a future implementation, when the adapter advertises MCP SSE, then `McpServer::Sse` connection setup works end to end.
2. Given invalid SSE server configuration, when session setup runs, then errors are sanitized and do not leak secrets.
3. Given existing stdio and HTTP MCP support, when SSE is added, then existing transports keep passing tests.

## Implementation Notes

- Deferred by product decision.
- Check current `rmcp` transport support and official MCP transport guidance before implementation.
- Do not advertise SSE until connection, tool discovery, invocation, and tests exist.

## Testing Notes

- Add transport-level tests with a local SSE MCP fixture if/when implemented.
- Preserve existing stdio and streamable HTTP MCP tests.

## Out of Scope

- Near-term ACP parity slice.
- ACP elicitation.
notes:
Reality check 2026-10-07 at 37388ac0611632a5cd6215a5aae22ad1e59d8b2d (main, clean). Linux, Rust 1.97.1. The 507-test suite, fmt, Clippy, docs, release build and cargo audit passed; the evidence below came from source inspection and bounded offline runs of the shipped binary. No live provider calls or real credentials were used.

## Observed defect
The adapter advertises mcpCapabilities.sse=true and README marks SSE Full, but its SSE branch speaks Streamable HTTP. Users supplying a legacy HTTP+SSE MCP server cannot connect.

Reproduction: start target/debug/acp-llm-adapter serve --backend mock with temporary state. Initialize ACP; actual advertisement is {"http":true,"sse":true,"acp":false}. Request session/new with mcpServers=[{"type":"sse","name":"legacy","url":"http://127.0.0.1:PORT/sse","headers":[]}]. The localhost fixture returns 405 to POST /sse; GET /sse opens text/event-stream and announces "event: endpoint\ndata: /messages\n\n", with JSON-RPC POST handling at /messages.
Actual: the fixture saw only [["POST","/sse"]]; no GET or endpoint handshake occurred, and no session/new response arrived during a bounded five-second probe. The probe then terminated its own adapter.

## Root cause and missed coverage
src/mcp.rs:248-262 constructs StreamableHttpClientTransport for the SSE entry, just as the HTTP branch does. src/mcp/tests.rs:112-139 builds StreamableHttpService; tests at :411 and :700 reuse it under the SSE enum. Passing those tests proves Streamable HTTP only.
The official MCP transport compatibility specification requires legacy GET/endpoint handling after POST 4xx: https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-03-26/basic/transports#backwards-compatibility (checked during this audit).

## Contract and repair plan
Keep the original criteria, including sanitized invalid-configuration errors. Implement the advertised legacy HTTP+SSE handshake, discovery and tool RPC at the MCP transport edge using an existing supported transport if available. Check current installed rmcp APIs before choosing a solution; new dependencies require the repository's demonstrated-gap/audit procedure. Any proposal to remove the advertised capability instead changes the agreed promise and belongs in a maintainer decision, not a silent documentation downgrade.
Bound connection setup and cleanup, propagate relevant headers safely, and ensure failed setup cannot leave an MCP process/task or an unusable ACP connection.

## Proof
A genuine localhost legacy fixture has separate GET event and POST message endpoints. Through shipped serve, initialize -> session/new -> tools/list -> permitted tool call -> result must complete. Assert the GET/endpoint handshake actually occurred. Denial must prevent invocation. Exercise headers, invalid configuration, failed setup and cancellation with finite deadlines; retain stdio and Streamable HTTP regressions. Tests using StreamableHttpService alone do not close this issue.

## Scope and dependencies
Size M. Limit to legacy transport and its visible startup/failure behavior; no ACP elicitation or hosting changes. Completion depends on the shared MCP permission repair (daa-deo) and the shared ACP error-sanitization repair because this transport's original acceptance includes both actual tool invocation and non-leaking failures.

## Verification and handoff
Run the focused regression red before changing executable behavior, then the complete affected suite and repository gates in docs/agent-testing.md. Use temporary state directories and localhost fixtures with dummy credentials. Tests must assert the observed consumer behavior and identify the failing protocol stage without logging real payloads. Record the root-cause lesson here before closing. Implementation is deferred because this approved operation records the audit findings; nothing has been fixed or claimed.
close_reason: Legacy GET/endpoint plus POST transport implemented; genuine shipped-serve fixture proves approval, cancellation, recovery, safe endpoints and cleanup. 592 tests and all gates pass, including Rust 1.95; ten final wire stress runs pass. Lesson recorded.

Existing Streamable HTTP/stdio behavior remains covered. Begin from clean main 3e9ed65 and a passing full baseline, then run a legacy fixture regression red before production edits. Genuine fixture exposes only GET /sse plus POST /messages?session=legacy and requires synthetic Authorization on both. The prior test used a Streamable HTTP fixture under an SSE enum and missed the wrong handshake. Baseline all-features suite passed 587 tests.

comments.author: 01a11ade-38c4-7892-8886-a9990c95866c
comments.text:
Implemented legacy HTTP+SSE at the existing MCP I/O boundary in src/mcp/sse.rs, wired from connect_mcp_sse_session. Uses only the installed reqwest, sse-reqwest-client and rmcp Transport APIs; no added dependencies or new framework. GET opens the event stream, the initial endpoint event supplies the separate POST destination, and typed MCP responses arrive as message events on the same stream. Configured headers reach both channels. HTTP retries and SSE reconnects are disabled so a disconnected legacy session cannot replay a mutating call.

Safety/lifecycle: HTTP(S) URLs without userinfo/fragments; empty, unsafe and cross-origin endpoints rejected before POST; both GET and POST redirects rejected; custom headers marked sensitive for HTTP Debug diagnostics. Connection, initialization and tool discovery share a five-second deadline; POST acknowledgements are bounded separately. The SDK session owns the stream without custom workers. Cancellation continues through the existing approval policy and MCP request handle. Invalid JSON, oversized events, contradictory endpoint events and transport failures close the stream, with static safe error displays and underlying typed causes at the transport layer. Existing ACP presentation keeps failed setup sanitized and the connection usable.

Proof: the previously recorded red legacy regression passed after implementation. Replaced the two misleading StreamableHttpService-under-SSE fixtures with a genuine localhost legacy server requiring GET /sse plus POST /messages?session=legacy and synthetic authorization on both. Existing HTTP/stdio coverage remains. New shipped serve tests prove advertised discovery, Ask rejection preventing invocation, explicit one-time approval and tool-result feedback, cancellation during approval including stale approval, running MCP cancellation delivery/recovery, session-close/disconnect stream cleanup, sanitized invalid setup and continued ACP use. Negative cases cover empty/cross-origin endpoints, GET/POST redirect targets never reached, malformed JSON, missing endpoint, silent initialization and stalled discovery after SDK startup. Pure URL checks cover scheme, host, port, userinfo and fragments. README now describes the actual transport, security and deadline contract.

Final verification at c1b25cc06d7178aa865cc8fb746d1fe7f1f7e8b2 plus this change: clean pre-change baseline of 587 tests; final 592 tests pass with LLM_API_KEY=skip-ci-no-key cargo test -q --all-features on Rust 1.97.1 and cargo +1.95 test -q --all-features. Both toolchains pass fmt check, Clippy all targets/features -D warnings, and rustdoc -D warnings. cargo build --release -q, cargo audit -q, instruction-size and git diff checks pass. Ten consecutive final cargo +1.95 test -q --test serve_mcp_sse runs pass. Isolated release dev --backend mock smoke returns EndTurn and expected text. The concurrent Dependabot change was preserved and is now committed separately. No live provider or external MCP service was called.

Lesson: a transport enum is not proof of wire compatibility. The previous SSE tests used a modern Streamable HTTP fixture, so they confirmed the wrong protocol. A legacy regression must prove the GET/endpoint handshake and distinct POST destination, then observe side-effect counts across denial/cancellation and event-stream ownership across failure/teardown. Reuse the SDK transport seam and existing bounded parser rather than adding detached workers or unsafe replay. This issue was an agent loopback audit finding, not an unconfirmed maintainer live-server defect; closure uses its stated genuine-fixture acceptance. No additional standing instruction or design question is needed. Changes remain uncommitted; no release merge performed.

title: Implement ACP session/delete
description:
## Goal
Implement ACP `session/delete` so clients can remove active and persisted sessions through the protocol.

## Scope
- In scope: register and handle `DeleteSessionRequest`; advertise `sessionCapabilities.delete`; cancel/close active session state when present; remove persisted metadata/history; return protocol errors for unknown or invalid session IDs.
- Out of scope: `session/fork`; broad persistence refactors; MCP transport changes.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. Given an active in-memory session, when `session/delete` is called, then any active turn is cancelled, the session is removed from memory, and the response succeeds.
2. Given a persisted session that is not active, when `session/delete` is called, then its persisted metadata and history are removed and future `session/list` calls omit it.
3. Given an unknown session ID, when `session/delete` is called, then the adapter returns a clear ACP error without deleting unrelated sessions.
4. Given initialization, when capabilities are returned, then `sessionCapabilities.delete` is advertised only after the handler is implemented.

## Testing
- Add ACP handler tests for active-session delete, persisted-only delete, unknown-session errors, and capability advertisement.
- Add filesystem session store tests for deleting persisted session directories/history.
- Run the repo-required baseline/current test, fmt, and clippy checks before closing.

## Notes
- `session/delete` is intentionally stronger than `session/close`: it should close active state and delete persisted state.
- Keep deletion scoped to validated session IDs; do not introduce broad filesystem deletion helpers.
close_reason: Implemented ACP session/delete

title: Emit ACP usage_update cost for DeepSeek sessions
description:
## Context

`acp-llm-adapter` turns DeepSeek chat-completion chunks into ACP JSON-RPC. ACP's
`UsageUpdate` supports an optional `cost: { amount, currency }`, and
`UsageUpdate::new(used, size)` has a `.cost(...)` builder. LouiseLM and other
ACP clients render that cost in session telemetry.

DeepSeek's `usage` payload never includes cost. It only sends token counts, so
the adapter cannot forward cost; it must compute it.

## Evidence

Live session log at
`~/.local/state/acp-llm-adapter/20260821-203140-1918775-acp-llm-adapter-deepseek-stdout-jsonrpc.log`
has 61 `sessionUpdate: "usage_update"` notifications, all of this shape:

```json
{"sessionUpdate":"usage_update","used":86898,"size":1000000}
```

None include `cost`. The raw DeepSeek usage in the stderr log is:

```json
{"prompt_tokens":3196,"completion_tokens":269,"total_tokens":3465,
 "prompt_tokens_details":{"cached_tokens":3072},
 "completion_tokens_details":{"reasoning_tokens":173},
 "prompt_cache_hit_tokens":3072,"prompt_cache_miss_tokens":124}
```

## Proposed

Maintain a per-model pricing table for the DeepSeek backend (deepseek-v4-pro,
deepseek-v4-flash) including cache hit, cache miss, and reasoning token rates,
with an escape hatch to override via config/env. Accumulate cost across turns in
the session and attach `cost: { amount, currency: "USD" }` to the
`UsageUpdate` sent by `src/turn.rs`.

Keep it small: start with a static table and a config override, not a plugin
system. Currency is USD for DeepSeek.
close_reason: Added DeepSeek V4 pricing, cumulative session cost accounting, ACP usage_update cost emission, env overrides, persistence, tests, and documentation

Acceptance criteria:

- When exceeded, session/prompt returns StopReason::MaxTurnRequests.
- Existing tool-call replay behavior still works below the limit.
- Tests cover the limit boundary and the stop reason.

title: M4: Model selection, image input & docs polish
description:
## Problem Statement

v0.1 runs a fixed model, handles text+files only, and first-run setup is non-obvious (GUI editors may not inherit DEEPSEEK_API_KEY from the shell). Polish for real-world use.

## Solution

Wire the unstable session/set_model + availableModels (v4-flash / v4-pro / v4-pro+thinking) for capable clients with DEEPSEEK_MODEL as the default; map ACP image content blocks to DeepSeek image_url parts; write the README including the GUI env-inheritance gotcha.

## User Stories

1. As a Zed user, I want to switch models mid-session, so that I can trade cost/quality per task.
2. As a CodeCompanion user, I want a sensible default model from env, so that it works without a picker.
3. As a user, I want to send images, so that the model can use screenshots/diagrams.
4. As a new user, I want clear setup docs, so that DEEPSEEK_API_KEY is found even when launched from a GUI editor.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Given a client supporting set_model, then availableModels are advertised and session/set_model switches the active model; otherwise DEEPSEEK_MODEL (default deepseek-v4-pro) is used.
2. Given an ACP prompt with image content, then it is forwarded as an OpenAI-style image_url content part to DeepSeek.
3. Given the README, then it documents env-only config and the agent_servers.env workaround for GUI-launched editors.

## Implementation Notes

- set_model lives behind the crate's unstable feature; a graceful no-op for clients lacking it.

## Testing Notes

- set_model present vs absent; image content mapping.

## Out of Scope

Auto model-router, MCP client support, loadSession.

    git worktree add /tmp/baseline HEAD
    cd /tmp/baseline && CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/tmp/baseline-target cargo test -q --no-fail-fast
    # test result: FAILED. 16 passed; 2 failed  (tests/acp_proxy_stdio.rs)

Failure:

    thread 'lifecycle::parent_death_does_not_depend_on_client_stdin_reaching_eof'
    panicked at tests/lifecycle/mod.rs:67:5:
    proxy descendants survived: [("proxy", 216613), ("holder", 216614)]

assert_descendants_gone (tests/lifecycle/mod.rs:66-79) excludes the 'client' and 'holder' roles from the aliveness check, so the survivor that actually fails the assertion is the **proxy process itself**. After the client goes away, the proxy is still running.

Deterministic: three consecutive full-suite runs produced the same two failures with the same counts. Unaffected by clearing ACP_LOG_UNREDACTED / ACP_LOG_MAX_BYTES / ACP_LOG_MAX_AGE_DAYS from the environment (that variable set causes a different, unrelated failure - see the logsink test-isolation bug).

## Why it was not caught

daa-30py's description attributed these two failures to an older fixture ignoring ACP_PROXY_TREE_ROLE ('tree did not start'). That premise is wrong: the message is 'proxy descendants survived', it reproduces on a clean tree with exactly one fixture artifact, and it still reproduces after daa-30py's fix made fixture selection exact. The stale-fixture bug was masking how these tests actually fail, not causing it.

## Acceptance

- Both tests pass on a clean worktree with a fresh target dir.
- The reap path covers parent death that does not reach stdin EOF, and client death when a second session is live, without touching the other session.
- State whether 9817a88's fix was incomplete or whether these two scenarios were known-red when it merged.
close_reason: gate:tests/lifecycle/mod.rs:119 — alive() now reads the state field from /proc/<pid>/stat and treats Z as gone, parsing the state as the first token after the final ')' so a comm containing spaces or parentheses cannot shift the field. Red: both lifecycle tests failed deterministically on three consecutive runs, each burning the full 5s wait_until deadline. Green: 18/18 in tests/acp_proxy_stdio.rs, suite time for that target down from 5.03s to 1.07s because the deadline is no longer being spent. Full suite matches a clean baseline with ACP_LOG_* cleared; fmt and clippy --all-targets --all-features clean. Not a product defect: the proxy exits and reaps its whole subtree correctly, as the per-role /proc state sampling in the comment shows. Priority dropped P1 to P2 and the issue retitled when the evidence contradicted the original premise. Lesson recorded here and in the code comment: liveness of a process you did not spawn cannot be tested by /proc directory existence, because nothing guarantees anyone reaps it. Third instance of the same failure mode as daa-30py and daa-oh9o — the local suite reporting failures that are properties of the developer's environment, not the code.

comments.author: claude/2fa16d4c-999c-4b99-8d90-8f1422f73de7
comments.text:
Diagnosis in the description is wrong. The proxy does not survive client death — it exits correctly and reaps every descendant. The test misreads an unreaped exit status as a live process.

## Evidence

Sampling /proc/<pid>/stat field 3 for every recorded role while the test runs:

    parent_death_does_not_depend_on_client_stdin_reaching_eof
      client  GONE
      proxy   Z      ppid=141502
      agent   GONE
      worker  GONE
      leaf    GONE
      holder  S      ppid=141502   (expected to survive)

    client_death_reaps_detached_descendants_without_touching_another_session
      killed tree:    client GONE, proxy Z, agent GONE, worker GONE, leaf GONE
      neighbour tree: all five S                    (correctly untouched)

The proxy is a **zombie**, and its whole subtree is gone. That is the reap path working. Reproduced by hand outside the harness too: build the tree, `kill -9` the client, and agent/worker/leaf disappear while client and proxy linger as `ZN`.

## Root cause

tests/lifecycle/mod.rs:109 defined liveness as directory existence:

    fn alive(pid: u32) -> bool {
        std::path::Path::new(&format!("/proc/{pid}")).exists()
    }

The kernel keeps /proc/<pid> until someone reaps the exit status. Both failing tests SIGKILL the proxy's parent, so no one is left to reap the proxy; it is reparented to the nearest subreaper and stays a zombie for as long as that subreaper declines to collect it. On this machine an ancestor subreaper (pid 141502) never reaps, so the zombie outlives the test's 5s deadline every time. Under an ancestry whose reaper collects promptly — a container with a reaping PID 1 — the window is too short to observe, which is why CI is green.

The three lifecycle tests that pass are exactly the three where someone reaps the proxy: proxy_termination and wrapped_agent_exit leave the client fixture alive to `wait()` on it, and client_eof_bounds makes the test process itself the proxy's parent. The two that fail are exactly the two that kill the parent. The pattern fits the zombie explanation and nothing else.

## Correction to the premise

daa-30py claimed these two failures were stale-fixture noise; I claimed they were a real reap defect from 9817a88. Both were wrong. 9817a88's fix is sound and its coverage was not red when it merged — it is red only under a process ancestry that does not reap orphans.

title: Serve wire logs attribute earlier sessions to the latest session
description:
Per-session logs can contain another session's wire traffic and mislabel the record envelope, making debugging evidence misleading.

## Observed
ACP_LOG=1; create A, create B, then prompt A. A's prompt request is in B/log.jsonl with envelope session_id=B but payload.params.sessionId=A. Route session-bearing frames by their actual session. Correlate request/response IDs when responses omit sessionId, in both directions, without mixing client and agent ID spaces. Keep genuinely unscoped frames in connection fallback; avoid falsely attributing initialize/list/unknown replies to last session. Handle out-of-order replies and sequential sessions, cleanup completed mappings, preserve redaction and wire transparency. Reuse existing connection/sink interfaces; don't broaden into a generalized protocol framework. Assess proxy's shared mechanism and fix common root if applicable; preserve opaque forwarding.
