title: ACP v1 spec parity for DeepSeek ACP adapter
description:
## Problem Statement

The DeepSeek ACP adapter should provide honest ACP v1 spec parity for the protocol phases it can support, using Claude ACP as a comparison reference without copying Claude-specific SDK behavior. The adapter currently covers many baseline methods, but the grill-me review identified lifecycle and notification gaps that affect client interoperability and visible session behavior.

## Solution

Implement the near-term ACP parity slice for session lifecycle, session metadata notifications, message grouping, and real plan updates. Keep DeepSeek API capability boundaries explicit: do not advertise image, audio, or binary prompt support because the current DeepSeek chat API path only supports text-oriented chat content and tool calls. Use Claude ACP behavior as reference material, not as a compatibility contract.

## User Stories

1. As an ACP client, I want the adapter to advertise only capabilities it actually supports, so that my UI does not offer broken prompt inputs.
2. As an ACP client, I want persisted sessions to be deletable through `session/delete`, so that session lists can be managed without manual filesystem cleanup.
3. As an ACP client, I want live `session_info_update` notifications when a session title or activity timestamp changes, so that session pickers and histories stay current during active use.
4. As an ACP client, I want stable message IDs on streamed chunks and prompt responses, so that live and replayed conversation content can be grouped reliably.
5. As a user, I want agent plan updates to represent actual agent planning, so that plan UI is meaningful rather than derived from prompt punctuation.
6. As a maintainer, I want unsupported ACP features recorded as deferred work, so that future parity improvements are visible without polluting the near-term slice.

## Implementation Decisions

- Target ACP spec parity first, with selected Claude-like UX only where it maps cleanly to ACP and DeepSeek capabilities.
- Include unstable ACP schema features already enabled by the dependency when they are relevant to the agreed parity slice.
- Implement `session/delete` as stronger than `session/close`: cancel/close active in-memory state if present, then delete persisted session metadata/history.
- Implement `session_info_update` despite Claude not currently emitting it, because the adapter already tracks title and `updatedAt` and the README calls the notification out as missing.
- Add stable ACP message IDs using client-provided IDs when available and generated UUIDs for assistant/thought chunks where needed.
- Replace the prompt-splitting plan placeholder with an explicit model/tool-driven plan mechanism.
- Keep content support honest: text, resource links, and embedded text resources are supported; images, audio, and binary/blob resources are not advertised.

## Testing Decisions

- Add focused ACP handler tests for `session/delete`, including active-session removal and persisted-session deletion.
- Add prompt-turn tests for `session_info_update` ordering and contents.
- Add stream/replay tests for message ID stability across user, assistant, and thought chunks.
- Add tool-loop tests for explicit plan update behavior and regression tests proving fake prompt-split plans are removed or gated.
- Continue running the repo-required baseline/current `cargo test`, `cargo fmt`, and `cargo clippy` checks when implementing each task.

## Out of Scope

- MCP SSE transport is deferred for now.
- ACP elicitation is deferred until an MCP elicitation bridge or model-visible `ask_user` tool is intentionally added.
- Image, audio, and binary/blob prompt input are not supported by this adapter unless DeepSeek API capabilities change.
- Claude-specific private `_meta` conventions and raw `_claude/sdkMessage` notifications are not part of this parity target.
- Literal implementation parity with the Claude TypeScript adapter is not a goal.

## Further Notes

The settled near-term order is lifecycle gaps first, then metadata/message grouping, then plan quality. Claude ACP remains useful as a behavior reference for session list shape, message IDs, tool rendering, and plan notifications, but ACP docs and this adapter’s architecture are the source of truth.
close_reason: Near-term ACP parity slice completed; remaining deferred items were resolved as out-of-scope for this milestone

title: Mock backend cannot emit tool calls, so no serve-level tool execution test exists
description:
daa-zsjw's acceptance asked for the cancellation fix to be verified at the serve level, with a live local command, because tests/serve_shutdown.rs only covers idle EOF. That verification could not be written: MockLlmClient (src/dev.rs:258) emits Thought, Message, Finished(EndTurn) and never a tool call, so no test can drive a real "acp-llm-adapter serve" process into executing run_command.

The gap is wider than one test. Every serve-level behaviour that depends on a tool call - permission prompting over real ACP, tool-call status updates reaching the client, cancellation mid-tool-call, shutdown while a tool runs - is currently unreachable from an integration test. The unit tests around run_command_tool_execution cover the function; nothing covers the path a real editor drives.

## Scope

- Let the mock backend emit a scripted sequence of tool calls, keyed off the prompt text or an environment variable so a test can ask for a specific one, e.g. a run_command with a chosen command string.
- Keep it honest: the mock should produce the same StreamEvent shape a real provider does, so a test that passes against it means something.
- Then write the serve-level test daa-zsjw wanted: drive serve through the handshake, trigger a long-running run_command, close stdin, and assert the process exits promptly and leaves nothing behind.

## Constraint

The mock is production code reached by --backend mock, not a test fixture, so the scripting hook has to be deliberate and documented rather than a hidden test backdoor.
close_reason: gate:src/dev.rs and tests/serve_shutdown.rs — the mock backend now answers a "!tool run_command <command>" prompt with a real run_command tool call, streamed as separate metadata and argument deltas with a ToolCalls finish reason, so a caller that only handled one combined delta would pass here and fail against a provider. It closes the turn when a tool result comes back, which unit tests pin explicitly because without it the agent loop re-issues the same call forever. Documented in README under Mock Backend and on the constant itself as an affordance of --backend mock, usable from an editor session, not a test-only hook - the constraint the issue set. That unlocked the serve-level test daa-zsjw wanted and could not have: it drives the real binary through initialize, session/new, a tool call, the permission round-trip and a mid-command disconnect. It immediately earned its keep by exposing daa-hivc, a real leak on the disconnect path, which is fixed in the same change. Full suite 126/323/18/2/11 green; the new test mutation-checked and stress-run 20 times. Still not covered, and worth a future issue if it matters: tool-call status updates reaching the client, and cancellation via session/cancel rather than disconnect.

title: Cancelling an editor file read leaves the session busy

title: History truncation collapses to 1 message when a single recent message exceeds the byte budget
description:
## Problem

`filter_messages_truncate` in src/turn.rs (added in fea6349, still present after
0a2eb66) walks the conversation backward from the most recent message, adding
each to the filtered list until one doesn't fit the remaining 512KB budget, then
`break`s immediately:

```rust
for msg in messages[1..].iter().rev() {
    let msg_size = estimate_message_size(msg);
    if msg_size > budget {
        break;   // <-- should skip/continue, not abort the whole walk
    }
    budget = budget.saturating_sub(msg_size);
    filtered.push(msg.clone());
}
```

Because messages are visited newest-first, a single oversized *recent* message
(e.g. a large tool result embedding a file read or command output) stops the
walk before any older, smaller messages get a chance — even though they would
fit. The function also unconditionally keeps `messages[0]` (the very first
message in the whole session, not necessarily a system prompt) forever,
re-sending it on every single API call regardless of size.

Net effect: whenever the most recent message alone is bigger than
`512KB - size(messages[0])`, the filtered history collapses to just
`[messages[0]]`. The model receives zero intervening context and effectively
re-answers the original first message repeatedly.

## Evidence

Observed directly in
~/.local/state/codecompanion-acp/20260715-163958-deepseek-acp-adapter-stderr.log:
`message_count` in the "sending chat completion request to DeepSeek" trace
grows normally (2,4,7,10,...22) across a tool-calling turn, then drops straight
back to `message_count=1` and stays there for 16 consecutive requests (~80s),
before recovering. This matches a long grill-me session where the user
observed the adapter appearing to "resend" the same original message
repeatedly.

## Fix

- Change `break` to skip-and-continue so smaller older messages still get a
  chance to fit after a single oversized recent message is skipped.
- Reconsider unconditionally pinning `messages[0]` forever — it's the oldest
  raw message, not a real system prompt, and can itself be arbitrarily large.

title: Confine explicit file tools and editor filesystem requests
description:
## Goal
Implement the maintainer-confirmed file authority contract from daa-eja6 for read_file, write_file, edit_file and list_dir.

## Scope
Shared path resolution and local/editor filesystem edges only; no shell or MCP authority changes, no broad core refactor. Preserve other sessions' claims and this session's prior uncommitted fixes.

## Checklist and acceptance
[x] Red local and editor tests reject outside absolute paths, ../ escapes, sibling-prefix paths, out-of-root symlinks and dangling links; zero forbidden editor read/write or approval requests and no outside mutation.
[x] Positive cwd/additional-root, absolute in-root, missing-file creation, and in-root symlink cases.
[x] Resolve existing ancestors and validate before permission/preflight; revalidate delegated writes after awaits.
[x] Directory-capability local I/O prevents symlink-swap escape after validation/approval.
[x] Run filesystem work off async executor threads.
[x] Preserve mode/cancellation/permission behavior; no mode bypasses roots.
[x] Update AGENTS/README and record client enforcement obligations without claiming an OS sandbox.
[x] Focused/full tests, lint, rustdoc, release, audit, size, diff and repeated filesystem fixtures.

## Implementation constraint
Standard-library canonicalize+starts_with is insufficient for the check/open race; rustix supplies platform-level pieces but not a portable confined filesystem API. Use a maintained capability filesystem wrapper only after cargo audit and current primary API documentation review; do not write unsafe or a custom path-walking syscall layer.

## Baseline
573 tests pass on Rust 1.95 before this change. The old resolve_tool_path passes absolute paths unchanged and local fs opens unrestricted paths. Actual red regression evidence will be recorded before executable changes.
close_reason: Confirmed filesystem policy implemented for explicit tools; regression, real-serve and complete gates pass.

Both local and editor routes are covered by the regressions. Baseline before these tests: 573 passing tests.

comments.author: 01a11a2d-1cf2-7620-abe6-ce12e14e76fd
comments.text: Completed: explicit file tools share ConfinedPath with cap-std directory-relative I/O; checks precede permissions, binary preflight, reads and writes. Editor requests revalidate canonical paths after waits; cancellation is checked again after validation/before local work. Filesystem work runs on blocking pool. Regressions cover all permission modes, traversal/prefix/absolute escapes, external/dangling/loop symlinks, safe symlinks/additional roots/new files, and file/parent replacement during approval. Real serve verifies zero forbidden approval/editor requests, unchanged outside sentinel, additional-root lookup, recovery and disconnect. Validation: 580 tests pass, clippy all targets/features, rustdoc -D warnings, release build, cargo audit (316 dependencies), instruction size 11353/12000, diff check; 10 repeated runs of 6 file-root unit tests plus the serve fixture pass. title: CLI: make --backend required on serve and dev
description:
## Goal
Make --backend a REQUIRED CLI flag on both `serve` and `dev`, eliminating the silent internal default so the effective backend is always present on the argv (and thus in debug filenames and the script's argv echo).

## Scope
- In scope: src/main.rs CLI definition + affected tests + README wording.
- Remove `default_value_t = Backend::DeepSeek` from the `serve` --backend arg (~src/main.rs:119) and `default_value_t = Backend::Mock` from the `dev` --backend arg (~src/main.rs:127), leaving `#[arg(long, value_enum)]`. Clap then treats both as required.
- Fix any test that parsed `serve`/`dev` WITHOUT --backend and relied on the default (notably the parse tests around src/main.rs:697-714). Grep test modules for parse_from/try_parse_from on serve/dev and add explicit --backend where the default was assumed.
- README: remove any wording that claims a default backend (e.g. "default deepseek"). Launch configs (README ~106-159) already pass --backend explicitly -> no change needed there.
- Out of scope: acp-debug.sh changes (sibling task); adding startup logging (deemed redundant once --backend is required).

## Acceptance Criteria
1. `cargo run -- serve` (no --backend) exits with a clap "required" error; same for `cargo run -- dev`.
2. `cargo run -- dev --backend mock` runs the smoke test successfully.
3. `--backend deepseek|glm|mock` still parse; invalid values still rejected (existing round-trip / invalid-value tests unaffected).
4. Full suite green with no new failures vs. baseline.

## Testing
- Baseline first per AGENTS.md: `git stash && cargo test -q 2>&1 | grep -E "^test result|FAILED"; git stash pop`.
- After changes: `cargo test -q`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`.

## Notes

- The dev->serve child spawn already passes --backend explicitly (src/dev.rs:113-128), so it is unaffected.
- No unwrap/expect/panic; keep clippy pedantic clean.

title: Shared log sink: record envelope, directory layout, non-blocking writer
description:
## Goal
A shared logging sink that both `serve` and `proxy` write through, so the two modes cannot drift into different formats.

## Scope
- In scope: state-root and directory-layout resolution; the NDJSON record envelope (timestamp, session id, direction, kind, payload); a bounded non-blocking writer that drops rather than blocks and counts drops; per-session file handle map; the connection-scoped fallback file used before any session id is known.
- Out of scope: wiring into `serve` or `proxy`; tracing integration; retention; redaction. Those are separate tasks that consume this one.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. Records serialize to one JSON object per line and round-trip through the same envelope type.
2. Records with no session id land in a connection-scoped file; records with a session id land under a directory keyed by that id.
3. A caller can switch a connection from "no session" to a session id mid-stream and subsequent records route to the new destination.
4. When the writer's queue is saturated, `write` returns without blocking and the dropped-record count increases.
5. The sink's root is configurable so proxy mode can use a root separate from the session store.

## Testing
- Unit tests over a temp directory: envelope round-trip, routing before/after session id is known, saturation drops counted.
- Follow the project test-logging convention: `test-log` as the default test attribute.

## Notes
- This is deliberately a shared foundation rather than something extracted later. Two consumers needing an identical format is exactly the case where "extract after" produces the drift the parent feature exists to remove.
- Non-blocking is not an optimization here: in proxy mode a blocked sink stalls the wrapped agent, which is worse than having no logs.
close_reason: Implemented as acp_llm_adapter::logsink in the library crate so both binaries can share it. LogSink/LogWriter split lets tests drive the writer inline, so backpressure and routing are deterministic with no sleeps. Calendar arithmetic moved from the binary's session module to acp_llm_adapter::timestamp rather than copied. 19 new tests; clippy and fmt clean.

title: Emit session_info_update on metadata changes
description:
## Goal
Emit ACP `session_info_update` notifications when prompt activity changes session metadata.

## Scope
- In scope: detect title and `updatedAt` changes during prompt setup; emit `SessionUpdate::SessionInfoUpdate` at the start of a prompt turn; include title only when newly derived and `updatedAt` whenever refreshed; keep lock-free async boundaries.
- Out of scope: changing title derivation heuristics beyond what is needed for notification correctness; emitting metadata updates on every streamed chunk.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. Given a new session with no title, when the first prompt begins, then the adapter emits `session_info_update` with the derived title and refreshed `updatedAt`.
2. Given an existing titled session, when a later prompt begins, then the adapter emits `session_info_update` with refreshed `updatedAt` and does not resend an unchanged title.
3. Given prompt setup fails before metadata changes are committed, then no misleading `session_info_update` is emitted.
4. Given persisted sessions, when history is saved, then stored title/updatedAt remain consistent with the notification values.

## Testing
- Add prompt-turn tests for first-turn title notification and later-turn timestamp-only notification.
- Add ACP handler/transport tests if needed to verify notification ordering relative to plan/message chunks.
- Run the repo-required baseline/current test, fmt, and clippy checks before closing.

## Notes
- Claude ACP currently does not emit this notification; this is intentionally spec-parity behavior for this adapter.
- Existing session state already tracks title and `updated_at`; prefer returning a small metadata-change value from turn setup over re-reading shared state after awaits.
close_reason: Emit session_info_update now omits unchanged titles on later turns

title: Populate title and updated_at on SessionInfo for session/list and session/resume
description:
## Motivation

When the user runs `/resume` inside Neovim (via deepseek-acp-adapter), they only see session IDs in the picker — no context about what the session was about or when it was last active. This makes it hard to choose which session to resume.

## What ACP Provides

The `SessionInfo` struct already has:

- **`title: Option<String>`** — intended as a human-readable label for the session (e.g., derived from the first user message)
- **`updated_at: Option<String>`** — ISO 8601 timestamp of last activity
- **`meta: Option<Meta>`** — a `serde_json::Map<String, Value>` for arbitrary extra data

The `session/resume` response also has `_meta` for agent-to-client extensibility.

## What Needs to Change

### 1. Adapter: populate `title` and `updated_at`

- `src/session.rs` `SessionStore::list_sessions()` — add `.title(...)` and `.updated_at(...)` when constructing `SessionInfo`
- `src/session_store.rs` `FilesystemSessionStore::list_persisted()` — same

### 2. Store the needed data

- `title`: derive from the first user `ChatMessage` in the session history (truncated to ~80 chars)
- `updated_at`: store a last-activity timestamp on `SessionRecord` and persist it in `PersistedSessionMeta`

### 3. Persist the new fields

- Add `title` and `updated_at` to `PersistedSessionMeta`
- Handle backward compat when loading old meta files (no title -> show session_id)

### 4. (Optional) Emit `session_info_update` notifications

The protocol has a `session_info_update` notification that can push metadata changes to the client during a session. Currently listed as not emitted.

## Client-Side

The Neovim CodeCompanion plugin would also need to display these fields in its session picker — that's out of scope for this crate, but populating the data unlocks it.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] New sessions get a `title` derived from the first user prompt
- [ ] `updated_at` is set on session creation and bumped on each `session/prompt`
- [ ] Old persisted sessions (no title/updated_at) don't break
- [ ] `session/list` returns `title` and `updated_at` for all sessions
- [ ] No new unwrap/expect/panic
close_reason: Implemented: SessionInfo now returns title (derived from first user msg) and updated_at (ISO 8601 timestamp) for session/list and session/resume. Backward compat with old persisted sessions.

title: acp-proxy never exits when the wrapped agent process exits before completing the ACP handshake
description:
acp-proxy spawns a wrapped agent CLI (e.g. `acp-proxy -- opencode acp`). If
that wrapped child process exits (any exit code) before ever completing an
ACP handshake over stdio, acp-proxy itself does not exit or otherwise signal
failure — it keeps running indefinitely. Any client spawning acp-proxy and
relying on process exit to detect a dead/misconfigured wrapped agent (e.g.
louiselm.nvim, see louiselm-8hau in the louiselm repo) hangs forever with no
error.

## Observed

2026-08-30, acp-proxy 0.7.3 (`~/.cargo/bin/acp-proxy`, built from this repo).

```
$ cat /tmp/fake-broken-agent.sh
#!/bin/sh
echo "Error: fake broken agent, postinstall never ran" >&2
exit 1

$ timeout 5 acp-proxy -- /tmp/fake-broken-agent.sh
Error: fake broken agent, postinstall never ran
```

The command did not return after the 5s `timeout` elapsed. `timeout`'s
SIGTERM to acp-proxy had no observed effect — the process was still running
well past 5 seconds (confirmed via `ps aux`, pid 433857 still alive, parent of
the already-dead `/tmp/fake-broken-agent.sh`). Had to `kill -9` the `timeout`
and `acp-proxy` processes manually to reclaim the terminal.

acp-proxy does relay the wrapped process's stderr correctly (the "Error: fake
broken agent..." line is printed by acp-proxy, presumably passthrough) — the
defect is specifically that it does not react to the wrapped child's exit by
exiting itself or emitting any ACP-level error/shutdown signal on its own
stdout.

Real-world trigger this was found while debugging: opencode CLI's npm
postinstall script hadn't run, so `opencode acp` exited immediately (exit 1)
without ever speaking ACP; `acp-proxy -- opencode acp` then hung
indefinitely, which surfaced upstream in louiselm.nvim as a chat session
stuck on "Starting" forever with no error (louiselm-8hau).

## Symptoms

- `acp-proxy -- <cmd>` does not terminate when `<cmd>` exits, regardless of
  `<cmd>`'s exit code.
- No ACP-level notification, error, or process exit communicates the wrapped
  child's death to whatever spawned acp-proxy.
- Not killable via a plain `timeout`/SIGTERM in the observed repro; needed
  SIGKILL. (Whether acp-proxy ignores SIGTERM specifically, or is blocked in
  an uninterruptible wait, is unconfirmed — see below.)

## Root cause

Unknown at the acp-proxy source level — this was found by black-box process
testing, not by reading acp-proxy's code. Hypothesis: acp-proxy spawns the
wrapped child and enters a read loop on the child's stdout waiting for ACP
JSON-RPC frames, but has no code path that watches for the child process
exiting (e.g. no wait()/waitpid handling wired to the read loop, or the
event driving shutdown is "stdout closed" but the child's stdout pipe stays
open past its own process exit in a way that doesn't trigger EOF promptly).
What would discriminate: instrumenting or tracing acp-proxy's process-exit
handling for the wrapped child, and checking whether it installs a SIGTERM
handler that never completes vs. genuinely ignoring the signal.

## Why it was not caught

No test in this repo (unverified — not inspected) exercises a wrapped child
that exits immediately without ever writing a valid ACP frame to stdout.

## Fix direction

Watch the wrapped child's exit (wait/waitpid or equivalent async completion)
concurrently with the stdio read loop; on child exit, acp-proxy should exit
itself (propagating the child's exit code or a distinguishable one) rather
than continuing to wait for protocol frames that will never arrive. Not
investigated: whether SIGTERM handling also needs a fix independently of the
child-exit-detection gap.

## Acceptance

- A regression test: spawn acp-proxy wrapping a script that exits
  immediately (zero or nonzero) without writing to stdout, assert acp-proxy
  itself exits within a bounded time.
- Live: `timeout 5 acp-proxy -- /tmp/fake-broken-agent.sh` (script above)
  returns within the timeout instead of hanging.

## Not covered

- Whether acp-proxy also mishandles a child that writes a partial/invalid ACP
  frame and then exits (only the "no output at all" case was tested here).
- The actual source-level mechanism — this bead is filed from black-box
  behavior, not a code read of this repo.
- The louiselm-side gaps this exposed (no startup timeout, dropped stderr) —
  tracked as louiselm-8hau and louiselm-s6cj in the louiselm.nvim repo, not
  here.
close_reason:
Root cause: main() returned ExitCode after the wrapped child exited. #[tokio::main]
drops the Runtime on return, which blocks until every spawn_blocking task finishes.
The stdin-forwarding pump reads via tokio::io::stdin(), a spawn_blocking thread doing
a real blocking read() on the proxy's own stdin. .abort() cancels the async wrapper
but cannot interrupt that OS-level blocking read, so if anything (a pipe, a terminal,
a real client) still holds the proxy's stdin open when the wrapped child dies,
Runtime::drop hangs forever even though wait_for_child() returned promptly.

Fix: main() now calls std::process::exit() directly instead of returning ExitCode,
bypassing the runtime's blocking-pool drain on shutdown. #[allow(clippy::exit)]
added with justification.

Regression test: tests/acp_proxy_stdio.rs
proxy_exits_when_the_wrapped_agent_dies_before_the_handshake, plus a new
ACP_LLM_ADAPTER_PROXY_FIXTURE_EXIT_IMMEDIATELY fixture env var so the fake agent
can exit before reading stdin. Verified the test fails (10s timeout) against the
pre-fix binary and passes after the fix. Live repro from the bead
(`timeout 5 acp-proxy -- fake-broken-agent.sh`) now returns exit 1 immediately.

Refs daa-yrsj

title: acp-debug.sh: backend-aware, collision-safe log filenames
description:
## Goal
Make acp-debug.sh log filenames carry a backend/variant label so runs of acp-llm-adapter against different backends are distinguishable, while staying generic for backend-less binaries (e.g. codex-acp).

## Scope
- In scope: acp-debug.sh only, plus the README "## Debugging" section.
- Derive a run label with precedence: ACP_DEBUG_LABEL env override -> else the --backend value auto-parsed from argv (handle both `--backend V` and `--backend=V`) -> else no label.
- Sanitize the label to [A-Za-z0-9._-] (replace anything else with `_`); empty stays empty.
- Place the label between binary name and stream suffix, OMITTED ENTIRELY when absent so codex-acp filenames are byte-for-byte identical to today.
- Add PID ($$) to filenames to prevent same-second collisions (timestamp is second-resolution; script appends with >> / tee -a).
- Optional hardening: ACP_BINARY="$(basename "$1")" so a path-qualified binary can't inject `/` into the filename.
- Final shape: <ts>-<pid>-<binary>[-<label>]-stderr.log and ...-stdout-jsonrpc.log
  e.g. 20260610-080836-32451-acp-llm-adapter-deepseek-stderr.log
- Out of scope: any Rust changes (handled by the sibling task).

## Acceptance Criteria
1. `./acp-debug.sh acp-llm-adapter dev --backend mock` produces files containing `-mock-`.
2. `ACP_DEBUG_LABEL=zzz ./acp-debug.sh acp-llm-adapter dev --backend mock` produces `-zzz-`, not `-mock-` (env override wins).
3. `./acp-debug.sh echo hello` produces `...-echo-stderr.log` with NO label segment (backend-less degrade, unchanged from today).
4. `ACP_DEBUG_LABEL=tag ./acp-debug.sh echo hello` produces `...-echo-tag-stderr.log`.
5. Two back-to-back identical invocations produce two distinct PID-stamped file pairs (no interleaving into one file).
6. README "## Debugging" shows the new ts-pid-binary-backend filename shape and documents ACP_DEBUG_LABEL.

## Testing
- Manual end-to-end runs above (logs land in ${XDG_STATE_HOME:-$HOME/.local/state}/acp-llm-adapter/).
- `bash -n acp-debug.sh` (syntax) and a shellcheck pass if available.

## Notes
- Script runs under `set -u`; guard the env read as ${ACP_DEBUG_LABEL:-}.
- Independent of the sibling CLI task: works whenever --backend is passed explicitly (README launch configs already do).
close_reason: Updated acp-debug.sh for backend-aware PID-stamped collision-safe filenames with ACP_DEBUG_LABEL override; updated README Debugging section

title: Handle non-UTF-8 file reads without internal ACP error
description:
When using `deepseek_acp_adapter`, a read-file tool call against a Cargo target fingerprint artifact fails as an internal ACP/JSON-RPC error instead of returning a controlled tool error.

Observed log excerpt:

title: Replace EofGuard with direct tokio::select! for stdin EOF
description:
## Source

Ponytail-audit finding #6 (shrink, borderline).

## Problem

src/main.rs defines an EofGuard type and attach_eof_guard function (~35 lines) to cancel a CancellationToken when stdin closes. This is correct and idiomatic, but a simpler approach (tokio::select! in the serve loop that also awaits stdin EOF) would eliminate the type and function entirely.

## What to do

Replace the EofGuard/attach_eof_guard pattern with a tokio::select! in stdio_transport_with_eof that races stdin read against shutdown signal, canceling the token directly when stdin EOF is reached.

## Acceptance Criteria

- EofGuard struct and attach_eof_guard function no longer exist.
- Stdin closure still causes prompt process shutdown.
- All existing tests pass identically.

## Estimated impact

~35 lines removed. Borderline -- current code is correct and idiomatic. Only worth it if the tokio::select! approach is clearly simpler.

## Note

This is borderline. The current code is correct, safe, and self-documenting. Apply only if the replacement is clearly simpler, not just different.
close_reason: Won't implement: the current EofGuard+attach_eof_guard pattern is already the simplest correct approach. RAII Drop-based cancellation is idiomatic Rust. A tokio::select! alternative would conflict with stdin ownership (the ACP transport owns stdin) or require an extra spawned task, adding complexity rather than reducing it. The tokio::select! in serve() already races against shutdown.cancelled() which EofGuard triggers cleanly. Per the issue's own note: 'current code is correct and idiomatic. Only worth it if the tokio::select! approach is clearly simpler' - it is not.

title: Invalid MCP setup closes serve without a session/new error response
description: Discovered while implementing daa-2jci on 2026-10-07. Offline regression: LLM_API_KEY=skip-ci-no-key cargo test --test serve_errors. After successful initialize, session/new and prompt recovery, send session/new with cwd /tmp and a stdio MCP server named AUDIT_PROVIDER_PRIVATE_SENTINEL whose command is the same relative string. Actual: serve closed stdout during session/new (request 19), with no error reply. Expected: InvalidParams with a fixed MCP command diagnostic and the connection still usable. Root cause confirmed in src/acp/mod.rs, NewSessionRequest registration: the spawned task propagates handle_new_session_request_connected(...).await? instead of passing the result to responder.respond_with_result. Installed agent-client-protocol 1.3.0 src/jsonrpc.rs:2536 documents that any spawned-task error shuts down the entire server. Existing MCP validation tests call handlers directly and miss the production response wiring. Repair is a narrow part of the already claimed daa-2jci ACP presentation lane: respond with the setup result, emit command notifications only on success, then keep serving. Acceptance: real serve regression returns safe errors for relative MCP commands, malformed headers and malformed URLs, then accepts a valid request. No live provider endpoints or real secrets used. This is automated discovery rather than a maintainer live-report defect; close with the passing regression and repository gate evidence. No additional claim or unrelated implementation lane is being taken.
close_reason: Fixed and verified: session/new sends sanitized setup errors through responder.respond_with_result instead of letting expected errors escape the connection-fatal spawned task. Red-green real serve regression covers bad MCP command/header/URL inputs and subsequent valid session creation. All 511 tests and repository gates pass in the isolated Rust 1.95 checkout. Lesson recorded in the issue comment; implementation is part of daa-2jci, uncommitted.

comments.text: Fixed within daa-2jci’s ACP presentation lane. The NewSessionRequest spawned handler now keeps the setup Result, emits available-command notifications only for success, and sends responder.respond_with_result(result). Regression was red with serve closed stdout during session/new (request 19); the same test now returns InvalidParams for relative MCP commands, malformed headers and malformed URLs, then accepts another valid session. Durable lesson: cx.spawn task failures are connection-fatal in this SDK; expected request failures must be delivered through the responder, as load/resume/prompt already do. Isolated at 37388ac plus only README.md, src/error.rs, src/acp/mod.rs and tests/serve_errors.rs changes: Rust 1.95 full suite 511 passing tests, fmt, Clippy all targets/features with -D warnings, rustdoc with -D warnings, release build, cargo audit, AGENTS.md size and diff checks all pass. title: Filtered session/list scans every persisted workspace
description:
A workspace-filtered ACP session/list request is answered with every persisted session known to the adapter. louiselm's :LouiselmResume sends cwd=/home/lotso/code/louiselm, but the adapter returns sessions from unrelated workspaces; louiselm filters them only after receiving the response. This makes the normal resume command scan and serialize all workspaces, and the cost is multiplied when multiple ACP agents are configured. The unfiltered :LouiselmResume! behavior should remain cross-workspace.

## Observed

Reproduced 2026-08-22 on Linux with acp-llm-adapter checkout at HEAD 9f49bf5, target/debug/acp-llm-adapter 0.7.2, and the live default state directory.

Protocol request:
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":2,"method":"session/list","params":{"cwd":"/home/lotso/code/louiselm"}}

Protocol response summary:
session/list cwd=/home/lotso/code/louiselm returned 23 sessions

The 23 metadata files break down as:
- 11 /home/lotso/code/louiselm
- 7 /home/lotso/code/acp-llm-adapter
- 3 /home/lotso/code/pokeragents
- 2 /home/lotso/dotfiles

The live state has 29 session directories, 23 valid meta.json files, and 124M under sessions/ (mostly history files). The request was sent to target/debug/acp-llm-adapter serve --backend mock; the response included all 23 valid metadata entries, including unrelated cwd values.

## Symptoms

- :LouiselmResume takes longer as persisted sessions/workspaces accumulate, despite requesting one exact cwd.
- The picker ultimately shows only the current workspace because louiselm defensively filters the adapter response in louiselm.nvim/lua/louiselm/session/validation.lua:189-215.
- :LouiselmResume! intentionally requests all workspaces and should continue to do so.

## Root cause

src/session.rs:752-766 calls FilesystemSessionStore::list_persisted() and appends every returned persisted session without checking cwd_filter. src/session_store.rs:112-137 implements list_persisted() by enumerating every child directory under the state sessions directory and parsing every meta.json. The behavior was introduced by commit 9e95f2c ("feat: make session listing include all persisted sessions sorted by recency"), which conflated the all-workspaces resume use case with the cwd-filtered one.

## Why it was not caught

The existing regression test in src/acp/tests.rs:1601-1621 creates only a persisted session whose cwd matches the request, so it proves inclusion but not exclusion. src/acp/tests.rs:1625-1685 likewise uses one workspace for the filtered merge case. No test asserts that a requested cwd excludes persisted sessions from another workspace.

## Fix direction

Honor cwd_filter when building the persisted list for session/list. Keep the current all-workspaces behavior when cwd_filter is None. The narrowest fix is to filter persisted SessionInfo entries by cwd before appending, ideally at the persistence-listing boundary so unrelated metadata is not read or serialized for a filtered request. Preserve deduplication and recency sorting.

## Acceptance

- A regression test creates persisted sessions in at least two cwds, requests session/list with one cwd, and asserts only that cwd is returned.
- A session/list request with no cwd still returns sessions from all workspaces.
- louiselm Resume receives only sessions for the current workspace while Resume! receives all workspaces.
- Listing does not read session history files.

## Not covered

The direct probe intentionally used a one-second stdin hold-open to let asynchronous ACP responses flush, so it is evidence of result breadth rather than a latency benchmark. The exact user-visible delay may also include starting and initializing each configured ACP agent; this bead isolates the confirmed adapter-side over-broad persisted-session discovery.
close_reason: Fixed in commit 703b781. SessionStore now passes cwd_filter into FilesystemSessionStore::list_persisted, so filtered session/list returns only matching persisted workspaces while cwd=nil still returns all. Added acp::tests::list_sessions_filters_persisted_sessions_by_requested_cwd; it failed before the fix with 2 results and passes after. Verification: cargo test list_sessions_ passed (6 tests), cargo test --lib passed (118 tests), cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings passed, cargo fmt --all -- --check passed, and wire probes returned 11 filtered vs 23 unfiltered sessions. Full cargo test remains blocked by pre-existing tests::main_returns_successful_exit_code invoking clap with test-harness arguments; unrelated to this change.

title: Replace fake plans with explicit plan updates
description:
## Goal
Replace prompt-splitting placeholder plans with explicit model/tool-driven ACP plan updates.

## Scope
- In scope: design and implement an explicit planning mechanism, such as a model-visible `update_plan`/`todo_write` tool; emit `SessionUpdate::Plan` only from that mechanism; remove or gate automatic prompt punctuation splitting; persist or replay plan state if needed for coherent session load behavior.
- Out of scope: full task-management integration; Claude SDK Task/Todo compatibility; visual client UI work.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. Given a normal prompt with multiple sentences, when no explicit plan tool is used, then the adapter does not emit a fake plan derived from punctuation.
2. Given the model calls the explicit planning tool with valid entries, when the tool is executed, then the adapter emits an ACP `plan` update with those entries and appropriate statuses/priorities.
3. Given invalid plan tool input, when execution occurs, then the adapter returns a clear tool failure without corrupting plan state.
4. Given a prompt turn with plan updates and other tool calls, when notifications are emitted, then plan updates remain ordered and do not duplicate unrelated tool-call notifications.
5. Given session load/replay requirements chosen during implementation, when history is restored, then plan behavior is documented and tested.

## Testing
- Add tool registry/execution tests for valid and invalid plan tool inputs.
- Add prompt-turn tests proving fake prompt-split plans are not emitted and explicit plan updates are emitted.
- Add replay tests if plan state is persisted or reconstructed.
- Run the repo-required baseline/current test, fmt, and clippy checks before closing.

## Notes
- The current `plan_from_prompt` helper is useful as a placeholder but misleading as user-facing agent planning.
- Claude maps TodoWrite/Task tools to ACP plan updates; this adapter should use a DeepSeek-appropriate explicit tool rather than Claude-specific tool names unless there is a strong reason to match them.
close_reason: Implemented explicit plan updates

title: Local run_command ignores cancellation without ACP terminal support
description: Code evidence found while verifying daa-eyj2: src/tools/execution/mod.rs:619-630 runs the no-terminal branch in spawn_blocking with std::process::Command::output(). Unlike the terminal branch above, it never consumes cancellation_token and keeps no Child handle to stop the command. A cancelled turn can therefore leave this branch blocked until the command exits. Possible consequence, not yet reproduced: direct acp-llm-adapter serve shutdown can wait on that blocking job after client EOF. tests/serve_shutdown.rs:41 tests only idle EOF. Deferred independently from proxy cleanup; add a no-network command/cancellation regression and verify serve shutdown with a live local command. Real LouiseLM glm/deepseek configurations invoke serve directly; proxy-based configurations receive daa-eyj2 cleanup.
close_reason: gate:src/tools/execution/tests.rs — the no-terminal branch now spawns through tokio::process::Command with kill_on_drop and selects on the cancellation token, matching the terminal branch contract: kill the command, return ToolExecution::failed("run_command cancelled"). Red first and measured: run_command_without_terminal_support_honours_an_already_cancelled_turn and _stops_a_command_cancelled_mid_flight both failed with "run_command ignored the cancelled token and waited for the command" and the target took 30.01s, the full sleep 30; after the fix the same tests pass in 0.20s. Full suite 126/319/18/1/11 green, fmt, clippy --all-targets --all-features and cargo doc clean. Also removes the blocking-task hazard the issue described: there is no spawn_blocking job left for runtime shutdown to wait on. Two pieces of the acceptance are deliberately NOT met and are filed rather than glossed: daa-0yi0, cancellation kills the shell but not its backgrounded descendants, proven with a standalone reproduction where sh dies and the grandchild survives - fixing it needs process groups and a non-Linux decision, a different change from this one; and daa-wu5e, the serve-level verification with a live command could not be written at all because MockLlmClient never emits a tool call, so no test can drive a real serve process into run_command. What is proven here is that the function honours cancellation promptly; what is not proven is the end-to-end serve shutdown path the issue also asked about.
